# Unreal Engine 5.9 documentation index

Every page of the 5.9 documentation's table of contents (see Coverage notes at the end), crawled 2026-11-09 by `gen/docs/crawl.ts`, extracted to `docs/ue59/pages/<slug>.md` by `gen/docs/extract.ts`, and read by summariser agents (the console-variable table and long pasted node graphs checked by search) whose cards (`docs/ue59/cards/*.jsonl`) this index is built from (`gen/docs/build_index.ts`).

How to use: search this file for the topic or an exact name (a setting, console variable, class, function or plugin: each entry lists them after "keys:"), then open the page's text in `docs/ue59/pages/` (the full page, offline) or its URL. **[core]** = a small single-player jam game is likely to need it; [useful] = depth or a less common system; [skip] = not for this kind of project. **5.9:** = what the page itself says is new, changed or removed in 5.9 (grep "5.9:" for all of them). Gotchas are the page's own warnings and limits.

2544 pages: 504 core, 1156 useful, 884 skip; 8 say something is new or changed in 5.9. API reference is not crawled: [C++ API](https://dev.epicgames.com/documentation/en-us/unreal-engine/API?application_version=5.9) | [Blueprint API](https://dev.epicgames.com/documentation/en-us/unreal-engine/BlueprintAPI?application_version=5.9) | [Python API](https://dev.epicgames.com/documentation/en-us/unreal-engine/python-api/?application_version=5.9).

Gotchas: Root Motion from Everything is not recommended for multiplayer; Root Motion from Montages Only is the network-suitable option; Most graph changes require a recompile.

- **[core]** [Animation Montage](pages/animation-montage-in-unreal-engine.md) ([web](https://dev.epicgames.com/documentation/en-us/unreal-engine/animation-montage-in-unreal-engine?application_version=5.9)) - Reference for Animation Montages: creating them, the timeline (Sections, Montage/Slot tracks, Timing), Slots and Slot Groups, the Montage Sections panel for playback order, Child Montages for overriding segments, and root motion replication in network games. keys: `Animation Montage`, `Create AnimMontage`, `Create New Section`, `Montage Sections`, `Slot Group`, `Preview Slot`, `Slot Manager`, `Create Child Montage`, `_Child`, `PlayMontage`, `Preview All`. Gotchas: Don't overlap sequences in the same Slot; they interfere; Child montages are read-only except for segment overrides and cannot be parents of other child montages; Root motion replication requires calling PlayMontage via an RPC; Multiple slots should have matching total lengths.
- **[core]** [Animation Optimization](pages/animation-optimization-in-unreal-engine.md) ([web](https://dev.epicgames.com/documentation/en-us/unreal-engine/animation-optimization-in-unreal-engine?application_version=5.9)) - Best practices for AnimBP performance: moving EventGraph logic into Thread Safe functions called from Blueprint Thread Safe Update Animation, using Property Access, keeping AnimGraph on Fast Path with Warn About Blueprint Usage, and tips such as Update Rate Optimizations, Animation Budget Allocator and fixed skel bounds. keys: `Blueprint Thread Safe Update Animation`, `Thread Safe`, `Property Access`, `Animation Fast Path`, `Warn About Blueprint Usage`, `Enable Update Rate Optimizations`, `Display Debug Update Rate Optimizations`, `AnimUpdateRateTick()`, `Component Use Fixed Skel Bounds`, `UAnimInstance::NeedsImmediateUpdate`, `FParallelAnimationCompletionTask`. Gotchas: Any calculation in AnimGraph pins (e.g. a multiply) breaks Fast Path; Break Transform also doesn't use Fast Path; Root motion-driven character movement prevents parallel animation update; Notifies should be non-Blueprint and run on the game thread; Animation Budget Allocator recommended over URO.
- **[core]** [Animation Shortcuts and Tips](pages/animation-shortcuts-and-tips-unreal-engine.md) ([web](https://dev.epicgames.com/documentation/en-us/unreal-engine/animation-shortcuts-and-tips-unreal-engine?application_version=5.9)) - Workflow tips for animation work plus a reference of PIE console commands for animation debugging (ShowDebug ANIMATION, DisplayAll/GetAll, show bones, Slomo, FORCESKELLOD, obj list) and how to define Cheat Scripts in DefaultGame.ini. keys: `ShowDebug ANIMATION`, `DisplayAll`, `GetAll`, `Slomo`, `p.VisualizeMovement`, `a.VisualizeLODs`, `FORCESKELLOD LOD=0`, `t.MaxFPS 0`, `obj list class="AnimSequence"`, `Log LogAnimMontage Verbose`, `CheatScript`, `DefaultGame.ini`. Gotchas: Shift-click opens a second asset of the same type in a new tab instead of replacing; Framerate changes affect the editor and can hurt it on weak hardware.

Gotchas: Slots are stored on the Skeleton; saving slot changes saves the Skeleton; Montages only play through Slots present in the AnimGraph; A montage playing on slots in the same group stops the active one; multi-slot montages must stay within one Slot Group.

Gotchas: Dead Blending node is experimental; not recommended for shipping; Inertialization request without an Inertialization/Dead Blending node downstream logs a runtime error; Anim Notifies from the source anim stop firing once inertial blending begins; Anim Layers can only blend in/out via inertial blending.
- **[core]** [Blending Gameplay and Sequencer Animation](pages/blend-gameplay-animation-to-cinematic-animation-in-unreal-engine.md) ([web](https://dev.epicgames.com/documentation/en-us/unreal-engine/blend-gameplay-animation-to-cinematic-animation-in-unreal-engine?application_version=5.9)) - How to blend a player character and camera seamlessly between gameplay and a Level Sequence: use the gameplay Animation Blueprint with a Slot instead of Custom Mode, blend-out regions, Keep State, Camera Cut Can Blend, input suppression and Set Cinematic Mode, and setting control rotation on exit. keys: `Use Animation Blueprint`, `Anim Class`, `Anim Slot Manager`, `Slot 'DefaultSlot'`, `Slot Name`, `When Finished`, `Keep State`, `Can Blend`, `Constrain Aspect Ratio`, `Disable Movement Input`, `Set Cinematic Mode`, `Set Control Rotation`. Gotchas: Blending cannot use Custom Mode; the character must run its gameplay Animation Blueprint; Slots are stored on the Skeleton, so editing Slots edits the Skeleton; With IK foot placement, place the Slot before the IK node or the character snaps to terrain on blend out; Transform section keeps holding the character until its section ends; shorten it to release control early.

- [useful] [Curve Driven Animation](pages/curve-driven-animation-in-unreal-engine.md) ([web](https://dev.epicgames.com/documentation/en-us/unreal-engine/curve-driven-animation-in-unreal-engine?application_version=5.9)) - How-to building a walk cycle purely from curves: create a Pose Asset from ThirdPersonWalk, rename two poses, create an animation from reference pose, and key variable curves to blend between them. keys: `Create PoseAsset`, `Create Animation`, `From Reference Pose`, `Add Variable Curve..`, `Preview Pose Asset`, `Append at the End`. - [useful] [Facial Animation Sharing](pages/facial-animation-sharing-in-unreal-engine.md) ([web](https://dev.epicgames.com/documentation/en-us/unreal-engine/facial-animation-sharing-in-unreal-engine?application_version=5.9)) - Workflow for sharing curve-driven facial animation across meshes on one master Skeleton: import a pose FBX, create a Pose Asset with named poses, translate curves through a Pose Asset node, override per-character Pose Assets in child AnimBPs, and strip bone tracks. keys: `Pose Asset`, `Anim Curves`, `Delete Curve`, `Remove All Bone Tracks`, `Animation Modifier`, `Child Animation Blueprint`. - [useful] [Full-Body IK](pages/control-rig-full-body-ik-in-unreal-engine.md) ([web](https://dev.epicgames.com/documentation/en-us/unreal-engine/control-rig-full-body-ik-in-unreal-engine?application_version=5.9)) - How to build a Full Body IK node in Control Rig for procedural adjustments like ground alignment or reaching: root bone, effectors tied to controls, bone settings (stiffness, preferred angles, limits), excluded bones, and a full node pin reference. keys: `Full Body IK`, `FullBodyIK`, `Effectors`, `Bone Settings`, `Rotation Stiffness`, `Position Stiffness`, `Use Preferred Angles`, `Excluded Bones`, `Pull Chain Alpha`, `Mass Multiplier`, `Root Behavior`, `Start Solve from Input Pose`. Gotchas: Only one custom mark can exist per frame; H.264/5 media scrubs with a few frames of lag; Apple ProRes scrubs best; Synchronous Scrubbing affects only scrubbing, not playback; Asterisk on playhead time means a sub-frame position, which happens when snapping is disabled.

Gotchas: A rig without a Backwards Solve node is not selectable in Bake To Control Rig; Spawn nodes only work in the Construction Event; Spawned element count limit defaults to 128 (Procedural Element Limit); Spawned elements' initial values are read-only in Details and must be set on the node.

- **[core]** [Actor Communication](pages/actor-communication-in-unreal-engine.md) ([web](https://dev.epicgames.com/documentation/en-us/unreal-engine/actor-communication-in-unreal-engine?application_version=5.9)) - Overview comparing ways Actors share information in Blueprint/C++: direct references, casting, interfaces (UInterface) and delegates/Event Dispatchers, with when-to-use guidance, a reference table and links to each quick start guide. keys: `Direct Communication`, `Casting`, `UInterface`, `Delegates`, `Event Dispatchers`. Gotchas: Direct, casting and interface calls all need a reference to the target Actor; Event Dispatcher listeners must subscribe (bind) to react.
- **[core]** [Add a Sprint Mechanic to the Player](pages/designer-09-sprint-input-action-in-unreal-engine.md) ([web](https://dev.epicgames.com/documentation/en-us/unreal-engine/designer-09-sprint-input-action-in-unreal-engine?application_version=5.9)) - Puzzle Adventure tutorial step adding sprint with Enhanced Input: create an IA_Sprint Input Action with a Down trigger, map it in IMC_Default, and swap Character Movement Max Walk Speed on the Triggered/Completed pins. keys: `Input Action`, `Input Mapping Context`, `IA_Sprint`, `IMC_Default`, `Value Type`, `Digital (bool)`, `Axis1D`, `Axis2D`, `Triggers`, `Actuation Threshold`, `Max Walk Speed`, `Enhanced Action Events`. Gotchas: Shift, Ctrl, Alt mappings are used by the editor and may not work in PIE; test in standalone or use another key; Down trigger fires immediately; Hold fires only after a held duration; Default Max Walk Speed is 600 cm/s.
- **[core]** [Add Footstep Sounds to a Character](pages/artist-11-add-footstep-sounds-to-a-character.md) ([web](https://dev.epicgames.com/documentation/en-us/unreal-engine/artist-11-add-footstep-sounds-to-a-character?application_version=5.9)) - Tutorial (Artist track) for surface-dependent footstep audio: randomized Sound Cues per surface, Physical Materials, a PrimaryDataAsset mapping Physical Material to Sound Cue, a function-library function that line traces down and plays the sound, triggered from AnimNotify FootPlant events in the Animation Blueprint and Event On Landed. keys: `Sound Cue`, `Wave Player`, `Random`, `Physical Material`, `PrimaryDataAsset`, `Line Trace By Channel`, `Break Hit Results`, `Play Sound At Location`, `AnimNotify_AN_FootPlant_Left`, `AN_FootPlant_Right`, `Event On Landed`, `Phys Material Override`. Gotchas: Set Variable Type before choosing Map container; booleans cannot be mapped so Map is unavailable on the default type; Compile the Blueprint before editing variable default values; Every Animation Blueprint the character uses needs the notify logic added; Physical Material can be set per actor via Collision > Phys Material Override or on a Material Instance (General > Phys Material).
- **[core]** [Add Post Process Volumes](pages/add-post-process-volumes.md) ([web](https://dev.epicgames.com/documentation/en-us/unreal-engine/add-post-process-volumes?application_version=5.9)) - Tutorial on bound vs unbound Post Process Volumes with Priority and Blend Radius, then setting exposure (Min/Max EV100), bloom, lens flare, color grading offset/contrast, and per-volume Lumen GI/Reflections quality settings. keys: `PostProcessVolume`, `Infinite Extent (Unbound)`, `Priority`, `Blend Radius`, `Min EV100`, `Max EV100`, `Bloom`, `Lens Flares`, `Color Grading`, `Lumen Scene Lighting Quality`, `Lumen Scene Detail`, `Max Roughness To Trace`. Gotchas: Higher Priority wins; leave wide gaps (10/100) between priority values; Emissive materials only contribute light when GI method is Lumen; Bloom Threshold -1 lets all colors contribute.
- **[core]** [Add Sounds to Fire Traps](pages/artist-09-adding-sounds-to-fire-traps-artist-track-unreal-engine.md) ([web](https://dev.epicgames.com/documentation/en-us/unreal-engine/artist-09-adding-sounds-to-fire-traps-artist-track-unreal-engine?application_version=5.9)) - Tutorial creating a looping Sound Cue (Wave Player), a Sound Attenuation asset (inner radius/falloff), and adding an Audio component to a trap Blueprint that plays/stops with the trap state. keys: `Sound Cue`, `Wave Player`, `Looping`, `Sound Attenuation`, `Inner Radius`, `Falloff Distance`, `Audio component`, `Attenuation Settings`, `Allow Spatialization`, `Play (Audio)`, `Stop`.
- **[core]** [Add Visual Effects to Your Game](pages/at12-adding-visual-effects-to-your-game.md) ([web](https://dev.epicgames.com/documentation/en-us/unreal-engine/at12-adding-visual-effects-to-your-game?application_version=5.9)) - Tutorial (Artist track) on Niagara basics: create a system from the Hanging Particulates emitter, build a translucent unlit SubUV fire material, make a Minimal Lightweight (stateless) emitter fire, add it as a Niagara component to a trap Blueprint, toggle it with Activate/Deactivate and drive a User Parameter from the Construction Script. keys: `Niagara System`, `Hanging Particulates`, `Minimal Lightweight`, `ParticleSubUV`, `Particle Color`, `Depth Fade`, `Sub UV Animation`, `Sprite Renderer`, `User Parameters`, `Set Niagara Variable (Float)`, `Niagara Particle System Component`, `Hidden in Game`. Gotchas: Lightweight (stateless) emitters perform better but support only a limited set of modules; Set Niagara Variable In Variable Name must match the Niagara user parameter name exactly; Sub Image Size must match the SubUV texture grid (6x6 here); Add the Niagara component as a child of the base component so it scales with it.
- **[core]** [Blueprint Best Practices](pages/blueprint-best-practices-in-unreal-engine.md) ([web](https://dev.epicgames.com/documentation/en-us/unreal-engine/blueprint-best-practices-in-unreal-engine?application_version=5.9)) - Guidance on structuring Blueprints: avoid heavy per-tick math (use C++), Level Blueprints vs Blueprint Classes, class vs local variables, functions vs macros (latent nodes, overriding, multiple exec pins), communication types, and editor/graph organization tips. keys: `Level Blueprint`, `Blueprint Class`, `Local Variables`, `Functions`, `Macros`, `Find in Current Blueprint`, `Search`. Gotchas: Heavy operations and complex math every tick are better in native C++; Latent nodes (e.g. delays) can be used in macros but not in functions; Functions can be overridden in child Blueprints and targeted on other objects; macros cannot.
- **[core]** [Blueprint Communication Usage](pages/blueprint-communication-usage-in-unreal-engine.md) ([web](https://dev.epicgames.com/documentation/en-us/unreal-engine/blueprint-communication-usage-in-unreal-engine?application_version=5.9)) - When-to-use guide for Blueprint communication: direct references, Event Dispatchers (one-to-many notifications like a boss OnDied), Blueprint Interfaces (shared contract like OnTakeWeaponFire) and Cast nodes (accessing a specialized subclass), with gameplay examples. keys: `Direct Blueprint Communication`, `Event Dispatchers`, `Blueprint Interfaces`, `Cast`, `Get Player Character`, `Bind`. Gotchas: A Cast fails if the object is not of the target class, so its functions are inaccessible; Objects not implementing an interface simply ignore the call.
- **[core]** [Blueprint Debugger](pages/blueprint-debugger-in-unreal-engine.md) ([web](https://dev.epicgames.com/documentation/en-us/unreal-engine/blueprint-debugger-in-unreal-engine?application_version=5.9)) - Reference for the Blueprint Debugger window (Tools or Blueprint Editor Debug menu): breakpoints, watches and hover tooltips during PIE/SIE, the Data Flow tab with object filtering, Call Stack and Execution Trace. keys: `Blueprint Debugger`, `Add Breakpoint`, `Disable Breakpoint`, `Enable Breakpoint`, `Remove Breakpoint`, `Watch this value`, `Data Flow`, `Call Stack`, `Execution Trace`, `{,,UnrealEditor-Core}::PrintScriptCallstack()`. Gotchas: Breakpoints persist in the project's .ini files but are not shared with other developers; Yellow ! breakpoints are invalid and never reached; recompiling may fix; Pins have no debug value until their node executes once; Macros do not appear in the Call Stack; PrintScriptCallstack only in editor builds.
- **[core]** [Blueprint Debugging Example](pages/blueprint-debugging-example-in-unreal-engine.md) ([web](https://dev.epicgames.com/documentation/en-us/unreal-engine/blueprint-debugging-example-in-unreal-engine?application_version=5.9)) - How to debug Blueprints during PIE/SIE: choosing the Debug Object instance, adding/disabling/enabling Breakpoints, watching pin values, and using the Debug window's Watch Window, Call Stack and Execution Trace. keys: `Debug Object`, `Add Breakpoint`, `Disable Breakpoint`, `Enable Breakpoint`, `Remove Breakpoint`, `Watch this value`, `Stop watching this value`, `Watch Window`, `Call Stack`, `Execution Trace`, `{,,UnrealEditor-Core}::PrintScriptCallstack()`. Gotchas: Breakpoints are saved in project .ini files and persist between sessions; A yellow breakpoint with ! is invalid and never hit; recompiling may fix it; Pins show no value until their node has executed at least once; Macros do not appear in the Call Stack; PrintScriptCallstack works only in editor builds.
- **[core]** [Blueprint Editor Cheat Sheet](pages/blueprint-editor-cheat-sheet-in-unreal-engine.md) ([web](https://dev.epicgames.com/documentation/en-us/unreal-engine/blueprint-editor-cheat-sheet-in-unreal-engine?application_version=5.9)) - Keyboard and mouse shortcut tables for the Blueprint Editor: selection, graph navigation, generic commands (compile, find), variable drag actions, node actions (breakpoints, duplicate, comment), pin actions and key+click shortcuts for creating common nodes. keys: `F7`, `Ctrl + Shift + F`, `Ctrl + F`, `Ctrl + B`, `F9`, `Ctrl + Shift + F9`, `Ctrl + D`, `B + Left-Click`, `D + Left-Click`, `S + Left-Click`, `P + Left-Click`, `Home`. - **[core]** [Blueprint Foundations](pages/blueprint-foundations.md) ([web](https://dev.epicgames.com/documentation/en-us/unreal-engine/blueprint-foundations?application_version=5.9)) - Introductory overview of Blueprint asset types (Class, Level Blueprint, Interface, Function/Macro Library, Editor Utility) plus a tour of the template BP_JumpPad covering components, Construction Script, Event Graph, instance-editable variables, functions, and comments. keys: `Blueprint Class`, `Level Blueprint`, `Blueprint Interface`, `Blueprint Function Library`, `Blueprint Macro Library`, `Editor Utility`, `Construction Script`, `Event Graph`, `Event ActorBeginOverlap`, `BP_JumpPad`, `Instance Editable`, `Compile`. Gotchas: Data-only Blueprints open in a compact editor and convert to full editor when logic is added; Function library functions are static and keep no per-instance state; Macro changes only apply after recompiling the Blueprints that use them; Blueprint Interfaces cannot add variables, edit graphs, or add components.

## Creating User Interfaces

- **[core]** [Anchors](pages/umg-anchors-in-unreal-engine-ui.md) ([web](https://dev.epicgames.com/documentation/en-us/unreal-engine/umg-anchors-in-unreal-engine-ui?application_version=5.9)) - Explains how Anchors (Min/Max X,Y plus offsets) position and stretch widgets on a Canvas Panel across screen sizes and aspect ratios, using preset anchors, stretch presets, and manually split Anchor Medallions to tie widgets to each other. keys: `Canvas Panel`, `Anchors`, `Anchor Medallion`, `Minimum (X,Y)`, `Maximum (X,Y)`, `Horizontal Stretch`, `Vertical Stretch`, `Stretch Both`, `Screen Size`. Gotchas: Wrong anchor choice can push widgets out of the viewport at some screen sizes/aspect ratios; Offsets are in Slate Units relative to the Anchor Medallion.
- **[core]** [Animating UMG Widgets](pages/animating-umg-widgets-in-unreal-engine.md) ([web](https://dev.epicgames.com/documentation/en-us/unreal-engine/animating-umg-widgets-in-unreal-engine?application_version=5.9)) - How to create UMG widget animations in the Animations and Timeline panels (+Animation, Auto Key, Add Key, multi-key editing), play/stop them from the graph via the animation variable, with an animated main menu example using Set Timer. keys: `Animations`, `Timeline`, `+Animation`, `Auto Key`, `Add Key`, `Play Animation`, `Stop Animation`, `Set Timer`, `Event Construct`, `Add to Viewport`.
- **[core]** [Creating Widget Templates](pages/creating-umg-widget-templates-in-unreal-engine.md) ([web](https://dev.epicgames.com/documentation/en-us/unreal-engine/creating-umg-widget-templates-in-unreal-engine?application_version=5.9)) - How-to for building a reusable User Widget button (CustomButton) with an instance-editable style variable and an Event Dispatcher so each placed instance can respond differently, then adding it to a HUD widget created from the Level Blueprint. keys: `Widget Blueprint`, `User Widget`, `Size Box`, `Set Style`, `Event Construct`, `Instance Editable`, `Expose on Spawn`, `OnClicked`, `Event Dispatcher`, `Create Widget`, `Add to Viewport`, `Set Show Mouse Cursor`. Gotchas: Use the variable Set Style node, not the Button function node; Without an Event Dispatcher every button instance runs the same OnClicked logic.
- **[core]** [Creating Widgets](pages/creating-widgets-in-unreal-engine.md) ([web](https://dev.epicgames.com/documentation/en-us/unreal-engine/creating-widgets-in-unreal-engine?application_version=5.9)) - Shows how to display a Widget Blueprint at runtime with Create Widget and Add to Viewport, remove it with Remove from Parent, control input with the Set Input Mode nodes and Set Show Mouse Cursor, and nest widgets with Add Child/RemoveChild. keys: `Create Widget`, `Add to Viewport`, `Remove from Parent`, `Owning Player`, `Set Input Mode Game and UI`, `Set Input Mode Game Only`, `Set Input Mode UIOnly`, `Set Show Mouse Cursor`, `Get Player Controller`, `Add Child`, `RemoveChild`. Gotchas: Set Input Mode UIOnly disables all game controls; use sparingly; Store the Create Widget return value in a variable to reuse or remove it later instead of re-creating.
- **[core]** [Driving UI Updates with Events](pages/driving-ui-updates-with-events-in-unreal-engine.md) ([web](https://dev.epicgames.com/documentation/en-us/unreal-engine/driving-ui-updates-with-events-in-unreal-engine?application_version=5.9)) - Compares three ways to feed HUD health/energy: function binding (cast every frame), property binding (cache reference in Event Construct, poll value), and event-driven updates via an Event Dispatcher in the character bound to Custom Events in the widget. keys: `Create Binding`, `Event Construct`, `Event Dispatcher`, `Call Update Health`, `Bind Event`, `Custom Event`, `UpdateHealth`, `UpdateEnergy`, `Progress Bar`. Gotchas: Function bindings run every frame even when values don't change, which hurts performance in complex UIs.
- **[core]** [Optimization Guidelines](pages/optimization-guidelines-for-umg-in-unreal-engine.md) ([web](https://dev.epicgames.com/documentation/en-us/unreal-engine/optimization-guidelines-for-umg-in-unreal-engine?application_version=5.9)) - UMG/Slate performance guidelines: use invalidation and Volatile, avoid Tick/OnPaint and property bindings in favour of events, trim and async-load widgets, limit Canvas Panels/Overlays, prefer Spacers over Size Boxes, avoid Scale Box+Size Box combos, limit Rich Text, and the relative CPU cost of widget animation methods. keys: `Invalidation Box`, `Global Invalidation`, `Retainer Panels`, `Volatile`, `Canvas Panel`, `Overlay`, `Spacer`, `Size Box`, `Scale Box`, `Rich Text`, `OnHealthChanged`, `SWindow`. Gotchas: Never use raw attribute binding; it polls every frame; Canvas Panels increment Layer IDs and add draw calls; don't nest them in small custom widgets; Combining Scale Boxes and Size Boxes can loop, flipping size every frame; Sequencer UMG animations have a startup cost and render-transform animations invalidate layout each frame.

- **[core]** [Auto Exposure](pages/auto-exposure-in-unreal-engine.md) ([web](https://dev.epicgames.com/documentation/en-us/unreal-engine/auto-exposure-in-unreal-engine?application_version=5.9)) - Explains Post Process Volume exposure (eye adaptation): Histogram, Basic and Manual metering modes and formulas, Local Exposure, exposure compensation curve, metering mask, speed up/down, EV100 luminance range, pre-exposure, full settings tables, and the HDR (Eye Adaptation) debug visualization. keys: `Metering Mode`, `Auto Exposure Histogram`, `Auto Exposure Basic`, `Exposure Compensation`, `Apply Physical Camera Exposure`, `Exposure Compensation Curve`, `Exposure Metering Mask`, `Min Brightness`, `Extend default luminance range in Auto Exposure settings`, `Local Exposure`, `r.EyeAdaptation.ExponentialTransitionDistance`, `r.EyeAdaptation.VisualizeDebugType`. Gotchas: Setting Min Brightness equal to Max Brightness (or Min/Max EV100) disables auto exposure; Local Exposure should always be set up when using Lumen Global Illumination; r.EyeAdaptation.Focus was removed; use an Exposure Metering Mask; Apply Physical Camera Exposure only affects Manual mode and makes most scenes much darker.
- **[core]** [Bloom](pages/bloom-in-unreal-engine.md) ([web](https://dev.epicgames.com/documentation/en-us/unreal-engine/bloom-in-unreal-engine?application_version=5.9)) - Describes the Post Process Volume bloom settings (Intensity, Threshold, per-blur Tint/Size), FFT-based Bloom Convolution with custom kernel textures, and the Bloom Dirt Mask, including texture setup best practices. keys: `Intensity`, `Threshold`, `Method`, `Convolution`, `Convolution Kernel`, `Convolution Scale`, `Convolution Center`, `Convolution Boost`, `Convolution Buffer`, `Dirt Mask Texture`, `Dirt Mask Intensity`, `Dirt Mask Tint Color`. Gotchas: Standard bloom is recommended for most games; Convolution is for cinematics or high-end hardware; Kernel and dirt mask textures need No Mipmaps and Never Stream enabled; Dirt Mask Texture cannot be blended between Post Process Volumes; Increasing Convolution Buffer hurts performance.
- **[core]** [Color Grading and the Filmic Tonemapper](pages/color-grading-and-the-filmic-tonemapper-in-unreal-engine.md) ([web](https://dev.epicgames.com/documentation/en-us/unreal-engine/color-grading-and-the-filmic-tonemapper-in-unreal-engine?application_version=5.9)) - Explains the ACES filmic tonemapper's Film settings (Slope, Toe, Shoulder, Black/White Clip) and the Post Process Volume Color Grading controls (Temperature, Global/Shadows/Midtones/Highlights, Misc, LUT), with a recommended color correction workflow. keys: `Slope`, `Toe`, `Shoulder`, `Black Clip`, `White Clip`, `Temperature Type`, `White Balance`, `Shadows Max`, `HighLights Min`, `Blue Correction`, `Expand Gamut`, `Color Grading LUT`. Gotchas: Film settings should be set project-wide, not changed per shot or dynamically; Do not use Gain to adjust exposure; use Exposure Bias/compensation; LUTs apply after tonemapping in LDR and won't match across HDR displays; prefer color grading controls.
- **[core]** [Command-Line Arguments Reference](pages/unreal-engine-command-line-arguments-reference.md) ([web](https://dev.epicgames.com/documentation/en-us/unreal-engine/unreal-engine-command-line-arguments-reference?application_version=5.9)) - Large table of command-line flags and -Key=Value arguments for the editor and game executables, covering RHI selection, logging, windowing/resolution, debugging (GPU crash, RDG, Vulkan validation), cooking/pak utilities, profiling and device profile overrides. keys: `-game`, `-Windowed`, `-ResX`, `-ResY`, `-log`, `-ExecCmds`, `-dx12`, `-nullrhi`, `-gpucrashdebugging`, `-unattended`, `-DPCVars`, `-statunit`. Gotchas: Command-line config overrides do not work with arrays; Config section ClassName omits the U or A prefix; Not all config settings are exposed in Project Settings; r. cvars belong in [/Script/Engine.RendererSettings]; s. in StreamingSettings; gc. in GarbageCollectionSettings.
- **[core]** [Creating and Using Custom Heightmaps and Target Layers](pages/creating-and-using-custom-heightmaps-and-layers-in-unreal-engine.md) ([web](https://dev.epicgames.com/documentation/en-us/unreal-engine/creating-and-using-custom-heightmaps-and-layers-in-unreal-engine?application_version=5.9)) - How to import externally made heightmaps and target layer weightmaps (PNG/RAW) into a Landscape, set up a basic LandscapeLayerBlend material with Layer Info objects, and match required layer resolutions. keys: `LandscapeLayerCoords`, `LandscapeLayerBlend`, `Layer Info`, `Import from file`, `Overall Resolution`, `ILandscapeHeightmapFileFormat`, `ILandscapeWeightmapFileFormat`. Gotchas: Heightmaps should be 16-bit single-channel grayscale; target layers 8-bit grayscale; RGB loses color and precision; Layer image must match the landscape resolution exactly or it will not import; Applying a layer-blend material turns the landscape black until Layer Info objects are assigned.
- **[core]** [Custom Events](pages/custom-events-in-unreal-engine.md) ([web](https://dev.epicgames.com/documentation/en-us/unreal-engine/custom-events-in-unreal-engine?application_version=5.9)) - How to create Blueprint Custom Events with input parameters and optional replication, call them from anywhere in the Blueprint via Call Function, and fix stale call nodes after changing parameters. keys: `Add Custom Event...`, `Call Function`, `Refresh Nodes`, `Refresh All Nodes`, `CE`, `KE`, `Print String`. - **[core]** [Dealing with a GPU Crash](pages/dealing-with-a-gpu-crash-when-using-unreal-engine.md) ([web](https://dev.epicgames.com/documentation/en-us/unreal-engine/dealing-with-a-gpu-crash-when-using-unreal-engine?application_version=5.9)) - How to recognize and debug GPU crashes (TDR timeouts and page faults) on D3D12/D3D11: reading DXGI_ERROR_DEVICE_REMOVED logs, RHI breadcrumbs, DRED and NVIDIA Aftermath output, the flags and cvars that enable them, handling VRAM exhaustion, ray-tracing tiling, and raising TdrDelay in the Windows registry. keys: `DXGI_ERROR_DEVICE_REMOVED`, `-gpucrashdebugging`, `-gpubreadcrumbs`, `-dred`, `-lightdred`, `-nvaftermath`, `r.GPUCrashDebugging`, `r.D3D12.DRED`, `D3D12.TrackAllAllocations`, `r.RayTracing.GlobalIllumination.RenderTileSize`, `TdrDelay`, `TdrDdiDelay`. Gotchas: CPU callstack of a GPU crash is irrelevant; errors are reported asynchronously; Full DRED has a significant performance cost; breadcrumbs and lightweight DRED only default on in Debug/Development; Aftermath dumps only on NVIDIA GPUs; Raising TdrDelay via registry edit is risky and won't fix all crashes; DXGI_ERROR_DEVICE_RESET usually means another app crashed.
- **[core]** [Decal Materials](pages/decal-materials-in-unreal-engine.md) ([web](https://dev.epicgames.com/documentation/en-us/unreal-engine/decal-materials-in-unreal-engine?application_version=5.9)) - Explains how to make Deferred Decal materials and project them with Decal Actors or mesh decals, the DBuffer vs GBuffer decal paths, the receiving material's Decal Response setting, Sort Order, and DBuffer material expressions for custom blending. keys: `Deferred Decal`, `Decal Actor`, `Decal Response`, `Receives Decals`, `Sort Order`, `Fade Screen Size`, `Decal Color`, `DBuffer Texture`, `ApplyDBuffer`, `r.Decal.NormalProjectionEnabled`, `Feature Level Switch`, `stat gpu`. Gotchas: Modulate blend mode silently falls back to Translucent with DBuffer decals; only Translucent and Alpha Composite are supported; Substrate and DBuffer material expressions require DBuffer Decals enabled; mobile does not support DBuffer decals; Materials using DBuffer expressions/ApplyDBuffer should set Decal Response to None to avoid double application; DBuffer decals need depth prepass; mesh decals are expensive with the Path Tracer.

- **[core]** [Landscape Materials](pages/landscape-materials-in-unreal-engine.md) ([web](https://dev.epicgames.com/documentation/en-us/unreal-engine/landscape-materials-in-unreal-engine?application_version=5.9)) - Reference for building landscape materials: weight vs alpha blending of painted layers and the Landscape Layer Blend, Sample, Coords, Switch, Weight and Visibility Mask nodes, height-blend black-spot fix, mobile sampler limits and assigning the material. keys: `Landscape Layer Blend`, `LandscapeLayerBlend`, `LB Weight Blend`, `LB Alpha Blend`, `LB Height Blend`, `Landscape Layer Sample`, `Landscape Layer Coords`, `Landscape Layer Switch`, `LandscapeLayerWeight`, `Landscape Visibility Mask`, `Landscape Layer Info`, `Landscape Material`. - **[core]** [Landscape Paint Mode](pages/landscape-paint-mode-in-unreal-engine.md) ([web](https://dev.epicgames.com/documentation/en-us/unreal-engine/landscape-paint-mode-in-unreal-engine?application_version=5.9)) - Guide to Landscape Paint mode: target layers, weight-blended vs non-weight-blended Layer Info objects, auto-creating layers from the material, weight blending methods, and the Paint, Smooth, Flatten and Noise tools with painting performance tips. keys: `Target Layers`, `Layer Info Object`, `Weight-Blended Layer (normal)`, `Non Weight-Blended Layer`, `Create Layers From Materials`, `Auto-Fill Target Layer Assets`, `Default Layer Assets Path`, `Advanced Weight Blending`, `Final Weight Blending (Legacy)`, `Weight Blend Group`, `Display Target Layer Thumbnails`, `Phys Material`. - **[core]** [Landscape Splines](pages/landscape-splines-in-unreal-engine.md) ([web](https://dev.epicgames.com/documentation/en-us/unreal-engine/landscape-splines-in-unreal-engine?application_version=5.9)) - How to create and edit Landscape Splines in Landscape Mode (Manage > Spline) for roads, paths and fences: placing/joining/splitting control points, assigning spline meshes, applying them to the heightmap via a Spline edit layer, selection tools, and all control point and segment properties. keys: `Landscape Splines`, `Spline`, `Spline Edit Layer`, `Use Auto Rotate Control Point`, `Auto-Rotate Always Forward`, `Landscape Spline Meshes`, `Spline Meshes`, `Half-Width`, `Side Falloff`, `Layer Name`, `Raise Terrain`, `Lower Terrain`. Gotchas: Splines do not change the heightmap until a Spline edit layer is added to the edit layer stack; Select All affects every spline actor in the level; use Select Spline Points/Segments for one graph; Scale gizmo on splines edits tangents instead of scaling.
- **[core]** [Light Types and Their Mobility](pages/light-types-and-their-mobility-in-unreal-engine.md) ([web](https://dev.epicgames.com/documentation/en-us/unreal-engine/light-types-and-their-mobility-in-unreal-engine?application_version=5.9)) - Describes the five light types (Directional, Sky, Point, Spot, Rect) and what Static, Stationary and Movable mobility mean for baking, dynamic shadows and cost, with links to per-type and per-mobility pages. keys: `Directional Light`, `Sky Light`, `Point Light`, `Spot Light`, `Rect Light`, `Static`, `Stationary`, `Movable`. Gotchas: A single object can be affected by at most four Stationary Lights; Shadow-casting Movable lights are the most expensive; unshadowed Movable lights are cheap.
- **[core]** [Local Fog Volumes](pages/local-fog-volumes-in-unreal-engine.md) ([web](https://dev.epicgames.com/documentation/en-us/unreal-engine/local-fog-volumes-in-unreal-engine?application_version=5.9)) - Explains Local Fog Volume actors: placeable spheres of radially faded height fog layered on top of Exponential Height Fog/Sky Atmosphere, their density/falloff/albedo/emissive/sort-priority properties, use with Volumetric Fog, and tile-based culling debug cvars. keys: `Local Fog Volume`, `Radial Fog Density`, `Height Fog Falloff`, `Fog Sort Priority`, `Local Fog Volume Apply on Translucent`, `Support Local Fog Volumes`, `r.SupportLocalFogVolumes`, `r.LocalFogVolume.TileDebug`, `r.LocalFogVolume.ApplyOnTranslucent`, `r.LocalFogVolume.RenderIntoVolumetricFog`, `r.LocalFogVolume.GlobalStartDistance`, `r.LocalFogVolume.TileMaxInstanceCount`. Gotchas: Non-uniform scaling is not supported; No volumetric shadowing/lighting unless Volumetric Fog is enabled on Exponential Height Fog; shadows and light functions are ignored otherwise; Fog Sort Priority and the TileDebug views do not work when Volumetric Fog is enabled; Not applied to translucent meshes unless r.LocalFogVolume.ApplyOnTranslucent is 1 (default 0).
- **[core]** [Lumen Global Illumination and Reflections](pages/lumen-global-illumination-and-reflections-in-unreal-engine.md) ([web](https://dev.epicgames.com/documentation/en-us/unreal-engine/lumen-global-illumination-and-reflections-in-unreal-engine?application_version=5.9)) - Overview of Lumen dynamic GI and reflections: enabling it in Project Settings, what it supports (sky light, emissive, translucency, water, two-sided foliage), all Project and Post Process Volume Lumen settings, update speed, disabling static lighting and Material AO. keys: `Dynamic Global Illumination Method`, `Reflection Method`, `Generate Mesh Distance Fields`, `Use Hardware Ray Tracing when available`, `Ray Lighting Mode`, `Hit Lighting for Reflections`, `Software Ray Tracing Mode`, `Lumen Scene Lighting Quality`, `Final Gather Quality`, `Max Trace Distance`, `Allow Static Lighting`, `r.Lumen.Reflections.MaxBounces`. Gotchas: Projects converted from UE4 do not enable Lumen automatically; Static mobility lights are not supported; lightmaps are hidden when Lumen is on; Global lighting changes can take seconds to propagate; raise update speed settings at extra GPU cost; Max Reflection Bounces needs Hardware Ray Tracing with Hit Lighting for Reflections.
- **[core]** [Lumen Performance Guide](pages/lumen-performance-guide-for-unreal-engine.md) ([web](https://dev.epicgames.com/documentation/en-us/unreal-engine/lumen-performance-guide-for-unreal-engine?application_version=5.9)) - Scalability and tuning guide for Lumen GI and reflections: quality levels via sg.GlobalIlluminationQuality/sg.ReflectionQuality, Lumen Lite (Irradiance Final Gather), Software vs Hardware Ray Tracing costs, reflection roughness/downsample cvars, radiance cache and screen probe gather controls, and profiling. keys: `sg.GlobalIlluminationQuality`, `sg.ReflectionQuality`, `r.Lumen.FinalGatherMethod`, `r.Lumen.Reflections.Allow`, `r.Lumen.Reflections.MaxRoughnessToTraceForFoliage`, `r.Lumen.Reflections.DownsampleFactor`, `Max Roughness To Trace`, `r.Lumen.ScreenProbeGather.DownsampleFactor`, `r.Lumen.AsyncCompute`, `r.GlobalDistanceField.Debug.LogModifiedPrimitives`, `Affects Distance Field Lighting`, `BaseScalability.ini`. Gotchas: Low scalability disables Lumen entirely; Moving Static-mobility actors invalidates the Global Distance Field static cache (expensive); Hit Lighting for Reflections is too expensive for games unless materials are trivial; Disable Async Compute (r.Lumen.AsyncCompute 0) when profiling Lumen alone.
- **[core]** [Lumen Technical Details](pages/lumen-technical-details-in-unreal-engine.md) ([web](https://dev.epicgames.com/documentation/en-us/unreal-engine/lumen-technical-details-in-unreal-engine?application_version=5.9)) - Technical detail on Lumen's Surface Cache and cards, screen tracing, Software (distance field) vs Hardware Ray Tracing with their limits and requirements, Far Field, platform support, visualization view modes and troubleshooting common artifacts like leaking, black reflections and slow propagation. keys: `r.Lumen.Visualize.CardPlacement`, `Max Lumen Mesh Cards`, `r.MeshCardRepresentation.SkeletalMesh`, `Ray Tracing Quality Switch`, `Detail Tracing`, `Global Tracing`, `r.DistanceFields.LogAtlasStats`, `Distance Field Resolution Scale`, `r.DistanceFields.SupportEvenIfHardwareRayTracingSupported`, `r.LumenScene.FarField`, `Affect Distance Field Lighting`, `Emissive Light Source`. Gotchas: Software RT does not support World Position Offset; walls should be at least 10 cm thick; large single meshes give poor distance fields; Hardware RT needs Windows 10+ DX12 and NVIDIA RTX 2000+ or AMD RX 6000+; skinned meshes add per-frame BVH update cost; Lumen is not compatible with Forward Shading; Lumen Scene covers 200 m by default (up to 800 m); Foliage and Instanced Static Meshes need Nanite for Surface Cache support.
- **[core]** [Material Data Manipulation and Arithmetic](pages/material-data-manipulation-and-arithmetic-in-unreal-engine.md) ([web](https://dev.epicgames.com/documentation/en-us/unreal-engine/material-data-manipulation-and-arithmetic-in-unreal-engine?application_version=5.9)) - Explains combining and splitting channels in the Material Editor (AppendVector, AppendMany, ComponentMask) and the rules for arithmetic between float, float2, float3 and float4 values, including which combinations error out. keys: `AppendVector`, `AppendMany`, `ComponentMask`, `Constant2Vector`, `Constant3Vector`, `Constant4Vector`, `Add`. Gotchas: Arithmetic between unequal vector sizes (e.g. float2 + float3) is invalid and errors; only a scalar float mixes with any size; AppendMany only accepts scalars; extra channels of vector inputs are discarded; A ComponentMask with no channels checked outputs nothing and errors downstream; Input order matters for Subtract and Divide.

- **[core]** [Material Parameter Collections](pages/using-material-parameter-collections-in-unreal-engine.md) ([web](https://dev.epicgames.com/documentation/en-us/unreal-engine/using-material-parameter-collections-in-unreal-engine?application_version=5.9)) - How to create a MaterialParameterCollection asset of global scalar/vector parameters, read it in materials with a CollectionParameter node, and change values at runtime from Blueprint with Set Scalar Parameter Value, plus its limits. keys: `MaterialParameterCollection`, `CollectionParameter`, `Set Scalar Parameter Value`, `Parameter Name`, `Collection`, `MPC_GlobalParams`, `Open Level Blueprint`. - **[core]** [Material Parameter Expressions](pages/material-parameter-expressions-in-unreal-engine.md) ([web](https://dev.epicgames.com/documentation/en-us/unreal-engine/material-parameter-expressions-in-unreal-engine?application_version=5.9)) - Reference for material parameter nodes exposed to Material Instances and runtime code: Collection Parameter, DynamicParameter for Niagara, ScalarParameter, VectorParameter, static switch/bool/component-mask parameters, and texture sample/object parameter variants. keys: `CollectionParameter`, `Material Parameter Collection`, `DynamicParameter`, `ScalarParameter`, `VectorParameter`, `StaticSwitchParameter`, `StaticBoolParameter`, `StaticComponentMaskParameter`, `TextureObjectParameter`, `TextureSampleParameter2D`, `TextureSampleParameterCube`, `FontSampleParameter`. Gotchas: A material can reference at most two Material Parameter Collections; each holds up to 1024 scalar and 1024 vector parameters; Static parameters cannot change at runtime and each used combination compiles a new shader permutation; VertexColor and Transform node are mutually exclusive; VertexColor comes out white; Sampling alpha of a texture without alpha returns zero.
- **[core]** [Material Properties](pages/unreal-engine-material-properties.md) ([web](https://dev.epicgames.com/documentation/en-us/unreal-engine/unreal-engine-material-properties?application_version=5.9)) - Reference for all Material Details properties: Material Domain, Blend Mode, Shading Model, Two Sided, advanced options, Nanite override, translucency lighting modes, usage flags, post-process, refraction, Max World Position Offset Displacement and Lightmass. keys: `Material Domain`, `Blend Mode`, `Shading Model`, `Opacity Mask Clip Value`, `Nanite Override Material`, `Lighting Mode`, `Used with Skeletal Mesh`, `Used with Niagara Sprites`, `Blendable Location`, `Refraction Method`, `Max World Position Offset Displacement`, `Out of Bounds Pixels`. Gotchas: Missing usage flag makes the default world grid material render in-game; Translucent/Additive/Modulate blend modes are not compatible with dynamic lighting; Two Sided does not work correctly with static lighting; Max WPO Displacement of 0 means no clamp and no bounds extension; clamping can flatten offsets.
- **[core]** [Materials](pages/unreal-engine-materials.md) ([web](https://dev.epicgames.com/documentation/en-us/unreal-engine/unreal-engine-materials?application_version=5.9)) - Hub page for Materials: links to essential concepts, physically based materials, Material Editor guide, properties, inputs, data types, Substrate, instances, functions, layered materials, tutorials, expression/function references and advanced topics like Custom Primitive Data and lit translucency. keys: `Material Instances`, `Material Functions`, `Material Expressions Reference`, `Material Editor`, `Substrate`.
- **[core]** [Motion Warping](pages/motion-warping-in-unreal-engine.md) ([web](https://dev.epicgames.com/documentation/en-us/unreal-engine/motion-warping-in-unreal-engine?application_version=5.9)) - Shows how to warp a character's root motion to line up with a target point: add Motion Warping notify-state windows in an Animation Montage, add the Motion Warping component, set warp targets in Blueprint, and play the montage (worked punch-to-target example). keys: `Motion Warping`, `Motion Warping Component`, `Add Notify State... > Motion Warping`, `Root Motion Modifier`, `Skew Warp`, `Warp Target Name`, `Warp Point Anim Provider`, `Add or Update Warp Target from Transform`, `Remove Warp Target`, `Add Root Motion Modifier Skew Warp`, `EnableRootMotion`, `Play Montage`. - **[core]** [Movable Light Mobility](pages/movable-light-mobility-in-unreal-engine.md) ([web](https://dev.epicgames.com/documentation/en-us/unreal-engine/movable-light-mobility-in-unreal-engine?application_version=5.9)) - Explains Movable (fully dynamic) lights: supported shadow methods (shadow maps, VSM, ray traced, distance field), shadow bias properties to fix acne or peter-panning, and shadow map caching for point/spot lights with its limits. keys: `Movable`, `Shadow Bias`, `Shadow Slope Bias`, `Shadow Cascade Bias Distribution`, `Shadow Filter Sharpen`, `r.Shadow.WholeSceneShadowCacheMb`, `r.Shadow.WholeSceneShadows`, `Stat ShadowRendering`. - **[core]** [Nanite Virtualized Geometry Overview](pages/nanite-virtualized-geometry-in-unreal-engine.md) ([web](https://dev.epicgames.com/documentation/en-us/unreal-engine/nanite-virtualized-geometry-in-unreal-engine?application_version=5.9)) - Overview of Nanite: how it works, which meshes should use it, how to enable it on import, per-asset or in batch, its feature set (skeletal meshes, landscapes, foliage, splines, displacement, tessellation) and what geometry, material and rendering features are unsupported. keys: `Build Nanite`, `Enable Nanite Support`, `Nanite > Enable`, `Fallback Relative Error`, `r.RayTracing.Nanite.Mode`, `Nanite Settings`, `Generate Lightmap UVs`, `World Position Offset`, `Project Settings > Engine > Rendering`. Gotchas: Only Opaque and Masked blend modes; unsupported materials get a default material with an Output Log warning; No Morph Targets, Forward Rendering, MSAA, Lighting Channels, VR stereo, distance/min-screen-radius culling; Requires DirectX 12 with SM6; hard limit of 16 million instances in scene; WPO displacement must be clamped; Custom nodes/POM may artifact; ray tracing uses Fallback Mesh unless r.RayTracing.Nanite.Mode 1 (experimental).
- **[core]** [Physical Lighting Units](pages/using-physical-lighting-units-in-unreal-engine.md) ([web](https://dev.epicgames.com/documentation/en-us/unreal-engine/using-physical-lighting-units-in-unreal-engine?application_version=5.9)) - Explains the physical units used for light intensity (lux for Directional, cd/m2 for Sky Light and emissive, candela/lumen/unitless for Point/Spot/Rect), conversion factors between them, and exposure tips for a physically based workflow. keys: `Intensity Units`, `Inverse Squared Falloff`, `Candela`, `Lumen`, `Unitless`, `Auto Exposure Max EV100`, `Histogram Max EV100`, `Apply Pre-Exposure before writing to the scene color`, `Visualize HDR`, `Project Settings > Rendering > Default Settings`, `Use Emissive for Static Lighting`. Gotchas: Only Unitless is available when Inverse Squared Falloff is disabled; Image going white after placing a light usually means the auto exposure range is too limited; Switching to the extended default luminance range breaks existing exposure setups; Keep instanced/child lights on the same unit as their parent to avoid default-value propagation issues.
- **[core]** [Physically Based Materials](pages/physically-based-materials-in-unreal-engine.md) ([web](https://dev.epicgames.com/documentation/en-us/unreal-engine/physically-based-materials-in-unreal-engine?application_version=5.9)) - Guidelines for the PBR material inputs Base Color, Roughness, Metallic and Specular, with measured real-world values, how to map roughness/metallic, and using cavity maps. keys: `Base Color`, `Roughness`, `Metallic`, `Specular`. Gotchas: Treat Metallic as binary (0 or 1) except for hybrid surfaces; Leave Specular at default 0.5; do not set to 0 for diffuse materials, raise Roughness instead; Specular input is not for reflection/variation maps; use Roughness maps.
- **[core]** [Post Process Effects](pages/post-process-effects-in-unreal-engine.md) ([web](https://dev.epicgames.com/documentation/en-us/unreal-engine/post-process-effects-in-unreal-engine?application_version=5.9)) - Reference for Post Process Volume settings (Priority, Blend Radius, Infinite Extent) and each category: lens effects (DOF, bloom, exposure, chromatic aberration, flares, vignette), color grading/film tonemapper, GI and reflection method selection, post process materials, SSAO/RTAO, motion blur, path tracing and film grain. keys: `Post Process Volume`, `Infinite Extent (Unbound)`, `Priority`, `Blend Radius`, `Blend Weight`, `Local Exposure`, `Final Gather Quality`, `Post Process Materials`, `Ambient Cubemap`, `Motion Blur`, `Film Grain Intensity`, `Rendering > Default Settings`. Gotchas: Ray Tracing GI, Ray Tracing Reflections and Ray Tracing Translucency are deprecated and may be removed; Ray tracing options require Support Hardware Ray Tracing and DirectX 12; Default post settings apply even without a volume; configured in Project Settings > Rendering > Default Settings; Overlapping volumes with equal Priority have undefined order.
- **[core]** [Post Process Materials](pages/post-process-materials-in-unreal-engine.md) ([web](https://dev.epicgames.com/documentation/en-us/unreal-engine/post-process-materials-in-unreal-engine?application_version=5.9)) - How to author Post Process domain materials and add them as Blendables: Blendable Location/Priority, blending material instances across volumes, SceneTexture (PostProcessInput0, GBuffer), CustomDepth and stencil for outlines/occlusion effects, TAA jitter, UVs, replacing the tonemapper, and known issues/FAQ. keys: `Post Process`, `Blendables`, `Blendable Location`, `Blendable Priority`, `Is Blendable`, `SceneTexture`, `PostProcessInput0`, `Render Custom Depth`, `Custom Depth Stencil Value`, `ScreenPosition`, `r.CompositionGraphDebug`, `Engine.FilmWhitePoint`. Gotchas: Output only via Emissive Color; outputting alpha is not supported (use Opacity); Use PostProcessInput0, not SceneColor, to avoid banding; After-tonemapping effects using depth/GBuffer jitter with TAA; World Position needs to run before temporal upscaling; Set default material parameters to a no-effect value or volume blend transitions are hard; Replacing the Tonemapper is work in progress.
- **[core]** [Scalability Reference](pages/scalability-reference-for-unreal-engine.md) ([web](https://dev.epicgames.com/documentation/en-us/unreal-engine/scalability-reference-for-unreal-engine?application_version=5.9)) - Reference for the engine scalability groups and their cvars (resolution scale, view distance, anti-aliasing, post process, shadows, textures, effects, foliage), Detail Mode, Material Quality Level with the Quality Switch node, skeletal mesh LOD bias, and customizing groups via DefaultScalability.ini. keys: `r.ScreenPercentage`, `r.ViewDistanceScale`, `r.PostProcessAAQuality`, `sg.PostProcessQuality`, `sg.ShadowQuality`, `sg.TextureQuality`, `sg.EffectsQuality`, `r.DetailMode`, `r.SkeletalMeshLODBias`, `foliage.DensityScale`, `BaseScalability.ini`, `DefaultScalability.ini`. Gotchas: Foliage meshes only respond to scalability if Enable Density Scaling is set; Quality Switch nodes add shader permutations and cannot be used for distance LOD; Detail Mode should only be used on objects with no gameplay effect.
- **[core]** [Shadowing](pages/shadowing-in-unreal-engine.md) ([web](https://dev.epicgames.com/documentation/en-us/unreal-engine/shadowing-in-unreal-engine?application_version=5.9)) - Overview of shadowing methods (shadow maps, Virtual Shadow Maps, ray-traced, distance field, Lightmass baked) chosen by light Mobility, plus per-light shadow properties (source radius/angle, attenuation radius, contact shadows, bias, cascaded shadow maps, far shadows) and performance tips for dynamic lights. keys: `Mobility`, `Source Radius`, `Source Angle`, `Source Length`, `Attenuation Radius`, `Cast Shadow`, `Cast Volumetric Fog`, `Volumetric Scattering Intensity`, `Contact Shadows Length`, `Far Shadow`, `Max Draw Distance`, `Build > Build All Levels`. Gotchas: Default shadow mapping does not support Nanite geometry and needs manual shadow distance setup; Static/Stationary lights show 'Preview' shadows until lighting is built; Lumen cannot be combined with baked global illumination; Contact shadows are screen-space and limited to what the camera sees.
- **[core]** [Sky Atmosphere Component Properties](pages/sky-atmosphere-component-properties-in-unreal-engine.md) ([web](https://dev.epicgames.com/documentation/en-us/unreal-engine/sky-atmosphere-component-properties-in-unreal-engine?application_version=5.9)) - Reference for the Sky Atmosphere component: project settings, planet/Rayleigh/Mie/absorption/art-direction properties, the SkyAtmosphere* material expressions for custom skydome materials, and the full list of r.SkyAtmosphere console variables. keys: `Support Sky Atmosphere`, `Support Sky Atmosphere Affecting Height Fog`, `Transform Mode`, `Aerial Perspective Start Depth`, `SkyAtmosphereViewLuminance`, `SkyAtmosphereLightDirection`, `SkyAtmosphereLightIlluminance`, `SkyAtmosphereLightDiskLuminance`, `Atmosphere Sun Light Index`, `TimeOfDay_default`, `r.SkyAtmosphere.FastSkyLUT`, `r.SupportSkyAtmosphereAffectsHeightFog`. Gotchas: Planet Top at Absolute World Origin mode makes the atmosphere non-movable; Ground Albedo only matters when MultiScattering is greater than 0; Light Index on SkyAtmosphere light expressions must match the Directional Light's Atmosphere Sun Light Index; FastSkyLUT and AerialPerspectiveLUT.FastApplyOnOpaque are faster but can show artifacts with high-frequency sky detail.
- **[core]** [Storing Custom Data in Materials Per-Primitive](pages/storing-custom-data-in-unreal-engine-materials-per-primitive.md) ([web](https://dev.epicgames.com/documentation/en-us/unreal-engine/storing-custom-data-in-unreal-engine-materials-per-primitive?application_version=5.9)) - How to use Custom Primitive Data: enable Use Custom Primitive Data on scalar/vector parameters, assign Primitive Data Index, set values per mesh from Blueprint or component defaults, keeping dynamic instancing to cut draw calls versus MIDs. keys: `Use Custom Primitive Data`, `Primitive Data Index`, `Set Custom Primitive Data Float`, `Set Custom Primitive Data Vector`, `Custom Primitive Data Defaults`, `stat scenerendering`, `r.MeshDrawCommand.DynamicInstancing`. - **[core]** [Substrate Materials Overview](pages/overview-of-substrate-materials-in-unreal-engine.md) ([web](https://dev.epicgames.com/documentation/en-us/unreal-engine/overview-of-substrate-materials-in-unreal-engine?application_version=5.9)) - Full guide to Substrate materials: enablement and conversion, Blendable vs Adaptive GBuffer, Slab inputs (Diffuse Albedo, F0, MFP), blend and lighting modes, BSDF/operator/helper nodes, parameter blending, translucency, performance and debug view modes. keys: `Substrate materials`, `Convert to Substrate`, `Front Material`, `Substrate Slab BSDF`, `Blendable GBuffer`, `Adaptive GBuffer`, `Substrate Vertical Layer`, `Substrate Horizontal Blend`, `Substrate Coverage Weight`, `Substrate Metalness-To-DiffuseAlbedo-F0`, `r.Substrate.BytesPerPixel`, `r.Substrate.MaxClosureCount`. Gotchas: Substrate is on by default for new projects; existing projects upgrading to 5.7+ stay non-Substrate unless opted in; Converting a material to Substrate is permanent, and Substrate materials render black if Substrate is disabled; Adaptive GBuffer only on SM6 PC/Mac/Linux and current consoles, costs more and forces DBuffer decals; Limitations: incomplete platform testing, Beta Path Tracer support, DX11 and Mac issues; glints need r.Substrate.Glints=1.
- **[core]** [Temporal Super Resolution](pages/temporal-super-resolution-in-unreal-engine.md) ([web](https://dev.epicgames.com/documentation/en-us/unreal-engine/temporal-super-resolution-in-unreal-engine?application_version=5.9)) - In-depth reference for TSR, the default temporal upscaler: screen percentage and convergence (stat tsr), Anti-Aliasing scalability group, history/Nyquist history, translucency and velocity, Has Pixel Animation, flicker analysis, history resurrection, ghosting troubleshooting, DumpGPU workflow and the full r.TSR.* cvar list. keys: `stat tsr`, `sg.AntiAliasingQuality`, `r.AntiAliasingMethod`, `r.ScreenPercentage`, `r.TSR.Visualize`, `r.TSR.History.ScreenPercentage`, `r.TSR.ShadingRejection.Flickering.Period`, `r.TSR.ShadingRejection.Flickering.FrameRateCap`, `r.TSR.Velocity.WeightClampingSampleCount`, `Has Pixel Animation`, `Output Depth and Velocity`, `Previous Frame Switch`. Gotchas: Epic/Cinematic AA quality stores history at 200% making the history update ~4x more expensive; use High or lower to save GPU; Translucent materials do not draw velocities by default and ghost; enable Output Depth and Velocity; Opaque materials with panning/pixel animation ghost unless Has Pixel Animation is set; WPO driven by animated material parameters needs the Previous Frame Switch node for correct motion vectors.
- **[core]** [Texture Asset Editor](pages/texture-asset-editor-in-unreal-engine.md) ([web](https://dev.epicgames.com/documentation/en-us/unreal-engine/texture-asset-editor-in-unreal-engine?application_version=5.9)) - Reference for the Texture Asset Editor: toolbar preview tools, texture info, LOD/mip, compression, texture (sRGB, filter, tiling, Never Stream), adjustment and compositing settings, the Oodle RDO panel and the per-platform resolved settings panel. keys: `Texture Asset Editor`, `Mip Gen Settings`, `LOD Bias`, `Texture Group`, `Never Stream`, `Compression Settings`, `Maximum Texture Size`, `Lossy Compression Amount`, `sRGB`, `Flip Green Channel`, `Virtual Texture Streaming`, `Engine > Texture Encoding`. Gotchas: Non-power-of-2 textures get NoMipMaps on import and cannot texture stream; top mip must be multiple of 4 for compression; Uncheck sRGB when channels are used as masks; Try Encodings changes are not saved; On-disk Sizes are only estimates; Editing a Final-encoded texture switches it to Fast (non-RDO) encode, which can look different.
- **[core]** [Texture Material Expressions](pages/texture-material-expressions-in-unreal-engine.md) ([web](https://dev.epicgames.com/documentation/en-us/unreal-engine/texture-material-expressions-in-unreal-engine?application_version=5.9)) - Reference for texture-sampling expressions: TextureSample, TextureObject, TextureObjectParameter, TextureSampleParameter2D/SubUV/Cube, TextureProperty, SceneColor, SpriteTextureSampler, FontSample and ParticleSubUV. keys: `TextureSample`, `TextureObject`, `TextureObjectParameter`, `TextureSampleParameter2D`, `TextureSampleParameterCube`, `TextureSampleParameterSubUV`, `TextureProperty`, `SceneColor`, `SpriteTextureSampler`, `MipValueMode`, `Sampler Type`, `SpriteTexture`. - **[core]** [Textures](pages/textures-in-unreal-engine.md) ([web](https://dev.epicgames.com/documentation/en-us/unreal-engine/textures-in-unreal-engine?application_version=5.9)) - Hub page on texture assets: supported import formats (png, tga, psd, exr, dds, tiff, etc.), power-of-two sizing advice, and links to the Texture Graph Editor, Texture Asset Editor, format settings, streaming and virtual texturing. keys: `Texture Graph Editor`, `Texture Asset Editor`, `.png`, `.tga`, `.exr`, `.dds`, `.psd`. Gotchas: Non-power-of-two textures are never streamed and get no mipmaps; Some GPUs do not support textures larger than 8192 pixels.
- **[core]** [Texturing Material Functions](pages/texturing-material-functions-in-unreal-engine.md) ([web](https://dev.epicgames.com/documentation/en-us/unreal-engine/texturing-material-functions-in-unreal-engine?application_version=5.9)) - Reference for texturing material functions: world/local-aligned and triplanar projection (WorldAlignedTexture, WorldAlignedNormal, WorldCoordinate3Way), DetailTexturing, CylindricalUVs, TextureCropping, CustomRotator, HeightLerp, SubUV_Function sprite sheets, TwoSidedTexturing and more. keys: `WorldAlignedTexture`, `WorldAlignedNormal`, `WorldCoordinate3Way`, `LocalAlignedTexture`, `DetailTexturing`, `CylindricalUVs`, `TextureCropping`, `CustomRotator`, `HeightLerp`, `SubUV_Function`, `TwoSidedTexturing`, `ZWorldSpaceFlow`. Gotchas: World-space projected textures swim on moving/animated objects; LocalAlignedTexture Normal input is nonfunctional; CameraWorldBlend appears still in development and may not give expected results; TwoSidedTexturing does nothing unless the material is Two Sided.
- **[core]** [Using Transparency in Materials](pages/using-transparency-in-unreal-engine-materials.md) ([web](https://dev.epicgames.com/documentation/en-us/unreal-engine/using-transparency-in-unreal-engine-materials?application_version=5.9)) - Tutorial for building translucent materials (Blend Mode Translucent, Opacity parameter), adding reflections via Surface TranslucencyVolume, tinted glass with Thin Translucent, checking overdraw in Shader Complexity, and fixing draw-order with Translucency Sort Priority. keys: `Translucent`, `Opacity`, `Lighting Mode`, `Surface TranslucencyVolume`, `Surface ForwardShading`, `Thin Translucent`, `Thin Translucent Material`, `Shader Complexity`, `Translucency Sort Priority`. Gotchas: Translucent colored shadows only work with Static Lighting and Lightmass; Many reflective translucent materials hurt performance; Overdraw from stacked translucency gets expensive per layer; Changing Translucency Sort Priority can cause new sorting issues for spawned effects; define a convention.
- **[core]** [Utility Material Expressions](pages/utility-material-expressions-in-unreal-engine.md) ([web](https://dev.epicgames.com/documentation/en-us/unreal-engine/utility-material-expressions-in-unreal-engine?application_version=5.9)) - Reference for utility material nodes such as Lerp, Fresnel, DepthFade, SphereMask, Noise, Vector Noise, BumpOffset, RotateAboutAxis, Desaturation, distance field nodes, QualitySwitch/FeatureLevelSwitch, Previous Frame Switch and Thin Translucent output. keys: `LinearInterpolate`, `Fresnel`, `DepthFade`, `SphereMask`, `Noise`, `Vector Noise`, `RotateAboutAxis`, `DistanceToNearestSurface`, `DistanceFieldGradient`, `Previous Frame Switch`, `QualitySwitch`, `Thin Translucent`. Gotchas: DistanceFieldGradient and DistanceToNearestSurface require Generate Mesh Distance Fields in Project Settings; Previous Frame Switch requires Output velocities due to vertex deformation enabled; Thin Translucent needs Blend Mode Translucent, Shading Model Thin Translucent, Lighting Mode Surface ForwardShading; Vector Noise is expensive at runtime; bake to a texture once the look is set.
- **[core]** [Viewport Modes](pages/viewport-modes-in-unreal-engine.md) ([web](https://dev.epicgames.com/documentation/en-us/unreal-engine/viewport-modes-in-unreal-engine?application_version=5.9)) - Reference for editor viewport view modes (Lit, Unlit, Wireframe, Lighting Only, Light/Shader Complexity, Lightmap Density, collision, LOD/HLOD coloration, GBuffer buffer visualization, landscape visualizers, exposure) with hotkeys and console commands. keys: `viewmode lit`, `viewmode unlit`, `viewmode wireframe`, `viewmode lightingonly`, `viewmode shadercomplexity`, `viewmode lightcomplexity`, `viewmode CollisionPawn`, `viewmode CollisionVisibility`, `viewmode LODColoration`, `viewmode hlodcoloration`, `MaxPixelShaderAdditiveComplexityCount`, `BaseEngine.ini`. - **[core]** [Virtual Shadow Maps](pages/virtual-shadow-maps-in-unreal-engine.md) ([web](https://dev.epicgames.com/documentation/en-us/unreal-engine/virtual-shadow-maps-in-unreal-engine?application_version=5.9)) - Full guide to Virtual Shadow Maps, the default UE5 shadow method for Nanite/Lumen: enabling, SMRT soft shadows, directional clipmaps, local lights, page caching and invalidation (WPO, Shadow Cache Invalidation Behavior), static caching, coarse pages, visualization modes, stats, profiling, platform requirements and limitations. keys: `Shadow Map Method`, `r.Shadow.Virtual.Enable`, `r.Shadow.Virtual.SMRT.RayCountDirectional`, `r.Shadow.Virtual.ResolutionLodBiasDirectional`, `r.Shadow.Virtual.Cache`, `r.Shadow.Virtual.Visualize`, `r.Shadow.Virtual.MaxPhysicalPages`, `r.Shadow.Virtual.Stats`, `r.Shadow.Virtual.NormalBias`, `Shadow Cache Invalidation Behavior`, `World Position Offset Disable Distance`, `Max World Position Offset Displacement`. Gotchas: Designed for Nanite; non-Nanite geometry is far more expensive, so enable Nanite even on low-poly meshes; WPO/PDO and skeletal deformation invalidate cached pages every frame; Exceeding the physical page pool causes corrupted/checkerboard shadows; Needs DX12 SM6.6 atomics or Vulkan; Subsurface Profile/transmission not supported.
- **[core]** [Volumetric Fog](pages/volumetric-fog-in-unreal-engine.md) ([web](https://dev.epicgames.com/documentation/en-us/unreal-engine/volumetric-fog-in-unreal-engine?application_version=5.9)) - Covers Volumetric Fog on the Exponential Height Fog component: global settings, per-light Volumetric Scattering Intensity and Cast Volumetric Shadow, local fog via Volume-domain particle materials, temporal reprojection, baked lighting, performance and unsupported features. keys: `Exponential Height Fog`, `Volumetric Fog`, `Scattering Distribution`, `Extinction Scale`, `View Distance`, `r.VolumetricFog.GridSizeZ`, `Volumetric Scattering Intensity`, `Cast Volumetric Shadow`, `Volume`, `Compute Fog Per-Pixel`, `profilegpu`, `r.PostProcessing.PropagateAlpha`. Gotchas: Shadow-casting Point/Spot lights cost about 3x in fog; Fast-moving lights (flashlights, muzzle flashes) leave trails from temporal reprojection; set their scattering to 0; Volume materials only work on particles; Not supported: IES/Light Functions on point/spot lights, Source Radius, fog center decoupled from camera.
- **[core]** [Working with Nanite-Enabled Content](pages/working-with-naniteenabled-content.md) ([web](https://dev.epicgames.com/documentation/en-us/unreal-engine/working-with-naniteenabled-content?application_version=5.9)) - Explains content types that break Nanite's pixel-proportional scaling (aggregate geometry like foliage, closely stacked surfaces, faceted normals) and covers Nanite foliage authoring with Preserve Area, Max WPO Displacement, static displacement mapping, runtime Nanite Tessellation setup, Nanite skeletal meshes and Nanite spline meshes. keys: `Preserve Area`, `Max World Position Offset Displacement`, `r.Nanite.AllowTessellation`, `r.Nanite.Tessellation`, `Enable Tessellation`, `Trim Relative Error`, `Displacement Maps`, `Displacement Fade`, `Max Edge Length Factor`, `r.Nanite.MaxPixelsPerEdge`, `r.SplineMesh.RenderNanite`, `ConsoleVariables.ini`. Gotchas: Nanite Tessellation and Static Displacement Mapping are experimental; r.Nanite.AllowTessellation is read-only and must be set in config; Vertex:triangle ratio of 2:1 or higher (faceted normals) makes Nanite meshes much more expensive; Masked cards and dense foliage render slower than solid geometry; enabling Nanite on card foliage is not always faster; Tessellation ignores Pixel Depth Offset, has no crack-free displacement, and large Magnitude hurts culling and VSM performance (use ~64x smaller Magnitude on Landscape).
- **[core]** [World Position Offset Material Functions](pages/world-position-offset-material-functions-in-unreal-engine.md) ([web](https://dev.epicgames.com/documentation/en-us/unreal-engine/world-position-offset-material-functions-in-unreal-engine?application_version=5.9)) - Reference for vertex-animation WPO material functions: SimpleGrassWind for foliage sway, SplineThicken, CameraOffset for depth sorting, ObjectPivotPoint, ObjectScale, PivotAxis, RotateAboutWorldAxis_cheap, StaticMeshMorphTargets and Wind. keys: `SimpleGrassWind`, `SplineThicken`, `CameraOffset`, `ObjectPivotPoint`, `ObjectScale`, `PivotAxis`, `RotateAboutWorldAxis_cheap`, `StaticMeshMorphTargets`, `Wind`, `Remove Degenerate Triangles`. Gotchas: SimpleGrassWind should be the last WPO node added; ObjectPivotPoint and ObjectScale only work in the vertex shader, not the pixel shader; SplineThicken meshes must be very thin, normalized UVs, imported with Remove Degenerate Triangles disabled; PivotAxis supports only uniform scaling.
- [useful] [Adding Global Shaders to Unreal Engine](pages/adding-global-shaders-to-unreal-engine.md) ([web](https://dev.epicgames.com/documentation/en-us/unreal-engine/adding-global-shaders-to-unreal-engine?application_version=5.9)) - C++ example of adding a Global Shader: .usf file, FGlobalShader subclasses with DECLARE_EXPORTED_SHADER_TYPE and IMPLEMENT_SHADER_TYPE, binding parameters, drawing a fullscreen quad, and testing with a console variable. keys: `FGlobalShader`, `DECLARE_EXPORTED_SHADER_TYPE`, `IMPLEMENT_SHADER_TYPE`, `ShouldCache`, `ModifyCompilationEnvironment`, `FShaderParameter`, `GetGlobalShaderMap`, `r.ShaderDevelopmentMode=1`, `recompileshaders changed`, `ELoadingPhase::PostConfigInit`, `.usf`. - [useful] [Building Texture Streaming Data](pages/building-texture-streaming-data-in-unreal-engine.md) ([web](https://dev.epicgames.com/documentation/en-us/unreal-engine/building-texture-streaming-data-in-unreal-engine?application_version=5.9)) - How to run Build Texture Streaming and use the accuracy view modes (Primitive Distance, Mesh UV Density, Material Texture Scale, Required Texture Resolution) to diagnose blurry or over-streamed textures. keys: `Build Texture Streaming`, `BuildMaterialTextureStreamingData`, `Material Texture Scales`, `Primitive Distance Accuracy`, `Mesh UV Density Accuracy`, `Required Texture Resolution`, `Streaming Distance Multiplier`, `r.Streaming.AnalysisIndex`, `r.Streaming.DropMips`, `log TextureStreamingBuild level all`. Gotchas: Decal and Landscape materials are not supported by the analysis; Material Instances keep stale data if a parent changed but children were not resaved; Textures with the same name in one material share required resolution; Non-UV0/world-position sampling falls back to UV channel 0 with scale 1.
- [useful] [Bump Mapping Without Tangent Space](pages/bump-mapping-without-tangent-space-in-unreal-engine.md) ([web](https://dev.epicgames.com/documentation/en-us/unreal-engine/bump-mapping-without-tangent-space-in-unreal-engine?application_version=5.9)) - Explains ddx/ddy derivative expressions and the bump-mapping material functions (ComputeFilterWidth, PerturbNormalHQ, PreparePerturbNormalHQ) that turn a grayscale/procedural bump into a world-space normal without tangent space. keys: `ddx`, `ddy`, `ComputeFilterWidth`, `PerturbNormalLQ`, `PerturbNormalHQ`, `PreparePerturbNormalHQ`, `Tangent Space Normal`. Gotchas: ddx/ddy only work in the pixel shader and show 2x2 block artifacts; World-space normal output needs the material's tangent-space normal setting off; Procedural bump is expensive; flipped/mirrored UVs not handled; PerturbNormalLQ is reference only, not in the function library.

- [useful] [Capsule Shadows Quick Start](pages/capsule-shadows-quick-start-in-unreal-engine.md) ([web](https://dev.epicgames.com/documentation/en-us/unreal-engine/capsule-shadows-quick-start-in-unreal-engine?application_version=5.9)) - Step-by-step tutorial: create a reduced shadow Physics Asset for the Third Person mannequin, assign it as the Shadow Physics Asset, enable Capsule Direct/Indirect Shadows on the character Mesh component, and build lighting to test. keys: `SK_Mannequin`, `Create > Physics Asset > Create`, `Minimum Bone Size`, `Shadow Physics Asset`, `Capsule Direct Shadows`, `Capsule Indirect Shadows`, `Capsule Indirect Shadow Min Visibility`, `ThirdPersonCharacter`, `Light Source Angle`. - [useful] [Cinematic Depth of Field](pages/cinematic-depth-of-field-in-unreal-engine.md) ([web](https://dev.epicgames.com/documentation/en-us/unreal-engine/cinematic-depth-of-field-in-unreal-engine?application_version=5.9)) - Explains Cinematic depth of field for desktop/console: how focal length, aperture (f-stop) and focus distance interact, procedural diaphragm blade bokeh, Cine Camera and Post Process DOF settings, optimization cvars, and the removed legacy Bokeh DOF. keys: `Focal Distance`, `Aperture (F-stop)`, `Maximum Aperture (minimum f-stop)`, `Number of Diaphragm Blades`, `Diaphragm Blade Count`, `Depth Blur Radius`, `Depth of Field Layers`, `r.DOF.Kernel.MaxBackgroundRadius`, `r.DOF.Kernel.MaxForegroundRadius`, `r.DOF.Scatter.MaxSpriteRatio`, `Draw Debug Focus Plane`. - [useful] [Cull Distance Volumes](pages/cull-distance-volumes-in-unreal-engine.md) ([web](https://dev.epicgames.com/documentation/en-us/unreal-engine/cull-distance-volumes-in-unreal-engine?application_version=5.9)) - Explains Cull Distance Volumes, which hide Actors beyond distances set per object size via Cull Distance pairs, with example values and best practices for avoiding popping. keys: `Cull Distance Volume`, `Cull Distances`, `Size`, `Cull Distance`, `Current Max Draw Distance`, `Cached Cull Distance`, `Max Draw Distance`, `Allow Cull Distance Volume`. - [useful] [Custom Material Expressions](pages/custom-material-expressions-in-unreal-engine.md) ([web](https://dev.epicgames.com/documentation/en-us/unreal-engine/custom-material-expressions-in-unreal-engine?application_version=5.9)) - How to use the Custom material expression to write HLSL inside a material: Code, Output Type, Inputs, Additional Outputs, Additional Defines, Include File Paths, with a blur example and known pitfalls. keys: `Custom`, `Code`, `Output Type`, `Inputs`, `Additional Outputs`, `Additional Defines`, `Include File Paths`, `Texture2DSample`. - [useful] [Customized UVs](pages/customized-uvs-in-unreal-engine-materials.md) ([web](https://dev.epicgames.com/documentation/en-us/unreal-engine/customized-uvs-in-unreal-engine-materials?application_version=5.9)) - Explains Customized UVs, which move UV math (e.g. tiling, world-space mapping) to the vertex shader via the Num Customized UVs material property, and when linear vs non-linear math gives correct results. keys: `CustomizedUVs`, `Num Customized UVs`, `TexCoord`, `Texture Coordinate`. Gotchas: Only Movable or Stationary lights; cannot be baked into lightmaps; Atlas materials cannot sample depth buffer, world position or GBuffer, and UVs should not be manipulated; Directional Lights are currently forced not to sample the atlas; Colored light functions need Deferred Lighting Uses Light Function Atlas enabled.
- [useful] [Light Mixer](pages/using-the-light-mixer-in-unreal-engine.md) ([web](https://dev.epicgames.com/documentation/en-us/unreal-engine/using-the-light-mixer-in-unreal-engine?application_version=5.9)) - Describes the Light Mixer editor window (Window > Light Mixer) that lists every light in the level, including light components inside Actors and Blueprints, for bulk editing, solo/mute, filtering, configurable attribute columns and user-defined Light Collections. keys: `Light Mixer`, `Window > Light Mixer`, `Sync Selection`, `Rebuild List`, `Open Generic Object Mixer Instance`, `Select or Add Collection`, `Replace Selected Actors With`, `Attach To`, `Environment Light Mixer`. Gotchas: Lights that are components of other Actors/Blueprints can be edited but not moved or reparented in the Light Mixer; The All collection cannot be deleted, duplicated, renamed or reordered; Added attribute columns appear in list order; column placement is not yet configurable.
- [useful] [Light Shafts](pages/using-light-shafts-in-unreal-engine.md) ([web](https://dev.epicgames.com/documentation/en-us/unreal-engine/using-light-shafts-in-unreal-engine?application_version=5.9)) - Explains Directional Light light shaft settings: the occlusion method that masks fog/atmosphere in-scattering and the bloom method that radially blurs bright scene color around the sun, with GPU costs. keys: `Enable Light Shaft Occlusion`, `Occlusion Mask Darkness`, `Occlusion Depth Range`, `Enable Light Shaft Bloom`, `Bloom Scale`, `Bloom Threshold`, `Bloom Tint`, `Light Shaft Override Direction`. Gotchas: Only 3 lighting channels supported; Does not work with Static lights or Static-mobility meshes; use Stationary or Movable; Only affects direct lighting on opaque materials; translucent and masked materials do not work.

- [useful] [Lit Translucency](pages/lit-translucency-in-unreal-engine.md) ([web](https://dev.epicgames.com/documentation/en-us/unreal-engine/lit-translucency-in-unreal-engine?application_version=5.9)) - Explains how translucent materials are lit via the translucency lighting volume, self-shadowing, reflection captures, Surface ForwardShading per-pixel lighting, and the Thin Translucent shading model for glass. keys: `r.TranslucencyLightingVolumeDim`, `r.TranslucencyLightingVolumeInnerDistance`, `r.TranslucencyLightingVolumeOuterDistance`, `Translucency Lighting Mode`, `Surface ForwardShading`, `Thin Translucent`, `Thin Translucent Material`, `TLM_Surface`, `Indirect Lighting Cache`. - [useful] [Material Analyzer](pages/unreal-engine-material-analyzer-tool.md) ([web](https://dev.epicgames.com/documentation/en-us/unreal-engine/unreal-engine-material-analyzer-tool?application_version=5.9)) - How to use the Material Analyzer (Tools > Audit > Material Analyzer) to list a material's instance descendants, group them by static overrides, create local collections and reparent to reduce shader permutations. keys: `Material Analyzer`, `Tools > Audit > Material Analyzer`, `Create Local Collection`, `Static Switch Parameters`. - [useful] [Material Data Types](pages/material-data-types-in-unreal-engine.md) ([web](https://dev.epicgames.com/documentation/en-us/unreal-engine/material-data-types-in-unreal-engine?application_version=5.9)) - Introduces the Float, Float2, Float3 and Float4 data types in the Material Editor and the Constant, Constant2/3/4Vector, Scalar Parameter and Vector Parameter nodes that create them. keys: `Constant`, `Scalar Parameter`, `Constant2Vector`, `Constant3Vector`, `Constant4Vector`, `Vector Parameter`, `Convert to Parameter`, `Channel Names`.
