- [useful] [Material Function Expressions](pages/material-function-expressions-in-unreal-engine.md) ([web](https://dev.epicgames.com/documentation/en-us/unreal-engine/material-function-expressions-in-unreal-engine?application_version=5.9)) - Reference for nodes used to build and call Material Functions: FunctionInput, FunctionOutput, MaterialFunctionCall, StaticBool, StaticSwitch and TextureObject. keys: `FunctionInput`, `FunctionOutput`, `MaterialFunctionCall`, `StaticBool`, `StaticSwitch`, `TextureObject`, `Use Preview Value As Default`, `Sort Priority`. - [useful] [MegaLights](pages/megalights-in-unreal-engine.md) ([web](https://dev.epicgames.com/documentation/en-us/unreal-engine/megalights-in-unreal-engine?application_version=5.9)) - Explains MegaLights, a stochastic ray-traced direct lighting path for many shadowed area lights: how to enable it, ray tracing vs VSM shadow methods, light complexity visualization, directional/particle light support, translucency and fog integration, scalability, profiling and limits. keys: `MegaLights`, `Allow MegaLights`, `MegaLights Shadow Method`, `r.MegaLights.Allow`, `r.MegaLights.DirectionalLights`, `r.MegaLights.Debug`, `r.MegaLights.Visualize.LightComplexity`, `r.MegaLights.NumSamplesPerPixel`, `r.MegaLights.DownsampleMode`, `r.MegaLights.HardwareRayTracing.EvaluateMaterialMode`, `r.MegaLights.SimpleLightMode`, `Fallback Relative Error`. Gotchas: Tagged experimental; designed for ray-tracing-capable PCs and current consoles, prompts to enable Support Hardware Ray Tracing; Incompatible with the Forward Renderer; water, clouds, heterogeneous volumes and local volumetrics unsupported; Directional lights are off by default; recommended to keep the sun on deferred lighting + VSM; Alpha-masked surfaces only correct via screen traces unless EvaluateMaterialMode 1 (costly); quality drops with many overlapping lights.
- [useful] [Mesh Distance Fields](pages/mesh-distance-fields-in-unreal-engine.md) ([web](https://dev.epicgames.com/documentation/en-us/unreal-engine/mesh-distance-fields-in-unreal-engine?application_version=5.9)) - Explains how per-mesh Signed Distance Fields and the Global Distance Field work (used for DFAO, DF shadows, GPU particle collision, and Lumen software ray tracing), how to enable and visualize them, tune resolution, and set up foliage. keys: `Generate Mesh Distance Fields`, `Distance Field Resolution Scale`, `Two-Sided Distance Field Generation`, `Affect Distance Field Lighting`, `Show > Visualize > Mesh Distance Fields`, `Show > Visualize > Global Distance Field`, `Visualize Distance Field`, `Software Ray Tracing`. Gotchas: Generated offline; cannot be generated at runtime; Only rigid meshes cast DF shadows; skeletal meshes need Capsule Shadows; WPO/displacement deformation causes self-shadowing artifacts; non-uniform scaling not handled correctly; Enabling Generate Mesh Distance Fields requires an editor restart; max 256 voxels per axis per mesh.
- [useful] [Mesh Distance Fields Properties](pages/mesh-distance-fields-properties-in-unreal-engine.md) ([web](https://dev.epicgames.com/documentation/en-us/unreal-engine/mesh-distance-fields-properties-in-unreal-engine?application_version=5.9)) - Reference of every Mesh Distance Field setting: Project Settings (Generate Mesh Distance Fields, voxel density), light properties for distance field shadows, Sky Light DFAO occlusion controls, Static Mesh Editor build/general settings and per-actor distance field options. keys: `Generate Mesh Distance Fields`, `Distance Field Voxel Density`, `Rendering > Software Ray Tracing`, `Distance Field Shadows`, `Distance Field Trace Distance`, `Ray Start Offset Depth Scale`, `Source Angle`, `Occlusion Max Distance`, `Occlusion Combine Mode`, `Distance Field Resolution Scale`, `Two-Sided Distance Field Generation`, `Distance Field Self Shadow Bias`. Gotchas: Generate Mesh Distance Fields raises build time and memory even if unused, and needs an editor restart; Changing Distance Field Voxel Density rebuilds all distance fields and needs restart; large values eat memory; Adjust Ray Start Offset Depth Scale only by small amounts; Affect Distance Field Lighting requires Cast Shadow enabled.
- [useful] [Misc Material Functions](pages/misc-material-functions-in-unreal-engine.md) ([web](https://dev.epicgames.com/documentation/en-us/unreal-engine/misc-material-functions-in-unreal-engine?application_version=5.9)) - Reference for miscellaneous material functions: TimeWithSpeedVariable, OffsetAndScaleTo1, PassThrough, SplitComponents and Flipbook (play a sprite-sheet texture as an animation by rows/columns). keys: `TimeWithSpeedVariable`, `OffsetAndScaleTo1`, `PassThrough`, `SplitComponents`, `Flipbook`, `Frac Time`. - [useful] [Movie Render Pipeline](pages/movie-render-pipeline-in-unreal-engine.md) ([web](https://dev.epicgames.com/documentation/en-us/unreal-engine/movie-render-pipeline-in-unreal-engine?application_version=5.9)) - Overview of offline rendering of Level Sequences with Movie Render Queue (jobs, presets, local/remote render, basic PNG render walkthrough), Movie Render Graph (graph-based configs), and the one-click Quick Render tool with its settings and Play Render Output viewer options. keys: `Movie Render Queue`, `Movie Render Graph`, `Quick Render`, `Window > Cinematics > Movie Render Queue`, `Render (Local)`, `Render (Remote)`, `Movie Pipeline Queue`, `Alpha Output`, `Support Primitive Alpha Holdout (Deferred)`, `Deferred Rendering`, `Quick Render Settings`, `Play Render Output`. Gotchas: Movie Render Queue plugin must be enabled and the editor restarted; Render (Remote) requires saving changes so the separate process can read them from disk; Deferred Rendering setting must exist in the config for an image to render; Game projects may disable Support Primitive Alpha Holdout (Deferred) to avoid its performance cost.
- [useful] [Neural Network Engine Overview](pages/neural-network-engine-overview-in-unreal-engine.md) ([web](https://dev.epicgames.com/documentation/en-us/unreal-engine/neural-network-engine-overview-in-unreal-engine?application_version=5.9)) - Explains the Neural Network Engine (NNE) API for running neural network inference at runtime or in editor: CPU, GPU and RDG interfaces, runtime lookup, importing models as UNNEModelData assets, creating models and model instances, with a minimal C++ CPU example. keys: `NNE`, `INNERuntimeCPU`, `INNERuntimeGPU`, `INNERuntimeRDG`, `UNNEModelData`, `UE::NNE::GetRuntime`, `UE::NNE::GetAllRuntimeNames`, `CreateModelCPU`, `CreateModelInstanceCPU`, `SetInputTensorShapes`, `RunSync`, `NNERuntimeORTCpu`. Gotchas: Beta feature; use caution when shipping; Not all runtimes are available on all platforms; always check returned weak/shared pointers for validity; SetInputTensorShapes must be called before first inference and whenever input shapes change; Caller owns input/output tensor memory and must keep it valid for the whole inference call.
- [useful] [NVIDIA Nsight Aftermath for GPU Pipeline Debugging](pages/nvidia-nsight-aftermath-for-gpu-pipeline-debugging-in-unreal-engine.md) ([web](https://dev.epicgames.com/documentation/en-us/unreal-engine/nvidia-nsight-aftermath-for-gpu-pipeline-debugging-in-unreal-engine?application_version=5.9)) - How to enable NVIDIA Nsight Aftermath GPU crash dumps on Windows/NVIDIA so the log shows a GPU marker stack after a device-removed/hung crash. keys: `r.GPUCrashDebugging`, `-gpucrashdebugging`, `ConsoleVariables.ini`, `[Aftermath]`, `DXGI_ERROR_DEVICE_REMOVED`, `DXGI_ERROR_DEVICE_HUNG`. - [useful] [Opacity Material Functions](pages/opacity-material-functions-in-unreal-engine.md) ([web](https://dev.epicgames.com/documentation/en-us/unreal-engine/opacity-material-functions-in-unreal-engine?application_version=5.9)) - Reference for the SoftOpacity material function, which combines Fresnel, depth fade and pixel depth so translucent objects fade near the camera and at edges. keys: `SoftOpacity`, `DepthFadeDistance`, `OpacityIn`, `FadeDistance`, `OutputUsesDepthBias`, `OutputNoDepthBias`. - [useful] [Optimizing and Debugging Projects for Real-Time Rendering](pages/optimizing-and-debugging-projects-for-realtime-rendering-in-unreal-engine.md) ([web](https://dev.epicgames.com/documentation/en-us/unreal-engine/optimizing-and-debugging-projects-for-realtime-rendering-in-unreal-engine?application_version=5.9)) - Hub page for rendering optimization: links to real-time guidelines, forward renderer, screen percentage/dynamic resolution, config files and scalability, stat commands, Nanite/LODs/texture streaming/culling, RenderDoc, Unreal Insights, GPUDump, Render Resource Viewer, Primitive Debugger and GPU crash pages.
- [useful] [Orthographic Camera](pages/orthographic-camera-in-unreal-engine.md) ([web](https://dev.epicgames.com/documentation/en-us/unreal-engine/orthographic-camera-in-unreal-engine?application_version=5.9)) - How to set a Camera actor to Orthographic projection (e.g. isometric games), its Ortho Width and clip-plane settings, and console variables for auto planes, view-origin correction, VSM clipmap tuning, debug forcing, and depth/fog adjustments. keys: `Projection Mode`, `Ortho Width`, `Auto Calculate Ortho Planes`, `Ortho Near Clip Plane`, `Ortho Far Clip Plane`, `Update Ortho Planes`, `r.Ortho.AutoPlanes`, `r.Ortho.AllowNearPlaneCorrection`, `r.Ortho.VSM.EstimateClipmapLevels`, `r.Ortho.Debug.ForceAllCamerasToOrtho`, `r.Ortho.DepthThicknessScale`, `r.Ortho.FogHeightAdjustment`. Gotchas: Cinematic cameras have no orthographic option; Debug ortho cvars are disabled in shipping builds; Newer features may not be optimized for orthographic; VSM with mixed Nanite/non-Nanite is tricky; Volumetric clouds render poorly in orthographic views.
- [useful] [Overview of Shaders in Plugins](pages/overview-of-shaders-in-plugins-unreal-engine.md) ([web](https://dev.epicgames.com/documentation/en-us/unreal-engine/overview-of-shaders-in-plugins-unreal-engine?application_version=5.9)) - High-level guide to adding global shaders in plugins: .ush vs .usf files, virtual shader paths (/Engine/, /Plugin/), render-thread rules, FGlobalShader skeleton, debug cvars and troubleshooting include errors. keys: `PostConfigInit`, `ENQUEUE_RENDER_COMMAND`, `IsInRenderingThread`, `FGlobalShader`, `IMPLEMENT_SHADER_TYPE`, `/Engine/Public/Platform.ush`, `r.ShaderDevelopmentMode`, `r.DumpShaderDebugInfo`, `ConsoleVariables.ini`, `.usf`, `.ush`. Gotchas: Plugins cannot add a new shading model to the Material Editor; Shader-containing modules need LoadingPhase PostConfigInit or you get 'not found' errors; r.DumpShaderDebugInfo=1 fills the disk quickly; All shaders must include Platform.ush/usf directly or indirectly.
- [useful] [Panini Projection](pages/panini-projection-in-unreal-engine.md) ([web](https://dev.epicgames.com/documentation/en-us/unreal-engine/panini-projection-in-unreal-engine?application_version=5.9)) - Explains the Panini projection post-process that corrects wide-FOV perspective distortion, controlled by r.LensDistortion CVars and applied in the upscale pass, plus a material WPO alternative. keys: `r.LensDistortion.Panini.D`, `r.LensDistortion.Panini.S`, `r.LensDistortion.ScreenFit`, `r.ScreenPercentage`. - [useful] [Path Tracer](pages/path-tracer-in-unreal-engine.md) ([web](https://dev.epicgames.com/documentation/en-us/unreal-engine/path-tracer-in-unreal-engine?application_version=5.9)) - Full guide to the hardware-accelerated Path Tracer: enabling it, using it in the viewport and Movie Render Queue, PathTracing post-process settings, denoisers, sky/atmosphere/fog, glass and absorption materials, supported-feature table, useful cvars and FAQ (HighResShot, runtime node, TDR timeouts, Nanite). keys: `Path Tracing`, `Support Hardware Ray Tracing`, `Support Compute Skin Cache`, `PathTracingRayTypeSwitch`, `PathTracingQualitySwitch`, `Path Tracing Buffer Texture`, `Enable Path Tracing`, `r.PathTracing.VisibleLights`, `r.PathTracing.Denoiser.Name`, `r.PathTracing.DispatchSize`, `r.RayTracing.Nanite.Mode`, `r.HighResScreenshotDelay`. Gotchas: Requires Hardware Ray Tracing, DirectX 12 and an RTX/DXR GPU; Moving lights, skinned meshes, Niagara and WPO do not invalidate accumulation, causing streaking in editor; use MRQ; HDRIBackdrop is incompatible (double-counted lighting); Heavy scenes can trigger D3D device-removed timeouts; tune r.PathTracing.DispatchSize/FlushDispatch.
- [useful] [Pivot Painter Tool 2.0](pages/pivot-painter-tool-2.0-in-unreal-engine.md) ([web](https://dev.epicgames.com/documentation/en-us/unreal-engine/pivot-painter-tool-2.0-in-unreal-engine?application_version=5.9)) - Guide to Pivot Painter 2.0, a 3ds Max MAXScript that bakes pivot, axis and hierarchy data into textures, plus import settings and the PivotPainter2FoliageShader material function for wind-driven hierarchical foliage animation and its optimization. keys: `PivotPainter2.ms`, `PivotPainter2FoliageShader`, `ms_PivotPainter2_*`, `Process The Selected Object Hierarchy`, `Tangent Space Normals`, `Shared Wind Settings`, `Wind Setting`, `BlendAngleCorrectedNormals`, `PivotPainter2`, `Combine Meshes`, `Full Precision UVs`, `VectorDisplacementMap(RGBA8)`. Gotchas: Requires 3ds Max (tested 2015/2016) with units set to centimeters; Textures need NoMipMaps, sRGB off, Nearest filter; 16-bit EXR uses HDR compression; Materials must have Tangent Space Normals disabled; Non-uniformly scaled meshes in Max give broken results; do a full reimport rather than Reimport.
- [useful] [Pixel Inspector](pages/pixel-inspector-in-unreal-engine.md) ([web](https://dev.epicgames.com/documentation/en-us/unreal-engine/pixel-inspector-in-unreal-engine?application_version=5.9)) - How to use the Pixel Inspector (Tools > Debug) to read final color, scene/HDR color and GBuffer values (normal, metallic, roughness, base color, shading model, AO) for a pixel under the mouse in any viewport. keys: `Pixel Inspector`, `Tools > Debug > Pixel Inspector`, `Apply Pre-Exposure before writing to the scene color`. Gotchas: Pre-Exposure field needs the Apply Pre-Exposure project setting enabled; Press Escape to freeze inspection on the last pixel.
- [useful] [Procedurals Material Functions](pages/procedurals-material-functions-in-unreal-engine.md) ([web](https://dev.epicgames.com/documentation/en-us/unreal-engine/procedurals-material-functions-in-unreal-engine?application_version=5.9)) - Reference for procedural texture material functions: GeneratedBand and GeneratedOffsetBands for UV bands, NormalFromHeightmap to derive a normal map from a heightmap TextureObject, and the animated NormalFromHeightmapChaos. keys: `GeneratedBand`, `GeneratedOffsetBands`, `NormalFromHeightmap`, `NormalFromHeightmapChaos`, `TextureObject`, `FunctionInput_Texture2D`. Gotchas: NormalFromHeightmap takes a TextureObject, not a TextureSample; NormalFromHeightmapChaos is expensive and may lack a heightmap input (page gives steps to add one).
- [useful] [Ray Tracing Performance Guide](pages/ray-tracing-performance-guide-in-unreal-engine.md) ([web](https://dev.epicgames.com/documentation/en-us/unreal-engine/ray-tracing-performance-guide-in-unreal-engine?application_version=5.9)) - Explains Hardware Ray Tracing costs (BLAS rebuilds for skinned/dynamic meshes, per-frame TLAS build, ray traversal, hit shading) and the cvars, stats and debug views to measure and cut them, including culling, WPO handling, memory residency, Far Field and a 60 fps cvar list. keys: `r.RayTracing.Geometry.SkeletalMeshes`, `r.RayTracing.Geometry.StaticMeshes.WPO`, `r.RayTracing.DynamicGeometry.MaxUpdatePrimitivesPerFrame`, `r.RayTracing.Scene.UseTracingFeedback`, `r.RayTracing.Culling`, `r.RayTracing.Culling.Radius`, `r.RayTracing.UseReferenceBasedResidency`, `Ray Tracing Min LOD`, `Visible in Ray Tracing`, `Ray Tracing Quality Switch`, `Stat SceneRendering`, `r.RayTracing.Visualize`. Gotchas: High-poly Skeletal Meshes rebuild BLAS every frame and quickly become a major GPU cost; WPO ignored in ray tracing by default; opt-in only works ~50 m around camera; Heavy mesh overlap (kitbashing, skyboxes, grass) makes traversal very slow; disable Visible in Ray Tracing; Traversal debug visualization modes are console-only.
- [useful] [Reflections Captures](pages/reflections-captures-in-unreal-engine.md) ([web](https://dev.epicgames.com/documentation/en-us/unreal-engine/reflections-captures-in-unreal-engine?application_version=5.9)) - Explains Sphere and Box Reflection Capture actors: how they capture static cubemaps and reproject them, lightmap mixing, using a specified HDRI cubemap, capture and Sky Light cubemap resolution, visualization view modes and limitations. keys: `Sphere Reflection Capture`, `Box Transition Distance`, `Reflection Source Type`, `Specified Cubemap`, `Build Reflection Capture`, `Reflection Capture Resolution`, `Reduce lightmap mixing on smooth surfaces`, `r.ReflectionEnvironmentBeginMixingRoughness`, `r.ReflectionEnvironmentEndMixingRoughness`, `r.ReflectionEnvironmentLightmapMixBasedOnRoughness`, `r.reflectioncapture.enablelightfunctions`, `SLS Specified Cubemap`. Gotchas: Captures are static at runtime; dynamic objects are not reflected; Static lights should not be used with the Reflection Environment because they put direct light into lightmaps; Cubemap resolution must be a power of 2; high values cost a lot of GPU memory; At most 341 reflection captures active at once; box shape only suits hallways/rectangular rooms.

- [useful] [Understanding Lightmapping in Unreal Engine](pages/understanding-lightmapping-in-unreal-engine.md) ([web](https://dev.epicgames.com/documentation/en-us/unreal-engine/understanding-lightmapping-in-unreal-engine?application_version=5.9)) - Guidelines for lightmap UVs for baked (static/stationary) lighting: auto-generation on import, custom unwraps, padding, Lightmap Coordinate Index and resolution, Lightmap Density view mode, World Settings lightmap compression/atlas size, and error coloring for overlapping/wrapping UVs. keys: `Lightmap Coordinate Index`, `Lightmap Resolution`, `Overridden Light Map Res`, `Min Lightmap Resolution`, `Source Lightmap Index`, `Destination Lightmap Index`, `Lightmap Density`, `Compress Lightmaps`, `Packed Light and Shadow map Texture Size`, `Use Error Coloring`, `Edit > Statistics`, `Build > Lighting Info`. - [useful] [User Scene Textures for Post Process Materials](pages/post-process-material-user-scene-textures-in-unreal-engine.md) ([web](https://dev.epicgames.com/documentation/en-us/unreal-engine/post-process-material-user-scene-textures-in-unreal-engine?application_version=5.9)) - Step-by-step guide to User Scene Textures, transient render targets written and read by post process materials for multi-pass effects, building a variable screen-edge blur from downsample and separable Gaussian blur passes chained via material instances and a TripleBilinearLerp function. keys: `User Scene Texture`, `User Texture Divisor`, `Resolution Relative To Input`, `Disable Pre Exposure Scale`, `Post Process Overrides`, `Scene Color Before Bloom`, `SceneTextureFetch`, `r.PostProcessing.UserSceneTextureDebug`, `PostProcessInput0`, `Blendable Priority`, `Post Process Materials`, `TripleBilinearLerp`. - [useful] [Using a Subsurface Profile](pages/using-a-subsurface-profile-in-your-unreal-engine-materials.md) ([web](https://dev.epicgames.com/documentation/en-us/unreal-engine/using-a-subsurface-profile-in-your-unreal-engine-materials?application_version=5.9)) - Walkthrough for creating a Subsurface Profile asset, setting a material's Shading Model to Subsurface Profile, overriding the profile in a Material Instance, and tuning Surface Albedo and Mean Free Path settings for skin or wax-like surfaces. keys: `Subsurface Profile`, `Shading Model`, `Mean Free Path Color`, `Mean Free Path Distance`, `Surface Albedo`, `SubsurfaceAmount`, `Create Material Instance`, `SM_Statue`. Gotchas: Subsurface Profile is screen-space based; Very large Mean Free Path Distance (e.g. 50) causes ghosted/multiple-image artifacts; around 5 looks natural; If no profile is assigned a default profile approximating Caucasian skin is used; Keep Opacity at 1 and tune the profile instead; Opacity only dampens the effect.
- [useful] [Using Bump Offset](pages/using-bump-offset-in-unreal-engine.md) ([web](https://dev.epicgames.com/documentation/en-us/unreal-engine/using-bump-offset-in-unreal-engine?application_version=5.9)) - Step-by-step tutorial building a brick material that uses the BumpOffset node (parallax mapping) driven by a height map in a texture alpha channel to offset UVs for added depth. keys: `BumpOffset`, `BumpOffset_Advanced`, `Height Ratio`, `T_Brick_Clay_New_D`, `T_Brick_Clay_New_N`. Gotchas: Node errors until a height map is connected to Height; Too high Height Ratio causes UV swimming; tutorial lowers 0.05 to 0.005; Does not change silhouette; illusion breaks at grazing view angles.

Gotchas: Option is greyed out unless Generate Mesh Distance Fields is enabled and light is Movable or Stationary; For Directional Lights DF shadows only apply beyond the CSM Dynamic Shadow Distance.
- [useful] [Using Look-up Tables for Color Grading](pages/using-lookup-tables-for-color-grading-in-unreal-engine.md) ([web](https://dev.epicgames.com/documentation/en-us/unreal-engine/using-lookup-tables-for-color-grading-in-unreal-engine?application_version=5.9)) - How to author a 256x16 color grading LUT in an image editor from a neutral LUT, import it with the right texture settings, and apply it via a Post Process Volume's Color Grading LUT. keys: `Color Grading LUT`, `Color Grading LUT Intensity`, `RGBTable16x1.png`, `NoMipMaps`, `Color Lookup Table`, `Color Grading > Global`. Gotchas: LUT texture must use Mip Gen Settings NoMipMaps and Texture Group Color Lookup Table; LUTs work in LDR sRGB after tonemapping and do not carry to HDR displays; Epic recommends the Post Process Color Grading controls instead.

- [useful] [Using Pix on Windows with Unreal Engine](pages/using-pix-on-windows-with-unreal-engine.md) ([web](https://dev.epicgames.com/documentation/en-us/unreal-engine/using-pix-on-windows-with-unreal-engine?application_version=5.9)) - How to install Microsoft PIX and attach it to the editor or game with the -AttachPix command-line argument to take single-frame GPU captures of D3D12 (or D3D11 via D3D11On12). keys: `-AttachPix`, `Force D3D11On12`, `Use Less CPU in Background`, `UEEditor.exe`. Gotchas: PIX supports Windows 10/11, D3D12, and D3D11 only via emulation (Force D3D11On12); Disable the 'Use Less CPU in Background' editor setting if captures are missing events; -AttachPix is the only setup step needed since UE 5.5.

- [useful] [Using Texture Masks](pages/using-texture-masks-in-unreal-engine.md) ([web](https://dev.epicgames.com/documentation/en-us/unreal-engine/using-texture-masks-in-unreal-engine?application_version=5.9)) - Tutorial on grayscale/channel-packed texture masks for emissive regions and per-region material properties, using the Starter Content chair, with tips on compression and sRGB. keys: `Texture Mask`, `T_Chair_M`, `M_Chair`, `sRGB`, `Sampler Type`, `Linear Color`. Gotchas: Uncheck sRGB on packed mask textures, then change existing sampler nodes to Linear Color or the material fails to compile; Alpha channels greatly increase texture memory; Green channel usually compresses best.
- [useful] [UV Editor](pages/uv-editor-in-unreal-engine.md) ([web](https://dev.epicgames.com/documentation/en-us/unreal-engine/uv-editor-in-unreal-engine?application_version=5.9)) - Describes the UV Editor (from Modeling Mode or right-click a mesh) with 2D/3D viewports and tools for sew, split, layout/repack, transform, align, distribute, channels, seams, AutoUV (PatchBuilder, UVAtlas, XAtlas) and unwrap methods, plus UDIM management. keys: `UV Editor`, `AutoUV`, `Patch Builder`, `UV Atlas`, `XAtlas`, `Unwrap`, `SpectralConformal`, `Layout`, `Repack`, `Sew`, `Split`, `Channels`. ## Gameplay Systems

- **[core]** [Actor Lifecycle](pages/unreal-engine-actor-lifecycle.md) ([web](https://dev.epicgames.com/documentation/en-us/unreal-engine/unreal-engine-actor-lifecycle?application_version=5.9)) - Order of Actor callbacks for load-from-disk, Play in Editor, SpawnActor and SpawnActorDeferred paths, then EndPlay/Destroy and garbage collection (BeginDestroy, FinishDestroy) and GC clustering settings. keys: `PostLoad`, `PostActorCreated`, `OnConstruction`, `PreInitializeComponents`, `PostInitializeComponents`, `BeginPlay`, `UWorld::SpawnActorDeferred`, `AActor::FinishSpawning`, `EndPlay`, `OnDestroyed`, `s.ForceGCAfterLevelStreamedOut`, `Create Garbage Collector UObject Clusters`. Gotchas: PostLoad and PostActorCreated are mutually exclusive; EndPlay does not guarantee destruction; actors can be resurrected on quick sublevel reload; OnDestroyed is legacy; put cleanup in EndPlay.
- **[core]** [Actors](pages/actors-in-unreal-engine.md) ([web](https://dev.epicgames.com/documentation/en-us/unreal-engine/actors-in-unreal-engine?application_version=5.9)) - Overview of AActor: placeable objects whose transform comes from the root component, component types (UActorComponent, USceneComponent, UPrimitiveComponent), spawning, ticking, replication, and destroying actors. keys: `AActor`, `SpawnActor`, `RootComponent`, `UActorComponent`, `USceneComponent`, `UPrimitiveComponent`, `Tick`, `TickComponent`, `Destroy`. Gotchas: Actors have no transform of their own; it comes from the root SceneComponent; Destroyed actors are marked pending kill and cleaned up at next garbage collection.

## Gameplay Tutorials

- **[core]** [Events](pages/events-in-unreal-engine.md) ([web](https://dev.epicgames.com/documentation/en-us/unreal-engine/events-in-unreal-engine?application_version=5.9)) - Reference for built-in Blueprint event nodes and their output pins: Level Reset, Actor Begin/End Overlap, Hit, Any/Point/Radial Damage, cursor over, Begin Play, End Play, Destroyed, Tick, Receive Draw HUD, Custom Event. keys: `Event Actor Begin Overlap`, `Event Hit`, `Event Any Damage`, `Event Point Damage`, `Event Radial Damage`, `Event Begin Play`, `Event End Play`, `Event Tick`, `Event Receive Draw HUD`, `Generate Overlap Events`, `Simulation Generates Hit Events`, `EEndPlayReason`. Gotchas: Overlap events need both actors to have Generate Overlap Events and overlap-allowing collision responses; Damage events execute only on the server (local client counts as server in single player); Event Level Reset only exists in the Level Blueprint; Receive Draw HUD only in HUD subclasses; Event Destroyed will be deprecated; use End Play.
- **[core]** [Saving and Loading Your Game](pages/saving-and-loading-your-game-in-unreal-engine.md) ([web](https://dev.epicgames.com/documentation/en-us/unreal-engine/saving-and-loading-your-game-in-unreal-engine?application_version=5.9)) - C++ guide to the SaveGame system: subclass USaveGame, then save/load with UGameplayStatics sync, async and binary (memory) functions using slot names and user indices. keys: `USaveGame`, `UGameplayStatics`, `CreateSaveGameObject`, `SaveGameToSlot`, `AsyncSaveGameToSlot`, `FAsyncSaveGameToSlotDelegate`, `LoadGameFromSlot`, `AsyncLoadGameFromSlot`, `SaveGameToMemory`, `SaveDataToSlot`, `LoadDataFromSlot`, `LoadGameFromMemory`. Gotchas: AsyncSaveGameToSlot is recommended to avoid frame hitches; Binary save/load functions are synchronous only; On development platforms saves are .sav files in Saved/SaveGames.
- **[core]** [Setting Up a Game Mode](pages/setting-up-a-game-mode-in-unreal-engine.md) ([web](https://dev.epicgames.com/documentation/en-us/unreal-engine/setting-up-a-game-mode-in-unreal-engine?application_version=5.9)) - Steps to create a Game Mode Base Blueprint, set its default pawn/HUD/controller classes, assign it as the project default in Maps & Modes, and override it per level in World Settings. keys: `Game Mode Base`, `Default Pawn Class`, `Project Settings > Maps & Modes`, `Default GameMode`, `World Settings`, `GameMode Override`. Gotchas: Character, HUD, PlayerController, Spectator and Game State classes must be created separately before assigning them in the Game Mode.
- **[core]** [Using the OnHit Event](pages/using-the-onhit-event.md) ([web](https://dev.epicgames.com/documentation/en-us/unreal-engine/using-the-onhit-event?application_version=5.9)) - C++ tutorial in the First Person template: a Cube actor binds OnComponentHit, applies damage when hit by the projectile, swaps to a damaged material on a timer, and the projectile adds an impulse at the hit location. keys: `OnComponentHit`, `AddDynamic`, `UGameplayStatics::ApplyDamage`, `SetSimulatePhysics`, `SetMaterial`, `GetTimerManager().SetTimer`, `FTimerHandle`, `AddImpulseAtLocation`, `IsSimulatingPhysics`, `Replace Selected Actors with`.

## Mobile Development

- **[core]** [Class Specifiers](pages/class-specifiers.md) ([web](https://dev.epicgames.com/documentation/en-us/unreal-engine/class-specifiers?application_version=5.9)) - Table of UCLASS specifiers (Abstract, Blueprintable, BlueprintType, Config, EditInlineNew, HideCategories, MinimalAPI, Placeable, Transient, Within, etc.) and class metadata specifiers (BlueprintSpawnableComponent, DisplayName, ChildCanTick, ToolTip, etc.) controlling engine and editor behavior. keys: `UCLASS`, `Abstract`, `Blueprintable`, `BlueprintType`, `Config=ConfigName`, `EditInlineNew`, `HideCategories`, `MinimalAPI`, `NotPlaceable`, `Transient`, `BlueprintSpawnableComponent`, `ChildCanTick`. - **[core]** [Compiling Game Projects](pages/compiling-game-projects-in-unreal-engine-using-cplusplus.md) ([web](https://dev.epicgames.com/documentation/en-us/unreal-engine/compiling-game-projects-in-unreal-engine-using-cplusplus?application_version=5.9)) - Explains UnrealBuildTool builds via .build.cs/.target.cs, the build configuration states (Debug, DebugGame, Development, Shipping, Test) and targets (Game, Editor, Client, Server), and how to build a project in Visual Studio with known VS issues. keys: `UnrealBuildTool`, `*.build.cs`, `*.target.cs`, `DevelopmentEditor`, `DebugGame`, `Shipping`, `Win64`, `Include Debug Files`, `-debug`, `-game`, `UnrealEditor-Win64-DebugGame.exe`. Gotchas: Must build an Editor target to open the project in Unreal Editor with code changes; Debug configuration needs the -debug flag when opening the editor; Uncooked configurations need -game; Shipping strips console commands, stats and profiling tools; 'Project is out of date' prompt can be safely suppressed.
- **[core]** [Console Variables and Commands](pages/console-variables-cplusplus-in-unreal-engine.md) ([web](https://dev.epicgames.com/documentation/en-us/unreal-engine/console-variables-cplusplus-in-unreal-engine?application_version=5.9)) - Explains console variables and commands in C++: registering CVars with TAutoConsoleVariable or IConsoleManager, reading values, tracking changes via sinks or callbacks, loading from ConsoleVariables.ini or [SystemSettings], -ExecCmds, and the SetBy priority order. keys: `TAutoConsoleVariable`, `IConsoleManager`, `RegisterConsoleVariable`, `FindConsoleVariable`, `FAutoConsoleVariableRef`, `FAutoConsoleVariableSink`, `GetValueOnGameThread`, `ECVF_Cheat`, `ECVF_SetByConsole`, `ConsoleVariables.ini`, `-ExecCmds`, `UnregisterConsoleVariable`. Gotchas: Avoid the old Exec interface; register through the console manager; OnChanged callbacks can deadlock or fire during init/serialization; prefer polling or sinks; Lower-priority sources cannot override a higher SetBy priority (e.g. command line beats device profile); -ExecCmds syntax omits the = used in ini files.
- **[core]** [Data Assets](pages/data-assets-in-unreal-engine.md) ([web](https://dev.epicgames.com/documentation/en-us/unreal-engine/data-assets-in-unreal-engine?application_version=5.9)) - Explains UDataAsset and UPrimaryDataAsset: creating a C++ data asset class, making instances via Content Browser Miscellaneous > Data Asset, PrimaryAssetType/GetPrimaryAssetId rules for Asset Manager loading, and when to prefer Data Only Blueprints. keys: `UDataAsset`, `UPrimaryDataAsset`, `GetPrimaryAssetId`, `PrimaryAssetType`, `Primary Asset Id`, `Miscellaneous > Data Asset`, `Tools > New C++ Class`, `Asset Manager`. Gotchas: Dynamic delegates are slower than regular delegates; Check IsBound before Execute; executing an unbound delegate can corrupt memory; ExecuteIfBound may leave output parameters uninitialized.

- **[core]** [Exposing Gameplay Elements to Blueprints](pages/exposing-gameplay-elements-to-blueprints-visual-scripting-in-unreal-engine.md) ([web](https://dev.epicgames.com/documentation/en-us/unreal-engine/exposing-gameplay-elements-to-blueprints-visual-scripting-in-unreal-engine?application_version=5.9)) - Explains the UCLASS, UPROPERTY and UFUNCTION keywords that make C++ classes, variables and functions visible to Blueprints, including using UPARAM(ref) to keep by-reference parameters as input pins and UPARAM(DisplayName) to rename pins. keys: `Blueprintable`, `BlueprintType`, `NotBlueprintable`, `BlueprintReadOnly`, `BlueprintReadWrite`, `BlueprintAssignable`, `BlueprintCallable`, `BlueprintPure`, `BlueprintImplementableEvent`, `BlueprintNativeEvent`, `UPARAM(ref)`, `UPARAM(DisplayName="X (Roll)")`. Gotchas: Pass-by-reference parameters become output pins unless marked UPARAM(ref); BlueprintImplementableEvent has no native implementation; the call is ignored if the Blueprint does not implement it; BlueprintNativeEvent costs more than plain functions; use only where a Blueprint override is needed; Classes default to NotBlueprintable unless inherited otherwise.

- **[core]** [Objects](pages/objects-in-unreal-engine.md) ([web](https://dev.epicgames.com/documentation/en-us/unreal-engine/objects-in-unreal-engine?application_version=5.9)) - Covers UObject basics: the UCLASS macro and Class Default Object, creating objects with NewObject and CreateDefaultSubobject, UHT header format with .generated.h and GENERATED_BODY, ticking via FTickableGameObject, and garbage-collection-based destruction (MarkAsGarbage, IsValid). keys: `UObject`, `UCLASS`, `GENERATED_BODY`, `NewObject`, `CreateDefaultSubobject`, `GetClass`, `FTickableGameObject`, `MarkAsGarbage`, `IsValid`, `TStrongObjectPtr`, `gc.PendingKillEnabled`, `UnrealHeaderTool`. - **[core]** [String Handling](pages/string-handling-in-unreal-engine.md) ([web](https://dev.epicgames.com/documentation/en-us/unreal-engine/string-handling-in-unreal-engine?application_version=5.9)) - Overview of FName, FText and FString: what each is for, Printf/UE_LOG formatting, a conversion table between them and to/from int32/float, and using the TEXT() macro for literals. keys: `FName`, `FText`, `FString`, `FString::Printf`, `UE_LOG`, `FText::FromString`, `FText::FromName`, `FCString::Atoi`, `FCString::Atof`, `FString::SanitizeFloat`, `INVTEXT`, `TEXT()`. - **[core]** [Unreal Object Handling](pages/unreal-object-handling-in-unreal-engine.md) ([web](https://dev.epicgames.com/documentation/en-us/unreal-engine/unreal-object-handling-in-unreal-engine?application_version=5.9)) - Overview of what the UObject system provides: zero-initialization, automatic nulling of UPROPERTY references to destroyed actors/components, serialization, CDO propagation, Cast/IsA and Super, garbage collection and its Project Settings tuning, and replication basics. keys: `UPROPERTY`, `TWeakObjectPtr`, `UObject::Serialize`, `Cast`, `IsA`, `Super`, `Destroy`, `DestroyComponent`, `Create Garbage Collector UObject Clusters`, `Actor Clustering Enabled`, `Time Between Purging Pending Kill Objects`, `bCanBeInCluster`. - [useful] [Asynchronous Asset Loading](pages/asynchronous-asset-loading-in-unreal-engine.md) ([web](https://dev.epicgames.com/documentation/en-us/unreal-engine/asynchronous-asset-loading-in-unreal-engine?application_version=5.9)) - Shows how to avoid loading everything at startup by using FSoftObjectPath/TSoftObjectPtr references, UObjectLibrary queries over unloaded asset data, and FStreamableManager SynchronousLoad/RequestAsyncLoad with a completion delegate. keys: `FSoftObjectPath`, `TSoftObjectPtr`, `UObjectLibrary`, `LoadAssetDataFromPath`, `FStreamableManager`, `RequestAsyncLoad`, `SynchronousLoad`, `FStreamableDelegate`, `ToSoftObjectPath`, `GameSingletonClassName`, `AssetRegistrySearchable`, `FAssetData`. - [useful] [Asynchronous Level Loading](pages/asynchronous-level-loading-in-unreal-engine.md) ([web](https://dev.epicgames.com/documentation/en-us/unreal-engine/asynchronous-level-loading-in-unreal-engine?application_version=5.9)) - Describes experimental async (multithreaded) loading for opening levels in the editor: enabling the Clang instrumentation build and race detection, turning it on by default in DefaultEngine.ini, and loader-safe coding practices. keys: `bEnableInstrumentation`, `BuildConfiguration.xml`, `-asyncloadingthread`, `s.DetectRaceDuringLoading`, `s.AsyncLoadingThreadEnabled`, `s.AllowMultithreadedLoading`, `[/Script/Engine.EditorStreamingSettings]`, `DefaultEngine.ini`. Gotchas: Experimental; race conditions may occur; Race detection recommends 24-32 GB free memory and runs 10-20x slower; Instrumentation compiler is Clang-based; MSVC-only code may need fixes; Avoid loader flushes, UI or transaction calls and global state in code called by the loader.
- [useful] [Character Encoding](pages/character-encoding-in-unreal-engine.md) ([web](https://dev.epicgames.com/documentation/en-us/unreal-engine/character-encoding-in-unreal-engine?application_version=5.9)) - Explains text encodings (ASCII, ANSI, UTF-8, UTF-16), UE's internal UTF-16/UCS-2 string storage, how text files are loaded and saved, recommended encodings for INI and source files, TCHAR conversion macros, and East Asian encoding pitfalls in C++ source. keys: `TCHAR_TO_ANSI`, `ANSI_TO_TCHAR`, `TCHAR_TO_UTF8`, `UTF8_TO_TCHAR`, `TCHAR_TO_OEM`, `FTCHARToANSI`, `FTCHARToUTF8`, `FUTF8ToTCHAR`, `appLoadFileToString`, `appSaveStringToFile`. Gotchas: Do not retain pointers from conversion macros; they are stack-allocated and short-lived; Internal encoding only supports the Basic Multilingual Plane; East Asian characters in C++ source can break comments/strings depending on code page; UTF-8 with BOM recommended; String literals in C++ source are discouraged.
- [useful] [Coding Standard](pages/epic-cplusplus-coding-standard-for-unreal-engine.md) ([web](https://dev.epicgames.com/documentation/en-us/unreal-engine/epic-cplusplus-coding-standard-for-unreal-engine?application_version=5.9)) - Epic's C++ coding standard: type prefixes (U/A/S/I/F/E/T, b for bools), naming, const correctness, C++20 feature rules (auto, lambdas and captures, enum class, nullptr), formatting, namespaces, include hygiene, API design and platform-specific code. keys: `ENUM_CLASS_FLAGS`, `MoveTemp`, `TEXT()`, `#pragma once`, `UE_LOG`, `TObjectPtr`, `CreateWeakLambda`, `FORCEINLINE`, `override`, `nullptr`, `UE::`. Gotchas: UHT requires correct type prefixes; Avoid auto except for lambdas, verbose iterators and templates; no structured bindings; Use explicit lambda captures; captured UObject pointers are invisible to GC; Enums exposed to Blueprints must be uint8-based; namespaces not supported for UCLASS/USTRUCT.
- [useful] [Console Variables Reference](pages/unreal-engine-console-variables-reference.md) ([web](https://dev.epicgames.com/documentation/en-us/unreal-engine/unreal-engine-console-variables-reference?application_version=5.9)) - One huge table (about 6,600 rows) listing every console variable with its default value and a one-line description, grouped by system: Animation, Audio (au.*), Blueprint, Enhanced Input, Niagara (fx.*), Physics (p.*), Networking, Scalability (sg.*), Show Flags, Slate/UMG, World Partition, and a big Rendering section with sub-tables for Lumen, Nanite, Shadow/VSM, Ray Tracing, TSR, Streaming and more. Use it to look up what a cvar does and what it defaults to when tuning performance or quality in the editor or DefaultEngine.ini. keys: `r.Lumen.HardwareRayTracing`, `r.DynamicGlobalIlluminationMethod`, `r.ReflectionMethod`, `r.Nanite`, `r.Shadow.Virtual.Enable`, `r.ScreenPercentage`, `r.AntiAliasingMethod`, `r.Streaming.PoolSize`, `t.MaxFPS`, `r.VSync`, `sg.EffectsQuality`, `r.Substrate`. Gotchas: Reference table only: name, default and short description, with no usage guidance; some rows have no description; r.Lumen.HardwareRayTracing: hardware ray tracing has large scene update costs above about 100k instances; Lumen falls back to software tracing when HWRT is unavailable; Several cvars are marked experimental, e.g. r.Nanite.Tessellation / r.Nanite.AllowTessellation, r.RayTracing.EnableOnDemand, r.Shadow.FilterMethod=1 (PCSS); r.Substrate is Beta; Some cvars are deprecated and point to replacements, e.g. r.BasePassOutputsVelocity -> r.VelocityOutputPass, a.SkeletalMesh.ISPC -> a.SkinnedAsset.ISPC.

Gotchas: Commandlet runs only C++ validation rules by default; Python validators must register themselves with UEditorValidatorSubsystem.AddValidator; ValidateLoadedAsset must call AssetPasses or AssetFails on every path; Validation runs on asset save by default.

Gotchas: Busy-waiting deprecated since 5.5, replaced by oversubscription with standby threads; Waiting limits scalability; prefer prerequisites; AddNested asserts if called outside a task; Pipes are non-copyable/non-movable and a task cannot be in multiple pipes.
- [useful] [Tasks System Reference](pages/tasks-system-references-in-unreal-engine.md) ([web](https://dev.epicgames.com/documentation/en-us/unreal-engine/tasks-system-references-in-unreal-engine?application_version=5.9)) - API reference for the UE::Tasks system: TTask/FTask Launch with prerequisites and priority, IsValid, IsCompleted, Wait with task retraction, GetResult, AddNested, plus FTaskEvent and FPipe. keys: `UE::Tasks`, `Tasks/Task.h`, `TTask`, `FTask`, `Launch`, `Prerequisites`, `UE_SOURCE_LOCATION`, `Wait`, `GetResult`, `AddNested`, `FTaskEvent`, `FPipe`. Gotchas: BusyWait is deprecated since UE 5.5; Every FTaskEvent must be triggered before destruction or it asserts; GetResult asserts on an invalid (unlaunched) task; A pipe must have no incomplete tasks when destroyed.
- [useful] [TSet](pages/set-containers-in-unreal-engine.md) ([web](https://dev.epicgames.com/documentation/en-us/unreal-engine/set-containers-in-unreal-engine?application_version=5.9)) - Reference for TSet, the hashed unordered container of unique elements: creating, Add/Emplace/Append, iteration, Contains/Find/Index queries, Remove/Empty/Reset, Sort, slack management (Reserve, Shrink, Compact) and custom DefaultKeyFuncs hashing. keys: `TSet`, `DefaultKeyFuncs`, `GetTypeHash`, `FSetElementId`, `TSetAllocator`, `Emplace`, `Append`, `Find`, `CompactStable`, `Shrink`, `Reserve`, `UPROPERTY`. ## Samples and Tutorials

- **[core]** [City Sample PCG](pages/city-sample-pcg-for-unreal-engine.md) ([web](https://dev.epicgames.com/documentation/en-us/unreal-engine/city-sample-pcg-for-unreal-engine?application_version=5.9)) - Explains the City Sample PCG demo plugin: a full procedural city built only with PCG and the PCG Primitives plugin, its 18 ordered PCG graphs and spline guides, pausing/debug/cleanup workflow, World Partition partitioning settings, Shape Grammar Definition assets (with MCP skill), and the Assign City Sample Building primitive and its style codes. keys: `PCGPrimitives`, `/PCGPrimitives/Primitives`, `Assign_CitySample_Buildings`, `Assign_ShapeGrammarDefinition`, `BP_ShapeGrammarRule`, `BP_ShapeGrammarDefinition`, `/PCGToolset/Skills/Skill_PCGShapeGrammarDefinition.Skill_PCGShapeGrammarDefinition`, `Tools > PCG framework > Cleanup All PCG components`, `Partition Grid Size`, `L_CitySamplePCG_demo`, `PCG_1_1_Terrain`, `@data.MaxHeight`. Gotchas: Graphs depend on each other in numbered order; editing a lower-numbered graph rebuilds everything after it (roads also re-level terrain); Streaming is disabled and PCG actors are not partitioned by default; enable partitioning, World Settings streaming and load actors in the World Partition editor, and all actors must be loaded to regenerate; Building collision needs a manual checkbox; Megaplants trees need Nanite foliage enabled in Project Settings; No Mass AI traffic/pedestrians or traffic lights; not a playable experience.

Gotchas: Advanced prompts that restructure graphs need you to understand the PCG graph to check the LLM's work; Replacing vegetation relies on suitable assets already being in the project plus semantic search.

Gotchas: bUseAVX is obsolete; MinCpuArchX64 raises PC minspec and crashes on CPUs without AVX; OptimizationLevel/FPSemantics require a private PCH; CircularlyReferencedDependentModules is legacy only.

Gotchas: Editor restart may be needed after enabling or disabling a plugin; Plugin config files are not packaged with projects; copy them to the project Config folder; Plugins do not support their own DDC distribution; Modules can only depend on modules at the same or higher level (engine cannot depend on project).

## Testing and Optimizing Your Content

- **[core]** [Asserts](pages/asserts-in-unreal-engine.md) ([web](https://dev.epicgames.com/documentation/en-us/unreal-engine/asserts-in-unreal-engine?application_version=5.9)) - Reference for UE C++ assertion macros: check family (halts, stripped in shipping), verify (expression always evaluated), and ensure (non-fatal, reports once to crash reporter), with build-config behavior and examples. keys: `check`, `checkf`, `checkSlow`, `checkCode`, `checkNoEntry`, `checkNoReentry`, `checkNoRecursion`, `unimplemented`, `verify`, `ensure`, `ensureMsgf`, `USE_CHECKS_IN_SHIPPING`. Gotchas: check expressions are not evaluated in Shipping, so they must have no side effects; use verify for side effects; Slow variants only run in Debug builds; ensure reports only once per session unless using ensureAlways; Ship with USE_CHECKS_IN_SHIPPING at default 0.
- **[core]** [Common Performance Considerations](pages/common-memory-and-cpu-performance-considerations-in-unreal-engine.md) ([web](https://dev.epicgames.com/documentation/en-us/unreal-engine/common-memory-and-cpu-performance-considerations-in-unreal-engine?application_version=5.9)) - Guidance on common CPU/memory pitfalls: garbage collection spikes and manual Collect Garbage, object pooling vs spawn/destroy, Tick vs callbacks/timers/tick intervals, async spreading of work, engine threads, Tasks System, and PSO caching for shader hitches. keys: `Project Settings > Engine > Garbage Collection`, `Collect Garbage`, `UObjectGlobals::CollectGarbage`, `Timer`, `Delay`, `FRunnable`, `Tasks System`, `PSO caching`, `Timing Insights`. Gotchas: Garbage collection runs cause processing spikes, especially after destroying many objects; Pooling trades memory for CPU and is less useful for plain C++ structs; Event-driven updates can be worse than Tick if fired many times per frame; Shader compilation causes hitches; use PSO caching/precaching.
- **[core]** [Gameplay Debugger](pages/using-the-gameplay-debugger-in-unreal-engine.md) ([web](https://dev.epicgames.com/documentation/en-us/unreal-engine/using-the-gameplay-debugger-in-unreal-engine?application_version=5.9)) - Gameplay Debugger Tool overlay for runtime AI/gameplay data (Pawn, AIController, Behavior Tree, EQS, perception, navmesh) in PIE, Simulate and standalone; activation keys, the Debug Camera Controller, and C++ extension with custom components and categories. keys: `EnableGDT`, `GameplayDebugger`, `GameplayDebuggingReplicator`, `Debug AI`, `ToggleDebugCamera`, `UGameplayDebuggingComponent`, `AGameplayDebuggingHUDComponent`, `EAIDebugDrawDataView::GameView1`, `PrintString`, `DebugComponentClassName`. Gotchas: Activated with the apostrophe key by default; select an enemy by pointing at it; GameplayDebugger module must be in the project's dependency modules; Extension only possible in C++; Blueprint projects use it as-is; In Simulate, enable the Debug AI show flag.
- **[core]** [Introduction to Performance Profiling and Configuration](pages/introduction-to-performance-profiling-and-configuration-in-unreal-engine.md) ([web](https://dev.epicgames.com/documentation/en-us/unreal-engine/introduction-to-performance-profiling-and-configuration-in-unreal-engine?application_version=5.9)) - Primer on frame time vs FPS, CPU/GPU/memory bottlenecks, and the profiling and configuration tools available (Unreal Insights, stat commands, RenderDoc, Perfetto, console variables, Output Log, config files, device profiles). keys: `Show FPS`, `Stat > Engine`, `stat unit`, `r.TemporalAA.Quality`, `Window > Output Log`, `Saved/Logs`, `Unreal Insights`, `RenderDoc`, `Perfetto`, `Device Profiles`. Gotchas: Profiling attached slightly worsens performance; Console in packaged builds only in Developer or Debug builds; use Blueprint/C++ to set cvars otherwise; Profile on target hardware; editor preview is not a substitute.
- **[core]** [Play In Editor Settings](pages/play-in-editor-settings-in-unreal-engine.md) ([web](https://dev.epicgames.com/documentation/en-us/unreal-engine/play-in-editor-settings-in-unreal-engine?application_version=5.9)) - Reference for Editor Preferences > Play settings: PIE mouse control, auto-recompile Blueprints, sound, new-window size/position, standalone launch parameters, multiplayer options, Play On Device build/launch configuration and server debug drawing. keys: `Edit > Editor Preferences > Play`, `Game Gets Mouse Control`, `Auto Recompile Blueprints`, `Enable Game Sounds`, `New Viewport Resolution`, `Always On Top`, `Additional Launch Parameters`, `Build Game Before Launch`, `Launch Configuration`, `Auto Compile Blueprints on Launch`, `ServerDrawDebug`. Gotchas: Play In Editor settings only apply to sessions in the Level Viewport; Window width/height 0 uses desktop resolution.
- **[core]** [Stat Commands](pages/stat-commands-in-unreal-engine.md) ([web](https://dev.epicgames.com/documentation/en-us/unreal-engine/stat-commands-in-unreal-engine?application_version=5.9)) - Table of stat console commands (stat unit, fps, game, gpu, scenerendering, memory, streaming, anim, ai, etc.) with detail on stat levels color codes, stat startfile/stopfile captures, and reading stat unit Frame/Game/Draw/GPU/RHIT times. keys: `stat unit`, `stat fps`, `stat gpu`, `stat game`, `stat SceneRendering`, `stat InitViews`, `stat levels`, `stat startfile`, `stat stopfile`, `t.HitchFrameTimeThreshold`, `stat UnitGraph`, `Saved/Profiling/UnrealStats`. Gotchas: StartFile keeps running after PIE closes; run stat StopFile to avoid huge .uestats files; Use a non-debug build when reading stat unit for bottlenecks; Visible static mesh elements dominate render thread cost under stat InitViews.
- **[core]** [Timing Insights](pages/timing-insights-in-unreal-engine.md) ([web](https://dev.epicgames.com/documentation/en-us/unreal-engine/timing-insights-in-unreal-engine?application_version=5.9)) - Overview of the Timing Insights window, the main Unreal Insights view for CPU/GPU profiling: Frames panel, Timing view, Timers/Counters, Callers/Callees, Log view, Quick Find, and special trace channels (ContextSwitch, Task). keys: `Timing Insights`, `Frames Panel`, `Timing View Panel`, `Timers and Counters`, `Callers and Callees`, `Quick Find`, `Verse Sampling`, `UE_LOG`, `-trace=default,ContextSwitch,Task`, `-tracehost=127.0.0.1`, `Save Range As…`, `Open Source in Visual Studio`. Gotchas: ContextSwitch and Task channels need administrator privileges to take effect; Open Source in Visual Studio needs Visual Studio already open.
- **[core]** [Trace](pages/trace-in-unreal-engine-5.md) ([web](https://dev.epicgames.com/documentation/en-us/unreal-engine/trace-in-unreal-engine-5?application_version=5.9)) - Overview of the Trace framework and Unreal Trace Server, the editor's Trace toolbar widget (channels, screenshots, bookmarks, destination, start/stop, snapshots), full trace channel list, Trace.Status, tail tracing and late connect. keys: `UnrealTraceServer.exe`, `Trace.Status`, `trace.screenshot`, `trace.bookmark`, `Save Trace Snapshot`, `Start Trace`, `-tracetailmb`, `-statnamedevents`, `trace.send`, `trace.start`, `-tracefile`, `[Trace.ChannelPresets]`. Gotchas: Trace Recorder listens on port 1981; Unreal Trace Server supports only one user per machine; MemAlloc, MemTag and Module channels must be enabled from the command line, not the widget; ContextSwitch needs running as administrator on Windows.
- **[core]** [Unreal Insights](pages/unreal-insights-in-unreal-engine.md) ([web](https://dev.epicgames.com/documentation/en-us/unreal-engine/unreal-insights-in-unreal-engine?application_version=5.9)) - Overview of Unreal Insights: launching from the editor Trace status bar or prebuilt exe, the Unreal Trace Server and store, loading .utrace files and live sessions, and the Timing, Memory, Networking, Slate, Asset Loading, Cooking and Audio Insights tools. keys: `UnrealInsights.exe`, `UnrealTraceServer.exe`, `UnrealTraceServer kill`, `.utrace`, `.ucache`, `Trace > Insights > Unreal Insights`, `Timing Insights`, `Memory Insights`, `Slate Insights`, `Audio Insights`, `RunUBT.bat UnrealInsights Win64 Development`, `%LOCALAPPDATA%/UnrealEngine/Common/UnrealTrace`. Gotchas: Trace Recorder listens on port 1981; Unreal Trace Server enabled for all desktop platforms as of UE 5.3.
- **[core]** [Unreal Insights Reference](pages/unreal-insights-reference-in-unreal-engine-5.md) ([web](https://dev.epicgames.com/documentation/en-us/unreal-engine/unreal-insights-reference-in-unreal-engine-5?application_version=5.9)) - Reference of all trace channels (core, engine runtime, editor, plugins) with source files, compile-time trace macros, runtime command-line options and Trace.* console commands, Unreal Insights launch options, and keyboard shortcuts for Timing and Networking Insights. keys: `UE_TRACE_ENABLED`, `-trace=<channel1>`, `-tracehost=<ip>`, `-tracefile`, `-notraceserver`, `-statnamedevents`, `Trace.File`, `Trace.Send`, `Trace.Enable`, `Trace.Pause`, `-OpenTraceFile`, `StateTreeDebug`. Gotchas: Memory channel equals memalloc,callstack,memtag; Memory_Light equals memalloc,memtag; AssetLoadTime requires CPU channel and -statnamedevents; WorldStreaming channels are experimental and subject to change; Trace.File defaults to YourProject/Saved/Profiling.
- **[core]** [Unreal Insights Trace Quick Start Guide](pages/trace-quick-start-guide-in-unreal-engine.md) ([web](https://dev.epicgames.com/documentation/en-us/unreal-engine/trace-quick-start-guide-in-unreal-engine?application_version=5.9)) - Step-by-step setup for Unreal Insights: launching or building UnrealInsights.exe (Explorer, Visual Studio, RunUBT.bat, Tools menu), running a game to get a live session, checking Trace.Status, opening a .utrace, and late connecting. keys: `UnrealInsights.exe`, `RunUBT.bat UnrealInsights Win64 Development`, `Tools > Unreal Insights > Run Unreal Insights`, `Trace.Status`, `Trace.SnapshotFile`, `Trace.Bookmark`, `Trace.Screenshot`, `Trace.Stop`, `Unreal Insights Session Browser`. Gotchas: Default channels are Gpu, Bookmark, Frame, Cpu and Log; Check no live session is running before late connecting; stop with Trace.Stop.

Gotchas: Requires plugin enable and engine restart; Reimport/Add LOD plans must run after an Import plan that kept its assets; Add LOD needs file names ending _lod00 and matching _lod0X files; Import Options must enable what the expected result checks (e.g. Import Materials).

## Understanding the Basics

- **[core]** [Actor Mobility](pages/actor-mobility-in-unreal-engine.md) ([web](https://dev.epicgames.com/documentation/en-us/unreal-engine/actor-mobility-in-unreal-engine?application_version=5.9)) - Explains the Static, Stationary and Movable Mobility setting on Static Mesh and Light Actors and how each interacts with Lightmass lightmaps, cached shadow maps, dynamic shadows and Lumen. keys: `Mobility`, `Static`, `Stationary`, `Movable`, `Lightmass`, `Volumetric Lightmaps`, `Cached Shadow Map`. Gotchas: Too many Stationary Lights affecting one Actor hurts performance; Movable shadow-casting lights are the most expensive shadowing method; Lumen is supported by Movable lights; Non-shadow-casting Movable lights add no cost in deferred rendering.
- **[core]** [Actor Ticking](pages/actor-ticking-in-unreal-engine.md) ([web](https://dev.epicgames.com/documentation/en-us/unreal-engine/actor-ticking-in-unreal-engine?application_version=5.9)) - Explains how actors and components tick: tick group order relative to physics, tick prerequisites, setting PrimaryActorTick/PrimaryComponentTick in constructors, enabling/disabling ticks, and custom FTickFunction structs. keys: `TG_PrePhysics`, `TG_DuringPhysics`, `TG_PostPhysics`, `TG_PostUpdateWork`, `PrimaryActorTick`, `PrimaryComponentTick`, `bCanEverTick`, `AddTickPrerequisiteActor`, `AddTickPrerequisiteComponent`, `SetActorTickEnabled`, `SetComponentTickEnabled`, `FTickFunction`. Gotchas: Physics data in TG_PrePhysics is one frame old; TG_DuringPhysics may see previous or current frame physics data; Set tick settings in the constructor before BeginPlay registers tick functions.
- **[core]** [Actors Reference](pages/unreal-engine-actors-reference.md) ([web](https://dev.epicgames.com/documentation/en-us/unreal-engine/unreal-engine-actors-reference?application_version=5.9)) - Overview of common placeable Actor types grouped by purpose (mesh, brush, lights, cameras, audio, gameplay volumes like Player Start/Trigger/Blocking/Kill Z/Pain Causing, Pawn/Character types, post process, reflection captures, decals, sky/fog/cloud, Text Render, Target Point) with links to each detail page. keys: `Static Mesh Actor`, `Skeletal Mesh Actor`, `Player Start`, `Trigger Volume`, `Blocking Volume`, `Kill ZVolume`, `Pain Causing Volume`, `Default Pawn`, `Paper Character`, `Post Process Volume`, `Text Render Actor`, `Target Point`. Gotchas: Kill ZVolume is different from the Kill Z option in World Settings; Default Pawn needs a controller before it responds to input; Post Process Volume effects can be costly at runtime.
- **[core]** [AI Controllers](pages/ai-controllers-in-unreal-engine.md) ([web](https://dev.epicgames.com/documentation/en-us/unreal-engine/ai-controllers-in-unreal-engine?application_version=5.9)) - Very short overview: AIController controls a Pawn by observing the world and making decisions without human input, in contrast to PlayerController. keys: `AIController`, `PlayerController`.
- **[core]** [AI System](pages/ai-system-settings-in-the-unreal-engine-project-settings.md) ([web](https://dev.epicgames.com/documentation/en-us/unreal-engine/ai-system-settings-in-the-unreal-engine-project-settings?application_version=5.9)) - Project Settings > AI System reference: perception, hot spot and EQS manager classes, Gameplay Debugger plugin loading, AI movement acceptance radii, partial paths and strafing defaults, EQS controller queriers, Blackboard SelfActor key, BT EQS-fail clearing, and default sight collision channel. keys: `Perception System Class`, `AIPerceptionSystem`, `EnvQueryManager Class`, `Enable Debugger Plugin`, `GameplayDebuggerPlugin`, `Forget Stale Actors`, `Acceptance Radius`, `Accept Partial Paths`, `Allow Strafing`, `Add Blackboard Self Key`, `SelfActor`, `Default Sight Collision Channel`. Gotchas: Enable BT AITasks is deprecated (Gameplay Tasks for move tasks are always enabled); AISystem Module, if set, must implement IAISystemModule.
- **[core]** [Aim Offset](pages/aim-offset-in-unreal-engine.md) ([web](https://dev.epicgames.com/documentation/en-us/unreal-engine/aim-offset-in-unreal-engine?application_version=5.9)) - How to create an Aim Offset (additive Blend Space) for directional aiming: set a Preview Base Pose, add aim poses, configure samples as Mesh Space additive, and drive Yaw/Pitch from the pawn's base aim rotation in the Animation Blueprint with a base pose input. keys: `Aim Offset`, `Aim Offset 1D`, `Preview Base Pose`, `Additive Anim Type`, `Mesh Space`, `Base Pose Type`, `Selected animation frame`, `Base Pose Animation`, `Ref Frame Index`, `Aim Offset Player`. Gotchas: Samples must be additive with Mesh Space, not Local Space; Must use the same Skeleton as the target mesh; Full yaw range can look wrong while running; limit it or aim pitch only; Aim Offset node needs a Base Pose connected.
- **[core]** [Ambient Sound Actor User Guide](pages/ambient-sound-actor-user-guide-in-unreal-engine.md) ([web](https://dev.epicgames.com/documentation/en-us/unreal-engine/ambient-sound-actor-user-guide-in-unreal-engine?application_version=5.9)) - How to place and configure an Ambient Sound Actor (Sound, Volume/Pitch Multiplier, Is UI Sound, attenuation overrides, modulation) and add an Audio component to a Blueprint with the OnAudioFinished event. keys: `Ambient Sound Actor`, `Auto Activate`, `Volume Multiplier`, `Pitch Multiplier`, `Is UI Sound`, `Override Attenuation`, `Attenuation Settings`, `Allow Spatialization`, `Source Effect Chain`, `OnAudioFinished`, `Audio component`. Gotchas: Auto Activate starts playback on spawn even if the player can't hear it; Plays once per trigger unless the Sound Wave is Looping or a Sound Cue loops; Audio Volume edits need a level geometry rebuild to take effect.
- **[core]** [Animation Notifies](pages/animation-notifies-in-unreal-engine.md) ([web](https://dev.epicgames.com/documentation/en-us/unreal-engine/animation-notifies-in-unreal-engine?application_version=5.9)) - Explains Animation Notifies on Animation Sequences: built-in notify types (Niagara/particle, Sound, cloth, Reset Dynamics), Skeleton Notifies used as AnimBP events, Notify States, Sync Markers, Montage Notifies, common properties, and custom AnimNotify/AnimNotifyState Blueprint classes. keys: `Play Niagara Particle Effect`, `Timed Niagara Effect`, `Skeleton Notify`, `Add Anim Notify Event`, `Montage Notify`, `Montage Notify Window`, `Disable Root Motion`, `AnimNotify`, `AnimNotifyState`, `Received Notify`, `Received Notify Tick`, `Montage Tick Type`. Gotchas: Montage Notify events (On Notify Begin/End) require Play Montage, not Play Anim Montage; Skeleton Notifies and Sync Markers are stored on the Skeleton asset, which must be saved; By default only Sync Group leader animations fire notifies.
- **[core]** [Animation Retargeting](pages/animation-retargeting-in-unreal-engine.md) ([web](https://dev.epicgames.com/documentation/en-us/unreal-engine/animation-retargeting-in-unreal-engine?application_version=5.9)) - Explains legacy skeleton-based animation retargeting: Bone Translation Retargeting modes (Animation, Skeleton, AnimationScaled), the recommended biped setup, Rig assets for different skeletons, IK bone strategy, and the Retarget Manager. keys: `Bone Translation Retargeting`, `Animation`, `Skeleton`, `AnimationScaled`, `Recursively Set Translation Retargeting Skeleton`, `Retarget Manager`, `Rig`, `Retarget Source`, `Retarget Base Pose`, `Show > Non-Retargeted Animation`. Gotchas: Only bone translation is retargeted; rotation always comes from the animation; Different skeletons need the same Rig assigned to both Skeleton assets.
- **[core]** [Auto Retargeting](pages/auto-retargeting-in-unreal-engine.md) ([web](https://dev.epicgames.com/documentation/en-us/unreal-engine/auto-retargeting-in-unreal-engine?application_version=5.9)) - Retarget animations between skeletons straight from the Content Browser (Retarget Animation Assets, auto-generated IK Rigs/Retargeter), plus the IK Rig editor's Auto Retarget Chains and Auto Create IK (FBIK) tools and the IK Retargeter's Auto Align pose tools. keys: `Retarget Animation Assets`, `Auto Generate Retargeter`, `Auto Retarget Chains`, `Auto Create IK`, `Auto Align`, `Align All Bones`, `Align Selected Using Mesh`, `Snap Character to Ground`, `Edit Retarget Pose`, `Export Retarget Assets`, `Include Referenced Assets`, `Target Preview Mesh`. Gotchas: Auto chain/FBIK generation matches bone names against templates; only common biped templates (UE4/UE5 Mannequin, MetaHuman, Stack O Bot) are listed; Export Options do not appear when using a pre-configured IK Retargeter asset; Error shown if skeleton cannot be matched to any template.
- **[core]** [Basic Components](pages/basic-components-in-unreal-engine.md) ([web](https://dev.epicgames.com/documentation/en-us/unreal-engine/basic-components-in-unreal-engine?application_version=5.9)) - Introduces Components as attachable units of functionality on Actors (lights, movement, audio, meshes, cameras) and explains that Components created as sub-objects are instanced per Actor. keys: `Spot Light Component`, `Rotating Movement Component`, `Audio Component`, `Instanced`. - **[core]** [Behavior Tree User Guide](pages/behavior-tree-in-unreal-engine---user-guide.md) ([web](https://dev.epicgames.com/documentation/en-us/unreal-engine/behavior-tree-in-unreal-engine---user-guide?application_version=5.9)) - Step-by-step guide to creating Behavior Tree and Blackboard assets, custom Blueprint Tasks, Decorators and Services, adding Blackboard keys, assigning the Blackboard to the tree, and wiring/editing nodes in the Behavior Tree Editor. keys: `Behavior Tree`, `Blackboard`, `New Blackboard`, `New Task`, `New Decorator`, `New Service`, `BTTask_BlueprintBase`, `BTDecorator_BlueprintBase`, `BTService_BlueprintBase`, `Blackboard Asset`, `Instance Synced`, `New Key`. Gotchas: Only Composite nodes can connect to the Root node; Connections only go output to input; For performance consider native (C++) Tasks/Services instead of Blueprint ones; Rename auto-named Task/Decorator/Service assets created from the toolbar.
- **[core]** [Blend Masks and Blend Profiles](pages/blend-masks-and-blend-profiles-in-unreal-engine.md) ([web](https://dev.epicgames.com/documentation/en-us/unreal-engine/blend-masks-and-blend-profiles-in-unreal-engine?application_version=5.9)) - How to create Blend Masks (per-bone 0-1 weights used by Layered Blend Per Bone) and Time or Weight Blend Profiles (per-bone blend speed) in the Skeleton Tree, and apply them to blend nodes, state machine transitions and montages. keys: `Add Blend Mask`, `Add Time Blend Profile`, `Add Weight Blend Profile`, `Layered Blend Per Bone`, `Blend Mode`, `Blend Masks`, `Recursively Set Blend Scales`, `Blend Profile`, `Blend Profile In`, `Blend Profile Out`, `Blend Poses by bool`. Gotchas: Blend Masks and Profiles are stored on the Skeleton asset; Masks and profiles share one column/menu, so name them clearly.
- **[core]** [Blueprint Class](pages/blueprint-class-assets-in-unreal-engine.md) ([web](https://dev.epicgames.com/documentation/en-us/unreal-engine/blueprint-class-assets-in-unreal-engine?application_version=5.9)) - Defines Blueprint Classes, the common parent classes (Actor, Pawn, Character, PlayerController, Game Mode), Blueprint inheritance from other Blueprints, and Data-Only Blueprints. keys: `Blueprint Class`, `Parent Class`, `Actor`, `Pawn`, `Character`, `PlayerController`, `Game Mode`, `Data-Only Blueprint`. Gotchas: Data-Only Blueprints can only tweak inherited properties; adding code, variables or components converts them to full Blueprints.
- **[core]** [Build Configurations Reference](pages/build-configurations-reference-for-unreal-engine.md) ([web](https://dev.epicgames.com/documentation/en-us/unreal-engine/build-configurations-reference-for-unreal-engine?application_version=5.9)) - Defines UBT build configuration states (Debug, DebugGame, Development, Shipping, Test) and targets (Game, Editor, Client, Server), with tables of which combinations exist for engine-source solutions versus project-only builds. keys: `Unreal Build Tool`, `Debug`, `DebugGame`, `Development`, `Shipping`, `Test`, `Development Editor`, `-debug`, `<GAME_NAME>Client.Target.cs`, `<GAME_NAME>Server.Target.cs`, `Include Debug Files`. Gotchas: Debug-config editor needs the -debug flag to see code changes; Shipping strips console commands, stats and profiling tools; Project-only (launcher engine) builds support only DebugGame/Development for Editor and DebugGame/Development/Shipping for Game.
- **[core]** [C++ Class Wizard](pages/using-the-cplusplus-class-wizard-in-unreal-engine.md) ([web](https://dev.epicgames.com/documentation/en-us/unreal-engine/using-the-cplusplus-class-wizard-in-unreal-engine?application_version=5.9)) - Explains the C++ Class Wizard (Tools > New C++ Class...) for adding a native class with a chosen parent from Common Classes or All Classes; it generates .h/.cpp, converts a Blueprint-only project to a code project, and compiles via Live Coding. keys: `Tools > New C++ Class...`, `C++ Class Wizard`, `Common Classes`, `All Classes`, `Live Coding`. Gotchas: Class names must be alphanumeric with no spaces; Requires a compatible Visual Studio (or Xcode) version installed; Live Coding is enabled by default and compiles the new files.
- **[core]** [Calling Blueprints in the Editor](pages/calling-blueprints-in-the-unreal-editor.md) ([web](https://dev.epicgames.com/documentation/en-us/unreal-engine/calling-blueprints-in-the-unreal-editor?application_version=5.9)) - How to mark a Blueprint Custom Event or Function as Call in Editor so it appears as a button in a placed Actor's Details panel, letting you run Blueprint logic in the editor without playing. keys: `Call in Editor`, `EditorUtilityActor`, `Editor Utility Widget`. Gotchas: Events/functions with inputs are not shown as buttons; Editor Utility Blueprints derived from Actor don't expose Call in Editor buttons; Editor-only base classes are not included in packaged builds.
- **[core]** [Camera Actors](pages/camera-actors-in-unreal-engine.md) ([web](https://dev.epicgames.com/documentation/en-us/unreal-engine/camera-actors-in-unreal-engine?application_version=5.9)) - Introduces Camera Actor and Cine Camera Actor, related actors (Camera Blocking Volume, Camera Rig Crane, Camera Rig Rail, Level Sequence Actor), and how to place a camera from Place Actors and preview its view in the viewport. keys: `Camera Actor`, `Cine Camera Actor`, `Camera Blocking Volume`, `Camera Rig Crane`, `Camera Rig Rail`, `Level Sequence Actor`, `Place Actors`.
- **[core]** [Changing the Default Level](pages/changing-the-default-level-of-an-unreal-engine-project.md) ([web](https://dev.epicgames.com/documentation/en-us/unreal-engine/changing-the-default-level-of-an-unreal-engine-project?application_version=5.9)) - Steps to set the Game Default Map and Editor Startup Map in Project Settings > Maps & Modes, with advanced Transition Map and Server Default Map options. keys: `Project Settings`, `Maps & Modes`, `Game Default Map`, `Editor Startup Map`, `Default Maps`, `Local Map Options`, `Transition Map`, `Server Default Map`.
- **[core]** [Characters](pages/characters-in-unreal-engine.md) ([web](https://dev.epicgames.com/documentation/en-us/unreal-engine/characters-in-unreal-engine?application_version=5.9)) - Overview of the Character class: a Pawn with CharacterMovementComponent, CapsuleComponent and SkeletalMeshComponent for walking, jumping, flying, swimming, and what CharacterMovementComponent configures. keys: `Character`, `CharacterMovementComponent`, `CapsuleComponent`, `SkeletalMeshComponent`. Gotchas: CharacterMovementComponent assumes a vertically oriented capsule for collision; CharacterMovementComponent is specific to Characters and cannot be used by other classes.
- **[core]** [Collision Settings](pages/collision-settings-in-the-unreal-engine-project-settings.md) ([web](https://dev.epicgames.com/documentation/en-us/unreal-engine/collision-settings-in-the-unreal-engine-project-settings?application_version=5.9)) - Project Settings > Collision: define custom Object Channels and Trace Channels and edit collision Preset profiles. keys: `Object Channels`, `Trace Channels`, `Preset`, `WorldStatic`. Gotchas: Maximum of 18 custom channels (object and trace combined); Deleting an in-use object channel reverts its uses to WorldStatic; deleting an in-use trace channel gives undefined trace behavior; Editing in-use collision presets changes collision behavior.
- **[core]** [Components and Collision](pages/quick-start-guide-to-components-and-collision-in-unreal-engine-cpp.md) ([web](https://dev.epicgames.com/documentation/en-us/unreal-engine/quick-start-guide-to-components-and-collision-in-unreal-engine-cpp?application_version=5.9)) - C++ tutorial building ACollidingPawn with a USphereComponent root, visual static mesh, toggleable particle system, spring-arm camera, and a custom UPawnMovementComponent whose TickComponent uses ConsumeInputVector, SafeMoveUpdatedComponent and SlideAlongSurface to collide and slide. - **[core]** [Components Window](pages/components-window-in-unreal-engine.md) ([web](https://dev.epicgames.com/documentation/en-us/unreal-engine/components-window-in-unreal-engine?application_version=5.9)) - Using the Blueprint Editor Components window: adding, removing, transforming and renaming components, assigning assets (e.g. Static Mesh) to them, and creating component events such as overlap events via Add Event. keys: `Components`, `Add Event`, `Variable Name`, `StaticMeshComponent`, `BoxComponent`, `CapsuleComponent`, `SphereComponent`, `My Blueprint`. - **[core]** [Directional Lights](pages/directional-lights-in-unreal-engine.md) ([web](https://dev.epicgames.com/documentation/en-us/unreal-engine/directional-lights-in-unreal-engine?application_version=5.9)) - Directional Light (sun) mobility options and full property reference: Light, Light Shafts, Lightmass, Light Function, Cascaded Shadow Maps, and Atmosphere and Cloud settings such as Atmosphere Sun Light, sun index, and cloud shadow parameters. keys: `Directional Light`, `Atmosphere Sun Light`, `Atmosphere Sun Light Index`, `Source Angle`, `Cast Cloud Shadows`, `Dynamic Shadow Distance MovableLight`, `Num Dynamic Shadow Cascades`, `Forward Shading Priority`, `Contact Shadow Length`, `Per Pixel Atmosphere Transmittance`, `r.VolumetricCloud.ShadowMap.MaxResolution`, `Light Shaft Bloom`. - **[core]** [First Person Rendering](pages/first-person-rendering.md) ([web](https://dev.epicgames.com/documentation/en-us/unreal-engine/first-person-rendering?application_version=5.9)) - Explains native first-person rendering: tag primitives with First Person Primitive Type (First Person / World Space Representation) so arms and weapons render with a separate FOV and scale to avoid clipping into walls, set up the Camera Component's first-person FOV/scale, add world-space representation meshes for shadows and RT reflections, enable first-person self-shadow via CVars, and use the related material nodes. keys: `First Person Primitive Type`, `World Space Representation`, `Enable First Person Field Of View`, `Enable First Person Scale`, `r.FirstPerson.SelfShadow`, `r.FirstPerson.SelfShadow.LightTypes`, `First Person Output`, `Transform Position`, `Is First Person`, `View Property`, `IsFirstPerson`, `Near Clip Plane`. Gotchas: Self-shadow, world-space representation shadows/reflections and the IsFirstPerson scene texture need the GBuffer bit: Allow Static Lighting must be disabled, and they do not work with mobile or forward rendering; Self-shadow is screen-space traced, so only on-screen casters work; No first-person shadows on the ground without Virtual Shadow Maps or ray-traced shadows; grooms/strand hair unsupported; Too small a First Person Scale makes geometry vanish at the near clip plane; World Space Representation needs the camera to own the components.
- **[core]** [First Person Template](pages/first-person-template-in-unreal-engine.md) ([web](https://dev.epicgames.com/documentation/en-us/unreal-engine/first-person-template-in-unreal-engine?application_version=5.9)) - Introduces the First Person game template and its Arena Shooter and Survival Horror variants, listing the Blueprints, levels, weapons, AI, UI and sprint/stamina assets and their Content folders. keys: `BPWeaponBase`, `BP_FirstPersonProjectile`, `BP_FP_Horror`, `Lvl_FirstPerson`, `Lvl_Shooter`, `Lvl_Horror`, `Content/Variant_Shooter`, `Content/Variant_Horror`, `Content/FirstPerson/Blueprints`, `Content/LevelPrototyping`. - **[core]** [IK Rig Retargeting](pages/ik-rig-animation-retargeting-in-unreal-engine.md) ([web](https://dev.epicgames.com/documentation/en-us/unreal-engine/ik-rig-animation-retargeting-in-unreal-engine?application_version=5.9)) - Reference for the IK Retargeter asset and Retarget Editor: creating the retargeter from IK Rigs, defining retarget chains and the pelvis, editing/importing retarget poses (A-pose vs T-pose, Auto Align), the op stack, exporting retargeted Animation Sequences, and Override Sets/Variables driven at runtime via the Retarget Pose From Mesh node. keys: `IK Retargeter`, `Auto Create Retarget Chains`, `New Retarget Chain…`, `Set Pelvis`, `Run Retarget`, `Auto Align`, `Snap Character to Ground`, `Export Selected Animations`, `Retarget Pose From Mesh`, `Override Set to Apply`, `Profile Ops`, `Ignore Root Lock in Preview`. Gotchas: Both source and target need IK Rig assets with matching retarget chains and a pelvis defined; Chain names are matched by fuzzy string match, so keep names consistent; Retarget variables cannot be arrays, maps, or sets; an override set must be active for bound variables to apply; Override Sets replace the former Retarget Profiles workflow; use an existing (not auto-generated) retargeter for batch export with overrides.

- **[core]** [Instanced Static Mesh Component](pages/instanced-static-mesh-component-in-unreal-engine.md) ([web](https://dev.epicgames.com/documentation/en-us/unreal-engine/instanced-static-mesh-component-in-unreal-engine?application_version=5.9)) - Explains Instanced Static Mesh (ISM) and Hierarchical ISM components for drawing many copies of one mesh cheaply, ISM vs HISM trade-offs (including with Nanite), per-instance custom data, and the tools that create them: Blueprint components, Merge Actors Batch, Foliage Mode, Packed Level Actor, and Modeling Mode Harvest Instances/Pattern/ISM Editor. keys: `Instanced Static Mesh Component`, `Hierarchical Instanced Static Mesh`, `TypedElements.EnableViewportSMInstanceSelection`, `Actor > Merge Actors > Merge Actors Settings`, `Batch`, `Level > Create Packed Level Actor`, `Harvest Instances`, `Pattern`, `ISM Editor`, `Custom Primitive Data`, `Per Instance Custom Data`, `Foliage Mode`. Gotchas: Collision, materials and shadows are component-level and cannot be edited per instance; HISMs suit thousands of static instances; moving instances can cause errors with HISM; ISM culls/LODs each instance on the GPU, expensive on low-power platforms; Nanite-only projects should use ISM; Replacing an instance with a different mesh in ISM Editor adds a second ISM component.
