- **[core]** [Navigation Mesh](pages/navigation-mesh-settings-in-the-unreal-engine-project-settings.md) ([web](https://dev.epicgames.com/documentation/en-us/unreal-engine/navigation-mesh-settings-in-the-unreal-engine-project-settings?application_version=5.9)) - Project Settings > Navigation Mesh (RecastNavMesh defaults) reference: debug draw options, tile generation debug, generation parameters (tile/cell size, agent radius/height/slope/step height, partitioning, tile pool and hard limit), query heuristics, Runtime Generation mode (Static, Dynamic Modifiers Only, Dynamic), plus actor-level tick, collision/overlap-on-streaming, HLOD, World Partition and cooking properties. keys: `Agent Radius`, `Agent Height`, `Agent Max Slope`, `Agent Max Step Height`, `Cell Size`, `Tile Size UU`, `Runtime Generation`, `Fixed Tile Pool Size`, `Tile Number Hard Limit`, `Region Partitioning`, `Force Rebuild on Load`, `Enable Drawing`. Gotchas: Be very careful changing Tile Number Hard Limit on big maps; empty tiles are allocated up front (176 bytes each) and it rounds up to a power of 2; Fixed Tile Pool Size must be enabled to support streaming; Is Editor Only Actor makes references to the actor NULL in cooked builds; Draw Clusters requires WITH_NAVMESH_CLUSTER_LINKS=1.
- **[core]** [Niagara Overview](pages/overview-of-niagara-effects-for-unreal-engine.md) ([web](https://dev.epicgames.com/documentation/en-us/unreal-engine/overview-of-niagara-effects-for-unreal-engine?application_version=5.9)) - Overview of Niagara systems, emitters (Emitter/Particle Spawn and Update, Event Handler, Render groups), modules, parameter types, the Niagara Asset Browser and custom Asset Tag Definitions, plus inheritance, dynamic inputs, micro expressions, events and data interfaces. keys: `Niagara System`, `Emitter Spawn`, `Emitter Update`, `Particle Spawn`, `Particle Update`, `Event Handler`, `Set Parameter`, `CustomHLSL`, `Niagara Asset Tag Definitions`, `Niagara Fluids`, `Dynamic Inputs`, `FX > Niagara System`. - **[core]** [Niagara Renderers](pages/render-module-reference-for-niagara-effects-in-unreal-engine.md) ([web](https://dev.epicgames.com/documentation/en-us/unreal-engine/render-module-reference-for-niagara-effects-in-unreal-engine?application_version=5.9)) - Parameter reference for Niagara emitter renderers: Component, Light, Mesh, Ribbon, Sprite and Decal renderers, including facing/sorting modes, sub-UV, cutout, tessellation and the default Particles.* attribute bindings each uses. keys: `Sprite Renderer`, `Mesh Renderer`, `Ribbon Renderer`, `Light Renderer`, `Decal Renderer`, `Component Renderer`, `Use with Niagara Sprites`, `Niagara Mesh Particles`, `Sort Order Hint`, `Particles.SubImageIndex`, `Particles.RibbonWidth`, `Preview Scene Settings`. Gotchas: Metadata exists only in the editor; do not use it in game logic; Bitmask enums support values 0-31; only first 32 entries shown; BlueprintReadOnly and BlueprintReadWrite are mutually exclusive, as are Edit* and Visible*; Config/GlobalConfig cannot be given default values and imply BlueprintReadOnly.
- **[core]** [Python](pages/python-settings-in-the-unreal-engine-project-settings.md) ([web](https://dev.epicgames.com/documentation/en-us/unreal-engine/python-settings-in-the-unreal-engine-project-settings?application_version=5.9)) - Project Settings reference for the Python plugin: startup scripts, extra sys.path entries, interpreter isolation, Developer Mode (stub generation), and Python Remote Execution over UDP multicast. keys: `Startup Scripts`, `Additional Paths`, `Isolate Interpreter Environment`, `UE_PYTHONPATH`, `Developer Mode (all users)`, `Enable Remote Execution`, `Multicast Group Endpoint`, `Multicast Bind Address`, `Multicast Time-To-Live`. Gotchas: Isolation mode ignores PYTHONPATH/PYTHONHOME and user site-packages; UE_PYTHONPATH is still added; Developer Mode regenerates the Python stub file on every editor start, adding boot time; Multicast TTL 0 limits to local host, 1 to local subnet.
- **[core]** [Rendering](pages/rendering-settings-in-the-unreal-engine-project-settings.md) ([web](https://dev.epicgames.com/documentation/en-us/unreal-engine/rendering-settings-in-the-unreal-engine-project-settings?application_version=5.9)) - Project Settings > Rendering full reference: Dynamic Global Illumination Method and Reflection Method (Lumen etc.), Lumen hardware/software ray tracing modes, Shadow Map Method (Virtual Shadow Maps), Support Hardware Ray Tracing, Generate Mesh Distance Fields, static lighting, forward shading, translucency sorting, Custom Depth-Stencil, default post-process (bloom, auto-exposure, motion blur, anti-aliasing incl. TSR), virtual textures, skin cache, culling, mobile and shader permutation reduction. keys: `Dynamic Global Illumination Method`, `Reflection Method`, `Use Hardware Ray Tracing When Available`, `Software Ray Tracing Mode`, `Shadow Map Method`, `Support Hardware Ray Tracing`, `Generate Mesh Distance Fields`, `Allow Static Lighting`, `Custom Depth-Stencil Pass`, `Anti-Aliasing Method`, `Support Compute Skin Cache`, `Forward Shading`. Gotchas: Lumen needs Generate Mesh Distance Fields for Software RT, and Support Hardware Ray Tracing for HW RT (which requires Support Compute Skincache); Hardware Ray Tracing has significant scene update cost above ~100,000 instances; Virtual Shadow Maps listed as Beta and unsupported with Forward Shading; movable Nanite meshes cast no dynamic shadows under Stationary lighting; Many settings require an editor restart.

- **[core]** [Skeletal Mesh Sockets](pages/skeletal-mesh-sockets-in-unreal-engine.md) ([web](https://dev.epicgames.com/documentation/en-us/unreal-engine/skeletal-mesh-sockets-in-unreal-engine?application_version=5.9)) - How to create, edit, copy and convert Sockets in the Skeleton Tree (including mesh-only Mesh Sockets) and attach actors to them in the level, in Blueprint components via Parent Socket, or dynamically with Attach/Detach functions and their transform rules. keys: `Add Socket`, `Create Mesh Socket`, `Paste Sockets To Selected Bone`, `Enable Socket Snapping`, `Parent Socket`, `Attach Actor To Actor`, `Attach Actor To Component`, `Attach Component To Component`, `Detach From Actor`, `Detach From Component`, `Snap to Target`, `Force Always Animated`. Gotchas: Sockets edit the Skeleton asset (Mesh Sockets edit the Skeletal Mesh), so that asset must be saved; Sockets are hidden in the viewport by default (Character > Bones > Sockets); Level attachment keeps the object's world transform; zero its transform to match the socket.
- **[core]** [Skeleton Editing](pages/skeleton-editing-in-unreal-engine.md) ([web](https://dev.epicgames.com/documentation/en-us/unreal-engine/skeleton-editing-in-unreal-engine?application_version=5.9)) - Covers the in-editor Skeleton Editing tools: converting a Static Mesh to a Skeletal Mesh, adding/orienting/mirroring/renaming bones, binding and painting skin weights (brush and vertex modes), attribute maps, hotkeys, and Python automation via SkeletonModifier and SkinWeightModifier. keys: `Skeletal Mesh Editing Tools`, `Convert to Skeletal Mesh`, `Editing Tools`, `Bind Skin`, `Edit Weights`, `Geodesic Voxel`, `Prune Weights`, `Add Weight Map Layer`, `unreal.SkeletonModifier`, `unreal.SkinWeightModifier`, `add_bones`, `commit_skeleton_to_skeletal_mesh`. Gotchas: Requires the Skeletal Mesh Editing Tools plugin and an editor restart; Skin weights are auto-normalized to 1; a single-influence vertex cannot be reduced below 1.0; Prefer adding weight to other bones rather than removing weight; Flooding a bone's weights to 0 sends them back to the root bone.
- **[core]** [Skeletons](pages/skeletons-in-unreal-engine.md) ([web](https://dev.epicgames.com/documentation/en-us/unreal-engine/skeletons-in-unreal-engine?application_version=5.9)) - Explains Skeleton assets: creation on FBX import or via Create Skeleton, Skeleton Tree icons, the animation data stored on the skeleton (notifies, curves, slots, blend masks), rules for sharing one skeleton across meshes, merging on import, and Compatible Skeletons via the Retarget Manager. keys: `Skeleton`, `Create Skeleton`, `Skeleton Tree`, `Retarget Manager`, `Manage Compatible Skeletons`, `Add Skeleton`, `Skeleton Editor`. Gotchas: Sharing a skeleton requires identical bone names and hierarchy order; extra bones may only be appended; Inserting bones can cause transform offsets; Compatible skeletons are bi-directional and need near-identical hierarchies and proportions.
- **[core]** [Sky Atmosphere Component](pages/sky-atmosphere-component-in-unreal-engine.md) ([web](https://dev.epicgames.com/documentation/en-us/unreal-engine/sky-atmosphere-component-in-unreal-engine?application_version=5.9)) - Setting up the physically based Sky Atmosphere with a Directional Light (Atmosphere Sun Light) and Sky Light, explaining Rayleigh/Mie scattering, absorption, altitude, height fog interaction, sky LUTs and cvars, skydome materials, space views, sunlight shafts quality, and debugging. keys: `Sky Atmosphere`, `Atmosphere Sun Light`, `Atmosphere Sun Light Index`, `Support Sky Atmosphere Affecting Height Fog`, `Is Sky`, `Transform Mode`, `r.SkyAtmosphere.FastSkyLUT`, `r.SkyAtmosphere.AerialPerspectiveLUT.FastApplyOnOpaque`, `r.SkyAtmosphere.SampleCountMax`, `ShowFlag.VisualizeSkyAtmosphere`, `TimeOfDay_Default`, `Right Ctrl + L`. Gotchas: Ground/lower hemisphere renders black without terrain or height fog; Second directional light gets no multiple scattering; Increasing AerialPerspectiveLUT size raises memory (3D texture); Mobile needs a skydome mesh with an Is Sky material.
- **[core]** [Sky Lights](pages/sky-lights-in-unreal-engine.md) ([web](https://dev.epicgames.com/documentation/en-us/unreal-engine/sky-lights-in-unreal-engine?application_version=5.9)) - Sky Light capture behavior per mobility (Static, Stationary, Movable), Real Time Capture for dynamic time-of-day, cubemap resolution, time slicing, DFAO shadowing, Lightmass sky bounces, and full property reference including cloud ambient occlusion. keys: `Sky Light`, `Real Time Capture`, `Recapture`, `RecaptureSky`, `Source Type`, `SLS Captured Scene`, `SLS Specified Cubemap`, `Cubemap Resolution`, `Sky Distance Threshold`, `Lower Hemisphere is Solid Color`, `Cloud Ambient Occlusion`, `r.SkyLight.RealTimeReflectionCapture.TimeSlice`. Gotchas: Real Time Capture needs a Sky Atmosphere in the scene and doesn't support Volumetric Fog; RecaptureSky() costs at least 120 ms and can hitch gameplay; Non-realtime Stationary/Movable sky lights only capture on load or Recapture; Movable Sky Light DFAO shadowing needs Mesh Distance Fields enabled.
- **[core]** [Sound Cue Editor](pages/sound-cue-editor-in-unreal-engine.md) ([web](https://dev.epicgames.com/documentation/en-us/unreal-engine/sound-cue-editor-in-unreal-engine?application_version=5.9)) - Introduces Sound Waves and Sound Cues, how to create a Sound Cue, open the editor, add nodes to the Sound Node Graph and preview playback. keys: `Sound Cue`, `Sound Wave`, `Wave Player`, `Wave Param`, `Play Cue`, `Play Node`, `Sounds > Sound Cue`. - **[core]** [Sound Cue Reference](pages/sound-cue-reference-for-unreal-engine.md) ([web](https://dev.epicgames.com/documentation/en-us/unreal-engine/sound-cue-reference-for-unreal-engine?application_version=5.9)) - Node-by-node reference for Sound Cues: the Output node (sound class, attenuation, submix, concurrency, priority) and Attenuation, Branch, Concatenator, Continuous Modulator, Crossfade, Delay, Doppler, Enveloper, Looping, Mixer, Modulator, Oscillator, Random, Switch, Wave Param and Wave Player nodes, plus how named parameters are set from Blueprint. keys: `Wave Player`, `Random`, `Modulator`, `Attenuation`, `Concatenator`, `Crossfade by Param`, `Continuous Modulator`, `Set Float Parameter`, `Set Boolean Parameter`, `Set Integer Parameter`, `Override Attenuation`, `Randomize Without Replacement`. Gotchas: Named parameters cannot be set inside the Sound Cue; the In Name in the Blueprint/code call must match exactly; The Looping node is not seamless; use the Looping flag on Wave Player for seamless loops; Sound Cues without an Attenuation node are not localized; Crossfade by Param does not support negative values; Random Preselect at Level Load does not apply in PIE.
- **[core]** [Spot Lights](pages/spot-lights-in-unreal-engine.md) ([web](https://dev.epicgames.com/documentation/en-us/unreal-engine/spot-lights-in-unreal-engine?application_version=5.9)) - Spot Light cone setup (Inner/Outer Cone Angle), mobility options, and property reference for Light, Light Profiles (IES), Lightmass and Light Function. keys: `Spot Light`, `Inner Cone Angle`, `Outer Cone Angle`, `Attenuation Radius`, `Source Radius`, `Min Roughness`, `Use Inverse Squared Falloff`, `IES Texture`, `Light Function Material`. - **[core]** [Variables, Timers, and Events](pages/quick-start-guide-to-variables-timers-and-events-in-unreal-engine-cpp.md) ([web](https://dev.epicgames.com/documentation/en-us/unreal-engine/quick-start-guide-to-variables-timers-and-events-in-unreal-engine-cpp?application_version=5.9)) - C++ tutorial making a Countdown actor with a UTextRenderComponent driven by a repeating timer (SetTimer/ClearTimer with an FTimerHandle), exposing the time via UPROPERTY(EditAnywhere) and the finish event as a BlueprintNativeEvent overridden in a Blueprint child. Explains BlueprintCallable vs BlueprintImplementableEvent vs BlueprintNativeEvent and Add call to parent function. keys: `FTimerHandle`, `GetWorldTimerManager`, `SetTimer`, `ClearTimer`, `UTextRenderComponent`, `UPROPERTY(EditAnywhere)`, `UFUNCTION(BlueprintNativeEvent)`, `_Implementation`, `BlueprintCallable`, `BlueprintImplementableEvent`, `Add call to parent function`, `Spawn Emitter At Location`. Gotchas: Editor-set property values are applied after the constructor but before BeginPlay, so read them in BeginPlay; A BlueprintNativeEvent's C++ body must be in a virtual function named <Name>_Implementation; Overriding the event in Blueprint replaces the C++ behaviour unless you add a call to the parent function.
- **[core]** [Vector Material Expressions](pages/vector-material-expressions-in-unreal-engine.md) ([web](https://dev.epicgames.com/documentation/en-us/unreal-engine/vector-material-expressions-in-unreal-engine?application_version=5.9)) - Reference for Material Editor nodes that output vectors: world/camera/object/particle positions, camera and reflection vectors, constant 2/3/4 vectors (with 2/3/4+click shortcuts), LightVector for decals/light functions, Object Bounds/Orientation, pixel and vertex normals, pre-skinned local normal/position, and the Vector Noise node (Cellnoise, Perlin, Gradient, Curl, Voronoi) with derivative helpers. keys: `ActorPositionWS`, `CameraPositionWS`, `CameraVectorWS`, `Constant3Vector`, `Constant4Vector`, `LightVector`, `Object Bounds`, `ObjectPositionWS`, `PixelNormalWS`, `VertexNormalWS`, `Pre-Skinned Local Position`, `Vector Noise`. Gotchas: LightVector only works in Deferred Decal or LightFunction material domains; VertexNormalWS only works in vertex-shader inputs like WorldPositionOffset; offsetting along it splits geometry at UV seams; Vector Noise is expensive at runtime; bake to a texture via Render Targets once the look is set (Cellnoise is cheap); Perlin tiling requires Tile Size to be a multiple of three.
- **[core]** [Volume Actors](pages/volume-actors-in-unreal-engine.md) ([web](https://dev.epicgames.com/documentation/en-us/unreal-engine/volume-actors-in-unreal-engine?application_version=5.9)) - Reference of common Volume actor types and uses: Blocking, Camera Blocking, Kill Z, Pain-Causing, Physics, Trigger, Audio, Cull Distance, HLOD, Lightmass Importance, Mesh Merge Culling, Post Process, Precomputed Visibility, Level Streaming and Nav Mesh Bounds volumes, plus the need to add visuals since volumes are invisible. keys: `Blocking Volume`, `Camera Blocking Volume`, `Kill Z Volume`, `FellOutOfWorld`, `APhysicsVolume`, `Trigger Volume`, `Cull Distance Volume`, `Lightmass Importance Volume`, `Post Process Volume`, `Level Streaming Volumes`, `Nav Mesh Bounds Volume`, `Create`. Gotchas: Volumes are invisible at runtime; add a visual cue; Kill Z destroys actors by default; override FellOutOfWorld for key items; Trigger Volumes need Overlap collision response for intended actors; Press P in the viewport to visualize the Nav Mesh.

## What's New

- **[core]** [Animation Curves](pages/animation-curves-in-unreal-engine.md) ([web](https://dev.epicgames.com/documentation/en-us/unreal-engine/animation-curves-in-unreal-engine?application_version=5.9)) - How to create, import (FBX custom attributes), keyframe and manage float Animation Curves stored on the Skeleton, and use them to drive material scalar parameters, morph targets, and Anim Blueprint values; also covers Metadata Curves that output a constant 1.0. keys: `Anim Curves`, `Window > Anim Curves`, `Add Curve`, `Import Custom Attribute`, `Get Curve Value`, `Get Active Curve Names`, `Get All Curve Names`, `Connected Bones`, `Max LOD`, `Convert To Metadata`, `Metadata Curves`. Gotchas: Curves are stored on the Skeleton asset, so creating them requires saving the Skeleton; Imported custom attributes must be float type and keyframed; Material curves affect all materials on the Skeletal Mesh that share the parameter name; Anim Curves panel only available in Skeleton, Animation Sequence, or Animation Blueprint editors.
- **[core]** [Animation Node Functions](pages/animation-blueprint-node-functions-in-unreal-engine.md) ([web](https://dev.epicgames.com/documentation/en-us/unreal-engine/animation-blueprint-node-functions-in-unreal-engine?application_version=5.9)) - Explains binding function graphs to AnimGraph nodes (On Initial Update, On Become Relevant, On Update) so logic runs only when the node updates, plus Sequence Player/Evaluator setter nodes, Convert nodes, and State Machine Set State/Get State/Is State Blending nodes. keys: `On Initial Update`, `On Become Relevant`, `On Update`, `Create New Binding`, `Anim Update Context Reference`, `Anim Node Reference`, `Set Sequence`, `Set Sequence with Inertial Blending`, `Set Explicit Time`, `Set State`, `Get State`, `Convert to Animation State Machine`. Gotchas: Bound existing functions must have Thread Safe enabled; Custom bound functions need two pass-by-reference inputs: Anim Update Context Reference and Anim Node Reference; Use pure (green) Convert nodes only when bound directly on the matching node type; otherwise use the function (blue) Convert nodes; On states, functions can only be bound to the state's Output node.
- **[core]** [Automatic Navigation Link Generation](pages/automatic-navigation-link-generation.md) ([web](https://dev.epicgames.com/documentation/en-us/unreal-engine/automatic-navigation-link-generation?application_version=5.9)) - Shows how to have the NavMesh automatically generate jump-down Navigation Links via the RecastNavMesh Generate Nav Links option, tune the Nav Link Jump Down Config, measure build cost, and add custom jump behaviour through a GeneratedNavLinksProxy Blueprint. keys: `RecastNavMesh-Default`, `Generate Nav Links`, `Nav Link Jump Down Config`, `Jump Length`, `Jump Max Depth`, `Sampling Separation Factor`, `Filter Distance Threshold`, `Link Proxy Class`, `Area Class`, `GeneratedNavLinksProxy`, `Draw Tile Build Times`, `NavLink Proxy`. Gotchas: Experimental; Link generation adds CPU cost to NavMesh tile generation; Jump Length has the largest impact; Raising Sampling Separation Factor speeds generation but can produce links that collide; Cost scales with the number of NavMesh border edges.
- **[core]** [Editor Utility Widgets](pages/editor-utility-widgets-in-unreal-engine.md) ([web](https://dev.epicgames.com/documentation/en-us/unreal-engine/editor-utility-widgets-in-unreal-engine?application_version=5.9)) - How to create an Editor Utility Widget (UMG-based custom editor tab), run it, and find it under the Tools menu. keys: `Editor Utility Widget`, `Editor Utilities`, `Run Editor Utility Widget`. Gotchas: Beta; Tab only docks with Level Editor tabs.
- **[core]** [How to Modify the Navigation Mesh](pages/modifying-the-navigation-mesh-in-unreal-engine.md) ([web](https://dev.epicgames.com/documentation/en-us/unreal-engine/modifying-the-navigation-mesh-in-unreal-engine?application_version=5.9)) - Hub page linking to the preparation guide and the main guide for modifying Navigation Mesh generation, with an optional sample project level LevelMod_Navigation_0. keys: `LevelMod_Navigation_0`.

- **[core]** [Scripting the Unreal Editor Using Python](pages/scripting-the-unreal-editor-using-python.md) ([web](https://dev.epicgames.com/documentation/en-us/unreal-engine/scripting-the-unreal-editor-using-python?application_version=5.9)) - Main guide to editor Python: enabling the Python Editor Script Plugin, every way to run scripts (Python console, py command, File menu, -ExecutePythonScript, pythonscript commandlet, init_unreal.py, startup scripts, editor-only Blueprint nodes), sys.path setup, how the unreal module reflects Blueprint-exposed APIs, and best practices (set_editor_property, ScopedEditorTransaction, ScopedSlowTask, logging). **5.9:** Blueprint classes and User Defined Structs now get their own generated Python wrapper types (e.g. BP_MyActor_C) instead of their native parent/StructBase; set Engine.Python.WrapBlueprintClassesOnDemand / WrapUserDefinedStructsOnDemand to false for the 5.8 behaviour. keys: `Python Editor Script Plugin`, `unreal.get_editor_subsystem`, `LevelEditorSubsystem.load_level`, `-ExecutePythonScript`, `-run=pythonscript -script=`, `init_unreal.py`, `UE_PYTHONPATH`, `set_editor_property`, `unreal.ScopedEditorTransaction`, `unreal.ScopedSlowTask`, `PythonCallable`, `Engine.Python.WrapBlueprintClassesOnDemand`. Gotchas: Python runs only in the editor, never in PIE, Standalone or cooked builds, so it cannot be gameplay script; Do not use py in -ExecCmd at startup; script may run before the level is loaded; The pythonscript commandlet does not load levels; call load_level first, and load_level fails by default (UnsavedChangesPolicy Fail) if packages are unsaved; Never move/rename assets with os/shutil; use unreal.EditorAssetLibrary or AssetTools; PCGComponent Generate/GenerateLocal unavailable from Python (use ExecuteGraphInstance).

- **[core]** [Unreal Engine 5.9 Preview Release Notes](pages/unreal-engine-5-9-release-notes.md) ([web](https://dev.epicgames.com/documentation/en-us/unreal-engine/unreal-engine-5-9-release-notes?application_version=5.9)) - UE 5.9 Preview release notes summarising new and changed features: Unreal Canvas, Python and Unreal MCP improvements and AI toolsets, Unreal Assistant, IK Retargeter operations, UAF and Control Rig updates, Lumen World Cache, AVBOIT, Nanite culling, Ambient Lighting Volumes, shadow debugging, Dynamic Wind, PCG Concave Hull, scriptable StateTrees and Blueprints, progressive navmesh, and a WebAssembly target. **5.9:** Lists 5.9 additions: Unreal Canvas, MCP server port/origin/protocol preferences and project MCP settings, more AI toolsets, Slate Qt Bridge (PySide6), script editing of Blueprints/StateTrees/choosers, new IK Retargeter ops, Lumen World Cache, AVBOIT, Nanite culling, Ambient Lighting Volumes, Dynamic Wind; Python Foundation Packages removed. keys: `Unreal Canvas Bridge`, `Slate Qt Bridge`, `Unreal MCP`, `Toolset Registry`, `Unreal Assistant`, `Proximity IK`, `Pelvis Volume`, `Limb Twist`, `UAF AnimGen`, `Lumen World Cache`, `Concave Hull`, `Mass Characters`. Gotchas: Unreal Canvas Bridge requires the Model Context Protocol plugin; Lumen World Cache requires Hardware Ray Tracing and is enabled per project; Ambient Lighting Volumes and Dynamic Wind are Experimental; Python Foundation Packages plugin was removed.

- [useful] [Ambient Lighting Volumes](pages/ambient-lighting-volumes-in-unreal-engine.md) ([web](https://dev.epicgames.com/documentation/en-us/unreal-engine/ambient-lighting-volumes-in-unreal-engine?application_version=5.9)) - Covers the experimental Ambient Lighting Volume actor, a box or sphere that multiplies (darkens or tints) Movable Sky Light diffuse lighting inside it with soft edges, including runtime Set Tint, overlap rules, visualization, settings and troubleshooting. keys: `Ambient Lighting Volume`, `Support Ambient Lighting Volumes`, `r.SupportAmbientLightingVolumes`, `Volume Shape`, `Tint`, `Soft Transition Distance`, `Volume Sort Priority`, `Set Tint`, `Show > Visualize`, `AmbientLightingVolumes`. ## Working with Audio

- **[core]** [Audio Engine Overview](pages/audio-engine-overview-in-unreal-engine.md) ([web](https://dev.epicgames.com/documentation/en-us/unreal-engine/audio-engine-overview-in-unreal-engine?application_version=5.9)) - High-level tour of the Unreal Audio Engine: importing Sound Waves, Sound Cues, attenuation/spatialization/occlusion, PlaySound vs SpawnSound Blueprint APIs, Sound Classes, Sound Mixes and ducking, modulation, concurrency and voice limits, DSP/submixes, cooking compression and debug commands. keys: `USoundWave`, `Sound Cue`, `Sound Attenuation Settings`, `PlaySoundAtLocation`, `PlaySound2D`, `SpawnSoundAtLocation`, `SpawnSoundAttached`, `Passive Mix Modifier`, `Property Matrix`, `stat soundwave`, `stat soundcues`, `Audio3DVisualize`. Gotchas: PlaySound functions are fire-and-forget; use SpawnSound to get an Audio Component for control, attachment or loops; Multichannel (quad/5.1/7.1) sources only support 2D playback; Imported audio is stored as 16-bit uncompressed .wav.
- **[core]** [Creating Procedural Music with MetaSounds](pages/creating-procedural-music-with-metasounds.md) ([web](https://dev.epicgames.com/documentation/en-us/unreal-engine/creating-procedural-music-with-metasounds?application_version=5.9)) - Tutorial building a stereo procedural music MetaSound Source (Trigger Repeat tempo, random melody from Scale to Note Array, sine/saw synths, crossfade, ladder filter with LFO, AD envelope, stereo delay) and a Blueprint actor whose trigger boxes change BPM, crossfade and melody via audio parameters. keys: `MetaSound Source`, `UE.Source.OneShot`, `Output Format`, `Trigger Repeat`, `BPM To Seconds`, `Scale to Note Array`, `Random Get (Float:Array)`, `MIDI To Frequency (Float)`, `Ladder Filter`, `AD Envelope (Audio)`, `Set Float Parameter (Audio)`, `Execute Trigger Parameter`. Gotchas: Remove the UE.Source.OneShot interface for persistent sounds like music; Set Float Parameter and Execute Trigger Parameter nodes may require turning off Context Sensitive search.
- **[core]** [MetaSound Function Nodes Reference Guide](pages/metasound-function-nodes-reference-guide-in-unreal-engine.md) ([web](https://dev.epicgames.com/documentation/en-us/unreal-engine/metasound-function-nodes-reference-guide-in-unreal-engine?application_version=5.9)) - Per-node reference for MetaSound function nodes with every input and output: Wave Player, envelopes (AD/ADSR), delays, dynamics, filters, generators (Sine/Saw/Noise/LFO/SuperOscillator), math, mixers, music/MIDI, random, array (Random Get/Shuffle), spatialization panners and trigger nodes. keys: `Wave Player`, `AD Envelope`, `ADSR Envelope`, `Random Get`, `Shuffle`, `Trigger Repeat`, `Trigger Sequence`, `Biquad Filter`, `Compressor`, `Map Range`, `Stereo Panner`, `Wave Writer`. Gotchas: Cue points closer together than the MetaSound block rate only trigger on the last cue point in that block; Grain Delay Max Grain Count is CPU intensive; high values reduce performance and can clip; Wave Writer renders at 48,000 Hz to Saved > AudioCaptures; Mono Mixer/Stereo Mixer gains are not clamped.
- **[core]** [MetaSounds](pages/metasounds-in-unreal-engine.md) ([web](https://dev.epicgames.com/documentation/en-us/unreal-engine/metasounds-in-unreal-engine?application_version=5.9)) - Hub page linking MetaSounds docs: overview, Quick Start, Templates Quick Start, procedural music, MetaSound Pages, Builder API, Reference Guide, Function Nodes Reference, and WaveTables overview/quick start.
- **[core]** [Sound Attenuation](pages/sound-attenuation-in-unreal-engine.md) ([web](https://dev.epicgames.com/documentation/en-us/unreal-engine/sound-attenuation-in-unreal-engine?application_version=5.9)) - Reference for every Sound Attenuation asset setting: volume falloff functions and shapes, spatialization (panning/binaural, non-spatialized radius, stereo spread), air absorption, listener focus, reverb send, occlusion tracing, priority attenuation, submix sends and plugin settings. keys: `Attenuation Function`, `Attenuation Shape`, `Falloff Distance`, `Enable Spatialization`, `Non-Spatialized Radius`, `3D Stereo Spread`, `Enable Air Absorption`, `Enable Listener Focus`, `Enable Occlusion`, `Occlusion Trace Channel`, `Use Complex Collision for Occlusion`, `Enable Submix Send`. Gotchas: Binaural spatialization needs headphones; Occlusion uses simple collision by default; complex shapes may falsely occlude; Reverb send needs a World Settings reverb or audio volume reverb and a sound class that allows reverb.
- **[core]** [Sound Classes](pages/sound-classes-in-unreal-engine.md) ([web](https://dev.epicgames.com/documentation/en-us/unreal-engine/sound-classes-in-unreal-engine?application_version=5.9)) - Reference for Sound Class assets: volume/pitch/LPF/attenuation scale, child class inheritance, passive Sound Mix modifiers, routing (Apply Ambient Volume), legacy flags like Is UISound and Is Music, default submix and reverb sends, modulation settings and loading behaviour. keys: `Sound Class`, `Child Classes`, `Passive Sound Mix Modifiers`, `Push Sound Mix Modifier`, `Apply Ambient Volume`, `Always Play`, `Is UISound`, `Is Music`, `Default Submix`, `Retain on Load`, `Prime on Load`, `Force Inline`. Gotchas: Low Pass Filter Frequency of 20,000 or above has no effect; Force Inline also requires each Sound Wave's Loading Behavior Override set to Force Inline; Radio filter settings only work on Windows/Xbox with the XAudio2 backend.
- **[core]** [Sound Concurrency Reference Guide](pages/sound-concurrency-reference-guide.md) ([web](https://dev.epicgames.com/documentation/en-us/unreal-engine/sound-concurrency-reference-guide?application_version=5.9)) - Reference for Sound Concurrency assets: Max Count, Limit to Owner, Resolution Rules, Retrigger Time, volume-scaling ducking and voice steal release, plus assigning a project default or per-source Concurrency Set and overrides. keys: `Sound Concurrency`, `Max Count`, `Limit to Owner`, `Resolution Rule`, `Stop Oldest`, `Prevent New`, `Stop Quietest`, `Retrigger Time`, `Volume Scale Mode`, `Voice Steal Release Time`, `Default Sound Concurrency`, `Concurrency Set`. Gotchas: All active components count toward Max Count, including silent synths; Source Buses take two slots; Volume Scale is applied after Stop Quietest rules; Sources must satisfy every concurrency in a Concurrency Set to play.

- **[core]** [Subtitles and Closed Captions Plugin](pages/subtitles-and-closed-captions-plugin-in-unreal-engine.md) ([web](https://dev.epicgames.com/documentation/en-us/unreal-engine/subtitles-and-closed-captions-plugin-in-unreal-engine?application_version=5.9)) - Explains the Subtitles and Closed Captions plugin: subtitle assets/AssetUserData with duration, offset, priority and type, display via a TextBlock widget set in Project Settings, the Blueprint/C++ queue/stop API, Sequencer subtitle tracks, SRT import and migration from legacy SoundWave/DialogueWave subtitles. **5.9:** Subtitles embedded as AssetUserData in localized Waves from 5.8 or earlier must be migrated (Migrate Embedded Subtitles to Asset, then Fix Localized Subtitle Waves). keys: `SubtitlesAndClosedCaptions`, `SubtitlesSubsystem.h`, `USubtitleAssetUserData`, `QueueSingleSubtitle`, `QueueSubtitlesFromAsset`, `StopAllSubtitles`, `StopSubtitlesInAsset`, `ESubtitleTiming::ExternallyTimed`, `UseSoundDuration`, `DefaultSubtitleWidget`, `au.UseNewSubtitles`, `Convert Basic Overlays to Subtitles`. Gotchas: Submix names cannot contain spaces; A submix has multiple inputs but only one output; Only one recording per submix at a time; default .wav path Saved\BouncedWavFiles; Output to Master EQ Submix must be enabled for Sound Class Mix EQ settings to work.

Gotchas: Only first-order (4-channel) ambisonic assets are supported; Files without four channels are treated as normal audio; Oculus Audio and Google Resonance soundfield submixes cannot connect to each other.

Gotchas: Plugin must be enabled under Edit > Plugins > Input Devices; Based on the OSC 1.0 protocol; types are transient and created in Blueprint.

## Working with Content

- **[core]** [Animation Sequence Editor](pages/animation-sequence-editor-in-unreal-engine.md) ([web](https://dev.epicgames.com/documentation/en-us/unreal-engine/animation-sequence-editor-in-unreal-engine?application_version=5.9)) - Tour of the Animation Sequence Editor: toolbar actions (Reimport, Apply Compression, Export, Key, Make Static Mesh, Edit In Sequencer/Control Rig), the full Animation Asset Details property list (interpolation, rate scale, retargeting source, additive anim type, root motion, compression, import settings), Skeleton Tree, Asset Editor types and Asset Browser. keys: `Reimport Animation`, `Apply Compression`, `Make Static Mesh`, `Edit In Sequencer`, `Rate Scale`, `Retarget Source Asset`, `Additive Anim Type`, `EnableRootMotion`, `Root Motion Root Lock`, `Force Root Lock`, `Bone Compression Settings`, `Allow Frame Stripping`. Gotchas: Mesh Space additive type is required for Aim Offsets; Child AnimMontages with a Parent Asset can only be changed via the Asset Mapping Table; Do Not Override Compression protects high-frequency animations from the CompressAnimations commandlet.
- **[core]** [Animation Sequences](pages/animation-sequences-in-unreal-engine.md) ([web](https://dev.epicgames.com/documentation/en-us/unreal-engine/animation-sequences-in-unreal-engine?application_version=5.9)) - Explains Animation Sequence assets: importing from FBX with the import options and Skeleton selection, baking from Sequencer, editing with additive bone tracks and Record, sharing animations across skeletons (compatible skeletons, retargeting, IK Rig), and Bone/Curve Compression Settings assets. keys: `Animation Sequence`, `FBX Import Options`, `Import Animation`, `Animation Length`, `Frame Import Range`, `Bake Animation Sequence`, `Add Key`, `Bone Compression Settings`, `Curve Compression Settings`, `Error Threshold`, `Codecs`, `Import All`. Gotchas: Animations with non-whole end frame values do not import correctly; fix in DCC or set the Frame Import Range; Leaving Skeleton blank on import creates a new Skeleton; bone names and hierarchy must match to reuse one; Bone Compression Settings need at least one codec in the list.
- **[core]** [Artist Quick Start](pages/artist-quick-start-in-unreal-engine.md) ([web](https://dev.epicgames.com/documentation/en-us/unreal-engine/artist-quick-start-in-unreal-engine?application_version=5.9)) - Beginner walkthrough: create a project, make Content Browser folders, import FBX meshes and TGA textures, export meshes from Maya, build a Rock material (Subsurface shading, texture samples, constants) in the Material Editor, and assign it as a Static Mesh's default or per-Actor material. keys: `Content Browser`, `Import`, `FBX Import Options`, `Material Editor`, `Shading Model`, `Subsurface`, `Texture Sample`, `Constant3Vector`, `Static Mesh Editor`, `Save All`, `Editor Preferences > Keyboard Shortcuts`. Gotchas: States the FBX import pipeline uses FBX 2018 and other export versions may be incompatible (the FBX Content Pipeline page says FBX 2020.2); Recommends power-of-two texture sizes.
- **[core]** [Blend Spaces](pages/blend-spaces-in-unreal-engine.md) ([web](https://dev.epicgames.com/documentation/en-us/unreal-engine/blend-spaces-in-unreal-engine?application_version=5.9)) - Explains Blend Space, Blend Space 1D, Aim Offset and Aim Offset 1D assets: creating them, setting axis names/ranges, placing samples, using them via a Blend Space player in the AnimGraph, and the Asset Details properties (triangulation vs grid, smoothing, weight speed, notify trigger mode) plus Blend Graph preview and debugging. keys: `Blend Space`, `Blend Space 1D`, `Aim Offset`, `Aim Offset 1D`, `Axis Settings`, `Use Grid`, `Preferred Triangulation Direction`, `Wrap Input`, `Smoothing Time`, `Weight Speed`, `Per Bone Overrides`, `Notify Trigger Mode`. Gotchas: Leave Use Grid disabled except for special cases like Wrap Input; triangulation is more accurate; Do not combine Weight Speed/Smoothing with Smoothing Time/Smoothing Type; Thin triangles shown in red, or red-highlighted samples in grid mode, will not blend properly; Wrap Input needs similar animations at both ends of the axis to avoid popping.
- **[core]** [Blend Spaces in Animation Blueprints](pages/blend-spaces-in-animation-blueprints-in-unreal-engine.md) ([web](https://dev.epicgames.com/documentation/en-us/unreal-engine/blend-spaces-in-animation-blueprints-in-unreal-engine?application_version=5.9)) - Explains the Blend Space node types in the AnimGraph: Blendspace Player (references an asset), Blend Space Graph (embedded, editable Blend Space with per-sample sub-graphs), and Blendspace Evaluator (externally driven normalized time), plus their properties. keys: `Blendspace Player`, `Blend Space Graph`, `Blendspace Evaluator`, `Play Rate`, `Loop`, `Reset Play Time when Blend Space Changes`, `Start Position`, `LOD Threshold`, `Teleport to Normalized Time`, `Aim Offset`. Gotchas: Blendspace Evaluator teleports to time by default so root motion and Anim Notifies don't evaluate; disable Teleport to Normalized Time to restore; LOD Threshold only appears for Aim Offset players.
- **[core]** [Camera Cut Track](pages/cinematic-camera-cut-track-in-unreal-engine.md) ([web](https://dev.epicgames.com/documentation/en-us/unreal-engine/cinematic-camera-cut-track-in-unreal-engine?application_version=5.9)) - Explains Sequencer's Camera Cut Track: creating it, binding cameras, making cuts at the playhead, blending between cameras or to/from gameplay with Can Blend, section properties and thumbnails. keys: `Camera Cut Track`, `Add Camera (+)`, `Camera Lock`, `Can Blend`, `Lock Previous Camera`, `Camera Binding ID`, `Draw Thumbnails`, `Draw Single Thumbnail`. Gotchas: Viewport camera control is disabled while locked to the Camera Cut Track; Camera Cut sections disallow gaps/overlaps unless Can Blend is enabled; Thumbnail generation costs editor performance.
- **[core]** [Constant Material Expressions](pages/constant-material-expressions-in-unreal-engine.md) ([web](https://dev.epicgames.com/documentation/en-us/unreal-engine/constant-material-expressions-in-unreal-engine?application_version=5.9)) - Reference for constant-type material expressions: Constant through Constant4Vector (with hotkeys 1-4), DistanceCullFade, Cascade particle nodes, PerInstanceFadeAmount, PerInstanceRandom, Time, TwoSidedSign, VertexColor, ViewProperty and PrecomputedAOMask. keys: `Constant`, `Constant2Vector`, `Constant3Vector`, `Constant4Vector`, `DistanceCullFade`, `PerInstanceFadeAmount`, `PerInstanceRandom`, `Time`, `TwoSidedSign`, `VertexColor`, `ViewProperty`, `PrecomputedAOMask`. Gotchas: PerInstanceFadeAmount and PerInstanceRandom only work on InstancedStaticMeshComponents; PrecomputedAOMask only works with baked Lightmass lighting; ParticleColor and related particle nodes refer to Cascade data.
- **[core]** [Coordinates Material Expressions](pages/coordinates-material-expressions-in-unreal-engine.md) ([web](https://dev.epicgames.com/documentation/en-us/unreal-engine/coordinates-material-expressions-in-unreal-engine?application_version=5.9)) - Reference for material expressions that output or modify coordinates: world/actor/object/camera positions, normals and tangents, Panner and Rotator for animated UVs, TextureCoordinate tiling/channels, ScreenPosition, ViewSize, SceneTexelSize, LightmapUVs. keys: `ActorPositionWS`, `CameraPositionWS`, `ObjectPositionWS`, `ObjectRadius`, `ObjectOrientation`, `Panner`, `Rotator`, `TextureCoordinate`, `VertexNormalWS`, `WorldPosition`, `ScreenPosition`, `ViewSize`. Gotchas: VertexNormalWS only works in vertex-shader inputs like World Position Offset; Offsetting along vertex normals splits geometry at UV seams; LightmapUVs outputs (0,0) if lightmap UVs are unavailable.
- **[core]** [Creating and Using Material Functions](pages/creating-and-using-material-functions-in-unreal-engine.md) ([web](https://dev.epicgames.com/documentation/en-us/unreal-engine/creating-and-using-material-functions-in-unreal-engine?application_version=5.9)) - How to create, edit, publish (Expose to Library, description, Library Categories) and use Material Functions, via the Palette, right-click search, or an Unspecified Function node. keys: `Material Function`, `Expose to Library`, `Library Categories Text`, `Material Function Call`, `Unspecified Function`, `Apply`, `Use Selected Asset from Content Browser`. Gotchas: Saved edits propagate to every material using the function; duplicate it if unsure; Must click Apply to propagate changes; User functions go in the Misc category by default.
- **[core]** [Creating and Using Material Instances](pages/creating-and-using-material-instances-in-unreal-engine.md) ([web](https://dev.epicgames.com/documentation/en-us/unreal-engine/creating-and-using-material-instances-in-unreal-engine?application_version=5.9)) - Step-by-step guide to building a parameterized parent Material (Scalar/Vector parameters, Convert to Parameter, slider ranges), creating and editing Material Instances, organizing parameters with groups and sort priority, and changing an instance's parent. keys: `Material Instance Constant`, `Create Material Instance`, `Scalar Parameter`, `Vector Parameter`, `Convert to Parameter`, `Slider Min`, `Slider Max`, `Group`, `Sort Priority`, `Group Sort Priority`, `Parameter Group Data`, `Parent`. Gotchas: Only parameter nodes are editable in instances; not every node can be parameterized; Changing the parent can remove the parameters the instance used.
- **[core]** [Creating Shiny Materials](pages/creating-shiny-materials-in-unreal-engine.md) ([web](https://dev.epicgames.com/documentation/en-us/unreal-engine/creating-shiny-materials-in-unreal-engine?application_version=5.9)) - Explains how Roughness, Metallic and Specular control reflectivity, then builds a parameterized material instance demonstrating gold metal and scuffed plastic looks. keys: `Roughness`, `Metallic`, `Specular`, `Scalar Parameter`, `Create Material Instance`. Gotchas: Leave Specular at 0.5 in most cases; it has no effect when Metallic is 1; Avoid Roughness of exactly 0 or 1; Many metallic surfaces reflecting each other can be expensive.
- **[core]** [FBX Content Pipeline](pages/fbx-content-pipeline.md) ([web](https://dev.epicgames.com/documentation/en-us/unreal-engine/fbx-content-pipeline?application_version=5.9)) - Short overview of the FBX import pipeline: one format covers Static Meshes, Skeletal Meshes, animations, morph targets, LODs, materials and textures; states the FBX SDK version used. keys: `FBX`, `FBX 2020.2`. - **[core]** [FBX Import Errors](pages/fbx-import-errors-in-unreal-engine.md) ([web](https://dev.epicgames.com/documentation/en-us/unreal-engine/fbx-import-errors-in-unreal-engine?application_version=5.9)) - Lists FBX importer error and warning messages with their causes and fixes, grouped by generic, mesh, Static Mesh, Skeletal Mesh and animation (bind pose, root bone, smoothing groups, material limits, LOD bones, track length). keys: `Export Smoothing Groups`, `Import Meshes In Bone Hierarchy`, `Use Time 0 as Reference Pose`, `Import Rigid Body`, `Create Physics Asset`, `CheckSingleInfluenceLOD`, `MAX_MESH_MATERIAL_INDEX`, `ComputePolygonSmoothingFromEdgeSmoothing`. - **[core]** [FBX Skeletal Mesh Pipeline](pages/fbx-skeletal-mesh-pipeline-in-unreal-engine.md) ([web](https://dev.epicgames.com/documentation/en-us/unreal-engine/fbx-skeletal-mesh-pipeline-in-unreal-engine?application_version=5.9)) - Technical overview of preparing, rigging, exporting (Maya/3ds Max) and importing Skeletal Meshes via FBX, including multi-part meshes, pivot at root bone, triangulation, materials/vertex colors, LOD import in Persona, and exporting back to FBX. keys: `FBX Import Options`, `Select Skeleton`, `LOD Import`, `LOD Settings`, `Screen Size`, `Reduction Settings`, `Asset Actions > Export`, `Smooth Bind`, `Skin modifier`. Gotchas: Pipeline uses FBX 2020.2; other versions may be incompatible; Only one animation per Skeletal Mesh can be imported per FBX file; Only diffuse and normal textures imported with materials; one vertex color set; Assets in cooked packages cannot be exported back to FBX.
- **[core]** [FBX Static Mesh Pipeline](pages/fbx-static-mesh-pipeline-in-unreal-engine.md) ([web](https://dev.epicgames.com/documentation/en-us/unreal-engine/fbx-static-mesh-pipeline-in-unreal-engine?application_version=5.9)) - Guide to preparing and importing Static Meshes via FBX: pivot, triangulation, UVs, materials, custom collision naming (UBX/UCP/USP/UCX), SOCKET_ helpers, vertex colors, Combine Meshes and importing LODs. keys: `UBX_`, `UCP_`, `USP_`, `UCX_`, `SOCKET_`, `Combine Meshes`, `Import LODs`, `FBX 2020.2`, `LOD Picker`, `Static Mesh Editor`. Gotchas: Uses FBX 2020.2; other versions may be incompatible; With multiple meshes in one file only the first mesh's custom collision imports; Only Color and Normal maps auto-connect; specular imports unconnected; Sockets only work with a single mesh per FBX; sphere/box collision fails with non-uniform scale.
- **[core]** [Geometry Scripting Through Blueprints](pages/geometry-scripting-through-blueprints-in-unreal-engine.md) ([web](https://dev.epicgames.com/documentation/en-us/unreal-engine/geometry-scripting-through-blueprints-in-unreal-engine?application_version=5.9)) - Tutorial creating a GeneratedDynamicMeshActor Blueprint that builds a procedural blockout box with 3D-widget size controls, subtracts a cylinder with Apply Mesh Boolean using a compute mesh pool, and bakes the result to a Static Mesh via a Call In Editor function. keys: `Geometry Script`, `GeneratedDynamicMeshActor`, `Event on Rebuild Generated Mesh`, `Append Box`, `Append Cylinder`, `Get Compute Mesh Pool`, `Request and Release Mesh`, `Apply Mesh Boolean`, `Show 3D widget`, `Copy Mesh to Static Mesh`, `Create New Static Mesh Asset From Mesh`, `Call in Editor`. - **[core]** [Geometry Scripting User Guide](pages/geometry-scripting-users-guide-in-unreal-engine.md) ([web](https://dev.epicgames.com/documentation/en-us/unreal-engine/geometry-scripting-users-guide-in-unreal-engine?application_version=5.9)) - Introduction to the Geometry Scripting plugin for generating and editing meshes from Blueprint and Python: UDynamicMesh, UDynamicMeshComponent, ADynamicMeshActor and AGeneratedDynamicMeshActor, the Target Mesh/Options node pattern, dynamic mesh pools, and component limitations versus static meshes. keys: `Geometry Script`, `UDynamicMesh`, `UDynamicMeshComponent`, `ADynamicMeshActor`, `AGeneratedDynamicMeshActor`, `FDynamicMesh3`, `On Rebuild Generated Mesh`, `UDynamicMeshPool`, `Request and Release Mesh`, `Create Dynamic Mesh Pool`, `Apply Mesh Plane Cut`, `Geometry Framework`. - **[core]** [Importing Assets Using Interchange](pages/importing-assets-using-interchange-in-unreal-engine.md) ([web](https://dev.epicgames.com/documentation/en-us/unreal-engine/importing-assets-using-interchange-in-unreal-engine?application_version=5.9)) - Overview of the Interchange import framework: pipelines, pipeline stacks and factories, the import/preview/conflict windows, importing at runtime via Blueprint (Interchange Manager), Python import, editing pipeline stacks in Project Settings, and creating custom pipelines in Blueprint, C++ or Python. keys: `Interchange Editor`, `Interchange Framework`, `Project Settings > Interchange`, `Choose Pipeline Stack`, `Interchange.FeatureFlags.Import.FBX`, `Interchange.FeatureFlags.Import.FBX.ToLevel`, `Get Interchange Manager Scripted`, `Create Source Data`, `Import Asset`, `InterchangePipelineBase`, `unreal.InterchangePythonPipelineBase`, `DefaultSceneLevelPipeline`. - **[core]** [Importing Audio Files](pages/importing-audio-files.md) ([web](https://dev.epicgames.com/documentation/en-us/unreal-engine/importing-audio-files?application_version=5.9)) - Explains how to create Sound Wave assets by importing audio files (Import button or drag-drop), the supported formats/bit depths/channels, and the available compression codecs. keys: `.wav`, `.ogg`, `.flac`, `.aif`, `.opus`, `.mp3`, `Sound Wave`, `Default Audio Compression Type`, `Bink Audio`, `ADPCM`, `PCM`, `Asset Actions > Export...`. - **[core]** [Math Material Expressions](pages/math-material-expressions-in-unreal-engine.md) ([web](https://dev.epicgames.com/documentation/en-us/unreal-engine/math-material-expressions-in-unreal-engine?application_version=5.9)) - Reference for math material nodes (Abs, Add, Append, trig and Fast variants, Ceil/Floor/Frac/Round/Truncate, Clamp, ComponentMask, Cross/Dot, Divide, Fmod, If, Lerp, Log, Max/Min, Multiply, Normalize, OneMinus, Power, Saturate, Step, SmoothStep, Sign, Sine/Cosine, SquareRoot, Subtract) with inputs and examples. keys: `LinearInterpolate`, `ComponentMask`, `AppendVector`, `Saturate`, `SmoothStep`, `Step`, `If`, `Fmod`, `Frac`, `DotProduct`, `Arctangent2Fast`, `Clamp Mode`. Gotchas: Arccosine/Arcsine/Arctangent/Arctangent2 are expensive and not reflected in instruction count; use Fast variants; Divide clamps divisors near zero to +/-0.00001; If compares only single float values; DotProduct needs equal channel counts; Logarithm nodes need positive inputs.

- **[core]** [Root Motion](pages/root-motion-in-unreal-engine.md) ([web](https://dev.epicgames.com/documentation/en-us/unreal-engine/root-motion-in-unreal-engine?application_version=5.9)) - How to make root bone motion in Animation Sequences or Montages drive character movement: Enable Root Motion and root lock options on the sequence, Root Motion Mode in the Animation Blueprint Class Defaults, how movement modes affect it, and debugging in the sequence editor. keys: `Enable Root Motion`, `Root Motion Root Lock`, `Force Root Lock`, `Use Normalized Root motion Scale`, `Root Motion Mode`, `Root Motion from Montages Only`, `Root Motion from everything`, `Ignore Root Motion`, `No Root Motion Extraction`, `show collision`. ## Coverage notes

The 5.9 table of contents (the site sidebar, read 2026-11-10) lists 2,554 pages. This index covers 2,535 of them plus 9 pages the crawl reached that the sidebar does not list (2,544 in all). 2,281 pages came from the crawl and 263 from the browser pane (see `gen/docs/README.md`). Not covered:

- 18 sidebar entries that redirect to another page in 5.9 (their content is the target page): `vertex-sculpt-tool-in-unreal-engine` -> `modeling-tools-in-unreal-engine`; `dynamic-sculpt-tool-in-unreal-engine` -> `modeling-tools-in-unreal-engine`; `lattice-tool-in-unreal-engine` -> `modeling-tools-in-unreal-engine`; `displace-tool-in-unreal-engine` -> `modeling-tools-in-unreal-engine`; `distance-field-ambient-occlusion-in-unreal-engine` -> `mesh-distance-fields-in-unreal-engine`; `adding-components-to-an-actor-in-unreal-engine` -> `gameplay-tutorials-for-unreal-engine`; `setting-up-character-movement` -> `gameplay-tutorials-for-unreal-engine`; `finding-actors-in-unreal-engine` -> `gameplay-tutorials-for-unreal-engine`; `respawning-a-player-character` -> `gameplay-tutorials-for-unreal-engine`; `possessing-pawns-in-unreal-engine` -> `gameplay-tutorials-for-unreal-engine`; `interface-quick-start-guide-in-unreal-engine` -> `actor-communication-in-unreal-engine`; `spawning-and-destroying-unreal-engine-actors` -> `actors-in-unreal-engine`; `using-spring-arm-components-in-unreal-engine` -> `using-cameras-in-unreal-engine`; `switching-between-multiple-fixed-camera-perspectives-in-unreal-engine` -> `using-cameras-in-unreal-engine`; `working-with-camera-components-in-unreal-engine` -> `using-cameras-in-unreal-engine`; `using-timers-in-unreal-engine` -> `gameplay-timers-in-unreal-engine`; `setting-up-android-single-instance-service-in-unreal-engine` -> `unreal-engine-5-8-documentation`; `cinematic-subscequences-track-in-unreal-engine` -> `sequencer-track-list-in-unreal-engine`.
